News.title: Costco shoppers in line for free cash from $14million email settlement over ‘misleading promotion’ – claim by Aug 24
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CASH IN Costco shoppers in line for free cash from $14million email settlement over ‘misleading promotion’ – claim by Aug 24

AMERICAN’S could be eligible for free cash as a US retail giant is forced to fork out $14M over misleading promotions.

Washington state residents affected by false advertising between June 2, 2021, and July 7, 2026, may qualify for a one-time cash payment.

Costco Wholesale Corp have agreed to pay the whopping sum in settlement of a class action lawsuit which claimed they sent commercial electronic mail messages with false or misleading subject lines.



The claim deadline is August 24.



The suit alleged Costco sent commercial emails to Washington residents with subject lines advertising temporary or time-limited promotions but then falsely extended those promotions beyond the stated time frame.

The plaintiffs said this violated Washington’s Commercial Electronic Mail Act and Consumer Protection Act.

Costco denies any wrongdoing but agreed to settle to avoid further litigation and expense.

The promotional emails include examples such as, “Today is the last day to access Member-Only Saving” or “Hot Buys available for 5 Days Only.”

Affected customers will have received an email from the wholesale behemoth between the aforementioned dates.

If individuals received an email or letter, it is likely they will qualify for the lump sum.

The exact amount each person receives depends on the number of valid claims submitted.



The settlement administrator will divide the net settlement fund equally among all approved claimants after deducting attorneys’ fees, litigation costs, settlement administration costs and a service award to the class representative.

The attorneys’ fees alone stand at $4,620,000.

Individuals can file a claim online or download a PDF claim form to print, complete and mail to the settlement administrator.

The final approval hearing will be on October 2.

It comes as Costco faced accusations of false advertising in a class action filed in January.



According to the suit, filed in the US District Court for the Southern District of California, Costco allegedly advertised that its Kirkland Signature Seasoned Rotisserie Chicken contains no added preservatives.

The plaintiff argued that in-store signs and details on the company’s website “create an overall net impression that the Rotisserie Chicken does not contain added preservatives.”

News.title: Terror suspect in Berlin Pride attack shot dead by police in raid on garden shed after ramming crowd with van
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

GUNNED DOWN Terror suspect who rammed into crowd at Berlin Pride shot dead after ‘trying to stab cops’ during raid on garden shed

POLICE have shot and killed the suspect who rammed a van into a crowd at a Berlin Pride event on Saturday night.

Cops confronted Abdul Ballout, 21, thought to be an “armed and dangerous Islamist” in a raid on a garden shed.



He is suspected of killing one and injuring 29 others in a “terrorist attack” targeting pride celebrations last night.

A huge police operation to hunt down Ballout culminated in a SWAT team gunning down the suspect in an allotment complex in Berlin’s Spandau district on Sunday.



Cops were attacked by the suspect, who rushed at officers with a “stabbing weapon”.

Berlin Police said: “Around 6 pm, the suspect in yesterday’s attack in the Großer Tiergarten was located in an allotment garden facility in Spandau.

“According to current findings, he is said to have rushed toward our emergency forces with a stabbing weapon, after which police firearms were used by our SEK Berlin.

“Despite immediate resuscitation measures initiated by the Berlin Fire Department, he died at the scene.”



Witnesses reported hearing two volleys of gunfire a few minutes apart during the raid.

The suspect was fatally wounded and died at 6.34pm, Bild reported.

Berlin’s Interior minister Iris Spranger said: “I am grateful to the security authorities for finding the attacker so quickly. That is a tremendous achievement.”

At least one person was killed and 29 injured when a van ploughed into a crowd at Berlin’s Christopher Street Day (CSD) Pride parade around 10pm last night.

News.title: Teen charged over supersized inflatable dinghy carrying record 165 migrants from France to Britain
News.content:
A TEENAGER has been charged after a supersized inflatable dinghy carrying 165 migrants was intercepted in the channel.

Sudanese national Chan Mathok Atak, 19, has been accused of endangering another during a journey by sea to the UK.



The teen was allegedly piloting the 13metre long dinghy, the National Crime agency has said.

He is due to appear at Margate Magistrates’ Court on Monday.



The inflatable, which was around the size of a standard bus, was carrying the largest number of people to have been crammed into a single boat.

It was picked up by a Border Force vessel on Wednesday, with the French lifeboat service calling it “alarming, unique, and exceptional”.

The RNLI said: “We are astonished by the number of people on board.”

The previous record was set earlier this month when 128 people made the crossing in one boat.

Home Office figures revealed that 366 people arrived on Thursday across three boats as the warm, sunny weather brought calm conditions.

The higher number of people in each boat is making the crossing route more dangerous, refugee charity Care4Calais said.



Boats used in the Channel are most commonly made in China, and have no purpose other than to carry migrants across the narrow 21-mile strait.

A total of 538 people have arrived in small boats during Andy Burnham’s first week as Prime Minister.

So far this year 13,007 migrants have come to the UK across the Channel, a 45 per cent decrease compared to this time last year.

A Home Office spokesperson previously said: “This Government is bearing down on small boat crossings, with removals of small boat migrants at record levels and asylum claims down by 12 per cent.

“The Home Secretary has signed a landmark new deal with France to boost enforcement action on beaches and put people smugglers behind bars.



“This builds on joint work that has stopped over 44,000 attempted crossings since the election.

“We have removed or deported almost 70,000 people who were here illegally – an increase of 41 per cent – and are going further to remove the incentives that draw illegal migrants to this country.”

Reform UK Leader Nigel Farage slammed the new PM for not mentioning the issue of immigration in his first speech and said: “Open borders Burnham will do nothing to stop the illegal and dangerous invasion of our country, he won’t even mention it.

“Only Reform will stop the boats.”

News.title: Man ‘punched by two men on Tube after being kissed by female passenger’ as cops release CCTV images
News.content:
TUBE 'ATTACK' Man ‘punched by two men on Tube after being kissed by female passenger’ as cops release CCTV images

A MAN has been allegedly attacked on a Tube train by two men after being kissed by a female passenger.

The incident happened on the Northern Line train in London on July 4 where two girls approached the victim – with one kissing him.



Two men then approached the man and allegedly punched him, leaving him with a broken nose and cuts to his face.

British Transport Police (BTP) has released CCTV images of two people they would like to speak to as part of its inquiry.



The victim was travelling southbound and boarded the train at Chalk Farm at around 10.50pm on Saturday.

A group of people boarded the carriage at the same time, with two girls approaching the victim and speaking to him.



After one of the girls kissed him, a member of the party saw and began punching the victim.

A second person joined in and also began throwing punches.

The victim and the group left the train at Euston, with the victim needing assistance from station staff.

He was taken to hospital after having sustained a broken nose as well as deep cuts to his face.



Officers believe the two men in the images could have information that may assist their inquiries.

BTP is calling for anyone who recognises the two men to text BTP on 61016, or call 0800 40 50 40, using the reference 840 of 4 July.

Information can be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Inside rise of ‘death doulas’ as A-list celebs sign up to ‘taboo’ side hustle & experts reveal question dying often ask
News.content:
DEATH is a topic many of us struggle to talk openly about, but as a rising number of A-list celebrities announce their plan to train as ‘death doulas’, many experts hope it’s a taboo that will finally be overcome.

The unusual career choice – which involves providing support to the dying – has attracted silver-screen royalty including Nicole Kidman, who took on the ‘role’ after experiencing death in her own family, and Davina McCall, who said she plans to do the same when she retires.





It’s a career that has skyrocketed in popularity, with doulas earning between £25 and £45 an hour.

To become a death doula in the UK, people are required to undertake a five day foundation course and can then provide non-medical emotional, practical and spiritual support to those with incurable conditions and their loved ones.

Louise Piper chairs End of Life Doula UK, an organisation that supports more than 450 end of life carers across the country.

She believes the rise in celebrity attention has pulled back the curtain for people to speak more openly about dying.

She said: “Nicole Kidman is a great humanitarian, she clearly cares.

“She experienced death through her own mother – I think her intentions and motivations around it are really positive.

“We’ve [somehow] become detached or divorced from death… we’ve sanitised it in a way.

“The more we can build that awareness and build that connection again, I think it’s a really important path that society can take to make [death] less fearful.”





Death doula Sean O’Connor, 56, from Cape Town, South Africa began his career in end-of life-care when he met a priest at a conference six years ago.

Speaking to The Sun, he says: “He asked me if I would see clients that he couldn’t.

“The priest was stretched and depleted. He needed some kind of backup to attend to these requests of spiritual support.

“Suddenly I found myself with someone, holding their hand and reassuring them that we’re all going to die – they’re just beating me to it.”

At the time Sean was running a death café – a non-profit organisation that invites people to talk openly about death and grief over tea and cake.

He had also trained in palliative care at the University of Cape Town medical school and taken several courses in end-of-life care.

Death doula roles include supporting patients – offering emotional comfort by reading or playing music – and their caregivers.

“I’m here to help ask the questions that people might be too scared to ask”, Sean said.

“As an outsider, I sometimes have a strange kind of authority. I’m prepared for anything.”

Sean said there has been a recent surge in the number of people showing interest in becoming a death doula, and asking for his guidance.



He said: “Many doulas go into the practice after their own experience witnessing death in their home.

“Death has become hidden from our generation – confined to hospitals and hospices.

“But Covid was a gamechanger. Millions of people around the world suddenly realised that [it] is really a part of life.

“There was a profound shift – talking about death was no longer taboo.”

The most common question people in their final moments ask Sean is “what will happen to me?”

Sean said this is “challenging”, because he cannot offer an answer.

“Death is a mystery – all I can offer is comfort”, he said.

Others seek reassurance that they have been a good partner or parent.



“Often this is something they need to hear before giving themselves permission to depart”, Sean said.

Sometimes a doula will carry out a patient’s last wish for them, after their death. Sean recalled one client who was very precise about the process of her memorial.

“She wanted me to sit at bench number 67 on a coastal path,” he said, adding she asked him to scatter white roses into the ocean.

“I sang, recited some poetry and I sat there for ages. I felt so privileged that I helped a person achieve what they wanted.”

Sean said there is a general “fascination with death” – but there are some cases that have really stuck in his mind.

In one “highly unusual” case, Sean was referred to a “dying” woman by her heartbroken former partner.

It was later revealed the woman had faked a stage-four cancer diagnosis in a twisted scam to fleece her ex of £15,000.

Sean said: “I got a call from a man who was incredibly distressed about his ex-girlfriend who only had weeks left to live.



“I met them both and there were lots of tears. She said she had so much more life to give and wasn’t ready to leave.”

When Sean returned home he received a text from the man, thanking him and asking to meet again.

But soon the woman’s ploy fell apart when her ex called the hospital she said she was receiving treatment at.

Sean said: “He couldn’t find her. Then I got a call from the woman’s phone. It was her husband. He had read the messages and was horrified.”

Her ex-partner had been paying her fake medical bills – which totalled more than £15,000.

“She was a fraudster leaving a trail of destruction in her wake”, Sean said.

“His empathy and love had kept him paying for treatment.”

Sean was inspired to become a death doula after his own experience with grief.

Aged seven, his father was diagnosed with heart disease and underwent a triple bypass, before passing away 18 years ago.



“My childhood and early adult life was punctuated with anticipatory grief. I was always waiting for him to die and I was scared”, he said.

“I am still scared of dying. But my work has made me comfortable knowing that one day I will.”

Given their close work with dying people and their families, death doulas have a unique insight into a person’s final moments and what happens.

For example, some doulas have reported patients having ‘deathbed visions’ – where a dying person sees and interacts with deceased loved ones while awake.

Emma Clare, CEO of End Of Life Doula UK, said she had witnessed several people “reaching up to a corner of the room” before they passed away.

She said: “They see and speak to relatives who have died before them.”

Another doula, Rachel Hawthorn, from West Yorkshire, said two of her clients experienced their late husbands appearing before them.

“One sat on the bed and spoke to her to say he was waiting for her – she found it comforting.”

End of Life Doula UK’s chair Louise Piper she said the number of doulas available to offer support in the UK is growing “exponentially each year”.

She added: “Some doulas work long term, some work for a small fee, and then we have this pot which we’re trying to build for subsidised support.



“So if a family needs [a death doula] and doesn’t have access to it either by the NHS or by themselves, we can help with that.”

News.title: Passenger sucked out of Ryanair jet at 15,000ft claims staff did nothing to help as frantic wife clung onto his legs
News.content:
A PASSENGER nearly sucked out of a Ryanair jet at 15,000ft has claimed that staff remained strapped in their seats and failed to help.

That Ljubisa Karovic came back from “the brink of death” – and lived to tell the tale – is nothing short of a miracle, but he has since been haunted by pain and the memories of how he dangled out of the aircraft window in 370mph winds.



Helped by two other passengers, his wife, Svetlana, desperately clung to his legs – while crew were “more interested in saving their own lives.”

The couple are critical of the way in which Ryanair crew responded to the disaster, claiming that they remained in their seats.



Svetlana told the Daily Mail: “When we were battling to hold onto Ljubisa the crew didn’t do anything, they looked more scared than us.

“It was only the passengers who helped and were brave.”



Their lawyer, Vasilis Tsiaras, who has vowed to secure a major payout, said: “My client came back from the brink of death, and we want to make sure that whoever is responsible for this is held accountable.

“It is not just about compensation but about establishing the truth as to what happened and the condition of this aircraft.

“There are also serious concerns about the conduct of the Ryanair crew.

“They were gripped by fear that the plane was about to crash which prevented them from doing anything to help Karovic as he was hanging out of the aircraft.”



He added: “It seems that the crew were more interested in saving their own lives. It was only the actions of the passengers that saved my client.”

Ljubisa and Svetlana have also claimed that not a single official has been in touch with them since the incident.

Ryanair has reportedly only emailed their son, who booked their flights, to ask if they want to rebook and to ask how his father is.



“Nobody from the company has contacted me directly, not even a phone call to show any concern,” Ljubisa explained.

His wife slammed Ryanair’s behaviour as “disgusting” and added: “We are going to be dealing with the aftermath of this for a very long time because it’s caused us a lot of psychological damage.

“But nobody from the airline has been in touch with either of us.”

The couple had been flying from Germany to Greece for a family birthday when broken bits of the jet engine hit the window, creating a gaping hole.

The dad-of-two is now in a neck brace with burns on his back and right hand.



He was also temporarily paralysed – and his head had swollen while he suffered damage to his right ear and eye.

The nightmare ordeal has also left psychological scars as he explained that he is not “functioning properly”.

“Now everything is bothering me,” Ljubisa added. “Mentally, I have hit rock bottom.

“It has an effect on both my work and family. It is a complete upheaval in my life.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The incident is now being investigated by the US National Transportation Safety Board which has already examined the aircraft and will issue a draft report in around 28 days.



The Sun has contacted Ryanair for a comment.

News.title: Powerlifter, 45, dies in jet ski accident in Majorca while riding with his partner as tributes paid to ‘incredible dad’
News.content:
JET SKI TRAGEDY Powerlifter, 45, dies in jet ski accident in Majorca while riding with his partner as tributes paid to ‘incredible dad’

A CHAMPION powerlifter died in a jet ski accident as tributes were paid to the “incredible fight”, an inquest heard.

Jeremy Paynter was on holiday in Spain when the accident took place as he was riding on the watercraft with his partner.



The jet ski tipped over and he was unable to climb back aboard after helping his partner back onto the jet ski, an inquest at Oakwood House in Maidstone heard.

Mr Paynter, from Seabrook near Hythe, was a dad of one seven-year-old daughter and was described as an “honest giant of a man”.



He was on holiday in Alcudia, Majorca when the tragic accident unfolded as the jet ski he and his partner were riding overturned whilst stationary.

Coroner Patricia Harding said: “The information before the court is that he was on a jet ski trip, on a stationary jet ski with his partner, wearing life jackets, when it tipped and they fell into the water.

“He pushed his partner back onto the jet ski but struggled to get on himself.”

The hearing was told Mr Paynter was eventually pulled onto nearby rocks but unable to be revived by emergency services.

His ex-wife, Karen Spencer, posted on Linkedin: “Jeremy was an incredible Dad to our amazing daughter.

“Jeremy was larger than life in every way. He made such an incredible, positive impact on everyone he met.



“I hope that he is looking down now and finally understands how much he is loved by so many people.”

The inquest has been adjourned for a full hearing to examine the circumstances of his death in more detail.

News.title: Urgent summer holiday warning to parents as hundreds of dangerous ‘chemical smelling’ squishy toys seized
News.content:
SQUISH SHOCK Urgent summer holiday warning to parents as hundreds of dangerous ‘chemical smelling’ squishy toys seized

PARENTS have been issued an urgent summer holiday warning after hundreds of dangerous squishy toys were seized.

Over 320 sensory toys have been confiscated by trading standard officers in Reading after reports of strong chemical smells.



Knock-offs of the viral “Squishy Dumpling” and “NeeDoh” toys were found to be missing the legally required safety information.

Reading Borough Council said although the toys may appear harmless, products that do not meet UK safety standards could pose a risk to children.



Parents and carers are now being urged to stop using any squishy toy that leaks, splits or becomes damaged – and never to heat, microwave or tamper with them.

The council warned that any products found to be non-compliant may be seized and businesses could face further enforcement action.



Councillor Finn McGoldrick, lead member for environmental services and community safety, said: “Parents and carers should be able to trust that the toys they buy for their children are safe.

“These product seizures demonstrate our ongoing commitment to protecting consumers and removing potentially dangerous products from the marketplace.

“During the summer holidays, I would ask people to remain vigilant and make sure any toys purchased are from reputable retailers, that you check for the appropriate safety markings, and report any concerns about unsafe products to our Trading Standards team.”

This comes after 1,000 fake “Squeezy Dumpling” toys were seized earlier this month after tests revealed they contain a cancer-causing chemical.



The knock-offs have been under a product recall alert notice, which prompted the Trading Standards Team to seize and destroy the toys from shelves across Hull.

Benzene, a cancer-causing chemical that was discovered inside the illegitimate toys, can cause immediate irritation, as well as long-term effects.

News.title: Berlin Pride crash updates: Suspect shot dead by police after terror attack
News.content:
Police have shot dead the suspect, 21-year-old Abdul Ballout, according to German media reports

The suspect in the Berlin Pride festival attack that left one person dead and at least 25 others injured has been shot dead, according to German media.

Police and prosecutors asked for help in finding 21-year-old Abdul Ballout after the attack on Saturday night. On Sunday evening, reports say he has now been shot and killed by police.

Germany’s Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said initial findings suggest "we have experienced an Islamist terror attack".

On Sunday evening, police confirmed that 'several people' had now been taken into custody.

News.title: Europe wildfires horror laid bare as 300,000 evacuated across multiple countries with Brits warned 'stay away'
News.content:
Europe wildfires horror laid bare as 300,000 evacuated across multiple countries with Brits warned 'stay away'

Brits heading to wildfire-hit holiday destinations have been warned by Foreign Office and ABTA to 'check ahead' as flames continued to spread rapidly across southwest France and northern Spain

"We don't know when we'll be back home": Father recounts family's evacuation amid wildfires around Bordeaux

British holidaymakers heading to wildfire-hit regions of France have been told to stay away from Bordeaux as the number of evacuations soared past 300,000.

‌



The Foreign Office issued the alert to UK tourists and expats on Sunday as the fires - which have been raging across southwest France and the northern tip of Spain since July 21 - spread further into heavily populated areas along the Bay of Biscay.

‌



The new travel advice said: "French authorities have evacuated campsites, tourist accommodation and some residential areas. Access to affected areas may be restricted and roads may close at short notice. Further evacuations may take place.

‌



"If you are in an affected area, or planning to travel there: follow instructions and updates from local authorities and emergency services at all times, and call 112 if you need emergency help. Check with your accommodation or travel provider before travelling."

View 5 Images Wildfires have now led to evacuations of more than 300,000 people across France and Spain (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Brooklyn Beckham and wife Nicola Peltz head to Nice for romantic holiday amid France wildfire READ MORE :

Exact date UK faces 32C burn as heatwave returns with a vengeance READ MORE :

A total of 65,000 to 70,000 British citizens live across the southern regions of France, making up roughly 43 per cent of the country's total British population, while French interior data tracks about 172,000 resident British citizens. Around nine to 10 million British residents visit France each year.

‌



Tourists have been told to stay away from Bordeaux in France as fires have advanced to within nine miles of the city. Local official Sophie Brocas said: "We urge tourists not to come to this region, at least until the situation is under control. I encourage tourists who are already here to consider another destination."

Karen Kissane, 51, from Newcastle, was on holiday in Barcelona when she first heard about the fires in Bordeaux, which where she has made her home. She told the Mirror: "It was horrifying and really frightening. I was not sure what I was returning back to."

After landing back in Bordeaux on Sunday, Karen said the pungent smell of smoke immediately hit her. " When I got off the plane and walked down the steps, the smell of burning in the air really hit me. It just felt really hot and humid, and there was wind in the air that was blowing the burning smell around. I could really sense that the fires could spread quickly because of the breeze," she added.

‌



View 5 Images (Image: Karen Kissane)

Karen revealed some of her friends were forced to leave their holiday homes in the nearby Cap Ferret peninsula as firefighters battled the flames. She added: " I do have some friends who have holiday properties in Cap Ferret and the areas that are worst hit, and they've been evacuated. I know of people who were evacuated at 3am, and they literally had to pick everything up and leave. For anyone who's holidaying in that area, it's an, it's an absolute no-go."

A spokesperson for ABTA said Brits heading to affected regions "should monitor the local news in the regions and any instructions or updates from the local authorities, as well as any guidance provided by their accommodation provider and travel company".

‌



They added: "We would also advise people scheduled to travel to check the Foreign Office advice for travel to France and Spain.”

View 5 Images Firefighters tackle a blaze in Ares, south-western France (Image: DAMIEN REMBERT/HANDOUT/EPA/Shutterstock)

More than 220,000 people have now been evacuated in the Girdone region of France as the latest estimates put the total area of the fires at 162 square miles. Local government chiefs in Bordeaux were last night [Sun] considering a "total evacuation" of the city of 260,000 people as wildfires approached its outer limits.

‌



The city told residents of its northern outer suburbs over the weekend as Bordeaux Mayor Thomas Cazenave described the blaze as being "at the gates" of the wider metropolitan area.

A Gironde official meanwhile ordered the partial closure of a major highway heading in and out of the city, and French national railway operator, SNCF, has suspended rail traffic south of Bordeaux until further notice.

Around 1,000 to 1,150 British citizens live directly within the city of Bordeaux, while nearly 40,000 reside across the wider region.

‌



View 5 Images Burnt-out cars in Pelayos de la Presa, west of Madrid (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Jérôme Sordel, 53, an estate agent from the suburb of Saint-Médard-en-Jalles, said he, his wife and his children were ordered to leave the family home on Saturday night.

He told the Mirror: "We spoke to our children and we just prepared a small backpack with the essentials: some shirts, some clothes, a bottle of water, and masks. Masks because there was a lot of smoke, just to protect ourselves. And all our identity papers. And that's it - we just left."

‌



When asked whether he knows when the family might return home, Jérôme said: "We don't have any, any information about that because the authorities, they are just managing it. They are dealing with the emergency.

"So they have to fight, the fire first. And when they have the information they will tell us, right now, with the wind is turning sometime so to the north, to the east, to the west. So the firemen, have to deal with, with this. I'm very proud, of them and, and this, I thank them that a lot."

In Spain, flames continue to spread through rural areas west of Madrid in the provinces of Toledo and Avila. Several fires have merged in the region, leading to the emergency evacuations of 70,000 people. One person died on Saturday in the Spanish town of Manises after being found in a car in a ravine near a forest fire.

‌



Over the weekend, a new blaze began spreading across a 13-mile area in the Val d'Uixo region, just north of Valencia, which local mayor Tania Baños warned was rapidly becoming "completely uncontrollable".

View 5 Images Firefighters of Paris Fire Brigade rest in Marcheprime west of Bordeaux (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Thousands of firefighters in France and Spain, supported by water-bombing aircraft from neighbouring European nations, have been deployed to battle the flames.

‌



But their task has been made punishingly difficult by temperatures of over 40C, prolonged drought conditions, and shifting coastal winds.

At the end of his Sunday Angelus prayer, Pope Leo XIV asked worshippers to pray for victims of "the devastating wildfires" and said: "I express my solidarity and invite everyone to pray for those affected and for the work of the rescue workers".

It comes as residents were finally allowed to return to their homes in the Cairngorms, Scotland, late on Saturday after an "apocalyptic" fire was tackled by over 500 firefighters and volunteer gamekeepers.

‌



In the Peak District, fire crews said they have made "significant progress" in recent days in their efforts to contain a blaze on Tintwistle Moor, near Glossop, which has been burning for over a month. Temperatures are set to reach highs of 32C or 33C in southern England on Wednesday, bringing a risk of exceptionally severe fires.

A yellow heat alert has been issued from 9am on Tuesday to 9am Friday for the East and West Midlands, the south-east, south-west and east of England, as well as Yorkshire and the Humber. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) issued the warning of possible “significant impacts” on health and social care services, including a rise in deaths among the elderly or people with health conditions, and an increase in drownings.

Forecasters are expecting this week’s heat to be a “north-south split”, with clouds and outbreaks of rain continuing in Northern Ireland, Scotland and northern England. But the peak will be “almost a blink and you miss it”, with temperatures widely cooling close to average by the weekend, said Met Office senior operational meteorologist Dan Stroud.

Article continues below

Wildfires, low water levels and drought are a result of the record-breaking temperatures and their longevity, as the UK faces more extreme weather fuelled by human-caused climate change, mostly from burning fossil fuels.

News.title: Four men killed in Merseyside crash named as heartbroken families pay tribute
News.content:
Four men killed in Merseyside crash named as heartbroken families pay tribute

Jack Diggle, 23, Benjamin Dooley, 23, Andrew Roberts, 24, and Craig Shackleton-Brady, 26 were killed after a black Cupra Formentor hit a lamppost in Huyton at 2am on Friday

View 5 Images Tributes to the four young men have been left at the site of the crash on Liverpool Road (Image: Liverpool ECHO)

The four men who were killed in a horrific car crash in Merseyside in the early hours of Friday morning have been named as their heartbroken families paid tribute.

‌



Jack Diggle, 23, Benjamin Dooley, 23, Andrew Roberts, 24, and Craig Shackleton-Brady, 26 were killed after a black Cupra Formentor left the road and hit a lamppost.

‌



The tragic incident took place just before 2am on Friday morning on Liverpool Road, Huyton. A 27-year-old man, a passenger in the car, was taken to hospital and remains there in a stable condition.

‌



The families and loved ones of all four men have now paid tribute to lost sons, brothers and partners, the Liverpool Echo reports.

A tribute to Jack described him as "kind, quiet, thoughtful, and loving" and loved by his family with all of their hearts.

The tribute read: "Jack was blessed with a wonderful group of friends, many of whom had been by his side for most of his life. He loved playing football with them and was a proud Everton supporter. He also had a passion for darts, whether he was watching it or playing himself. In fact, he was due to travel to Blackpool today with his friends to watch the darts, something he had been looking forward to."

‌



Jack's mum shared the devastation the family are currently feeling adding: "Jack and I went out for a meal together on Thursday. It was such a lovely time, just mother and son, enjoying each other's company. Little did I know that it would be the last time we would spend together.

"The loss of Jack has left a hole in our lives and in our hearts that can never be filled. We will carry him with us every day and miss him for the rest of our lives. Our Jack, our gentle giant, we love you beyond words and will love you forever. Rest peacefully, son."

View 5 Images Jack Diggle (Image: Merseyside Police)

‌



The family of Andrew Roberts say they are at a "complete loss for words" after the heartbreaking news. A tribute said: "Our beautiful Andrew. Your heart is full of kindness and that's why so many people love you. Our worlds are shattered, and we just keep waiting for you to come through the door saying this is all a dream, but it's never going to come.

"Life can change in an instant, and Andrew's passing is a painful reminder of how precious every moment really is. Although his time with us was short the memories he left us will last us all a lifetime. We love you so much our Andrew/ Pip as many knew him. See you soon our boy watches over us forever."

Andrew's mum Linda said: "My beautiful blue-eyed boy, I can’t believe I'm having to even write this. My sweetheart boy could never do no wrong, my life will never be the same with you not here. My heart will forever be broken. I love you son, from mum."

‌



Andrew's brothers Carl and Thomas added: "Pip, our baby bro. Even though you were our younger brother we always looked up to you. You will always be the glue to our crazy family. We Love you lil bro."

View 5 Images Andrew Roberts (Image: Merseyside Police)

Andrew's sister Chloe and nephews Lewis and Lucas said: Andooooo, my big brother and the best uncle to my boys. My heart is in pieces. Your Lewy adores you more than life itself and you are the best role model to him. You will forever be his favourite uncle, his best friend, and his whole world. What are we going to do without you in our life? We love you forever and always."

‌



Another tribute came from Andrew's girlfriend Kiera which said: "My Andrew, my best friend. I never imagined I would ever have to live without you. I am so lost now. You were my whole life, and I don’t know how I’m going to cope without you, but I promise I'm going to try stay strong for you and keep you proud of me like you always were. Please know I always love you Andrew."

Andrew's dad, also called Andrew, said: "I am heartbroken. You were the world to me son and the best son anyone could ask for. I can’t imagine life without you. Loved beyond words and never to be forgotten."

Ben Dooley's mum Kerry said it was her and her son "always", he was her world and her best friend. Her tribute said: "My life is ripped apart and I don't know how I will do life without you. We did everything together.

‌



"I'm waiting for you to walk through the door and say "you ok mum" you was the kindest person I knew with a heart of gold. Do anything for anyone. Loved by everyone who met you. I can't describe how much I will miss you, it hurts so much. Fly high my baby boy. I love you."

Ben's sister Demi said: "Ben my little brother my one and only sibling, the one who always gave me advice and looked out for me, my heart is broken. Feels like a terrible dream, I miss you so much already, the laughs we had and all the memories I will cherish for ever. love you my brother till we meet again."

View 5 Images Benjamin Dooley (Image: Supplied/Demi Lea)

‌



Craig Brady's family have described him as a "well-mannered family man" adding: "His love, loyalty, and generosity touched everyone who knew him.

"Craig was a devoted and loving father to his two children who were always at the centre of his world. His pride in being a dad shone through in everything he did, and the love he gave his family will continue to live on in their hearts forever.

"He was also a dedicated brother, always looking out for his sibling and offering support whenever it was needed. To his brother, Craig was more than family — he was an inspiration, someone to admire and look up to, whose strength, character, and kindness set an example every day."

‌



The emotional tribute continued: "Anyone who knew Craig will remember his infectious laugh. It had a way of lighting up a room, bringing smiles to those around him and making even ordinary moments feel special.

View 5 Images Craig Shackleton-Brady (Image: Merseyside Police)

"His warmth and sense of humour created memories that friends and family will cherish forever. Craig had a passion for life and for the things he loved. He was a proud Liverpool supporter, following his team with unwavering loyalty and enthusiasm. He enjoyed the excitement of the darts and had a keen interest in cage fighting, embracing the passion and energy that these sports brought.

Article continues below

"Above all, Craig will be remembered for his kind heart, his devotion to his family, and the joy he brought to others. Though he will be deeply missed, his spirit lives on through the love he shared, the memories he created, and the countless lives he touched."

News.title: Mum of girl, 8, who died from E.coli in sea urges PM to 'put public health before profit' over sewage scandal
News.content:
The mother of Heather Preen, the eight year-old who died after contracting E.coli on a Devon beach, has made a direct plea to Andy Burnham to prevent any other family going through the same heartache.

“Put public health before profit, simple as that,” said Julie Maughan in a blunt ask of the new PM. “You have to do everything you can.

“Somebody could die again, and how is that going to be on your watch and you have done nothing to stop this? The thought of having another child die, or significant harm for doing what comes naturally, playing in water, is horrific.”

View 5 Images Julie Maughan wearing a 'For Heather' T-shirt, with sales from proceeds of its clothing range and accessories going to Kidney Research UK. https://forheather.org/ (Image: Paul Marriott)

‌



Her appeal to force failing water companies to clean up their act - including having signs at beaches when they have discharged sewage into bathing waters - comes as families across the country head to the coast for the start of the summer holidays

Yet new data from the charity Surfers Against Sewage shows privatised water companies in England have used storm overflows - designed to act as relief valves when the sewerage system is at risk of being overwhelmed - near bathing waters for 116,000 hours since mid-May.

According to the group, one of the worst offenders is South West Water. It claims the company has breached Environment Agency guidance for discharges into or near 20 bathing sites in its area since May, lasting a combined 26,425 hours.

Giles Bristow, chief executive, Surfers Against Sewage, said: “Summer holidays should mean fun in the water, not a gamble with your health. But that’s the reality while our water industry keeps dumping raw sewage into our seas and rivers.”

‌



South West Water was the centre of allegations after the tragic death of Heather in 1999.

Julie, husband Mark Preen and their two daughters, did like so families are doing now and began a beach holiday when the schools broke up.

The getaway in Dawlish began as a fun-filled break together, but turned into a nightmare when, on a day at the beach, they came to a sewage outflow pipe and Heather accidentally put her foot into what was coming out.

View 5 Images Julie Maughan said daughter Heather Preen loved holidays on the beach (Image: Birmingham Mail)

‌



As featured in powerful Channel 4 docu-drama Dirty Business, the youngster later fell horribly ill and it was confirmed she had infected E. coli O157, the most aggressive strain.

Though most people recover, in rare cases, as happened to Heather, it can lead to the life-threatening form of kidney failure hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS). She died on August 8.

Heather loved collecting shells and some of those from the beach before she fell ill are still dotted around Julie’s home near Bromsgrove.

An emotional Julie says “For me, there are the last things she touched, they’re the last things she held. That week before all it happened, she had the best of time. So those shells don’t represent her death, they represent the joy and remind me of how happy she was before all this happened. I have the most horrendous memories of Heather in intensive care, so these shells remind me of when she wasn’t.”

‌



Julie’s marriage did not survive the grief - she separated from Mark, a builder, who later took his own life.

View 5 Images Data suggests water firms are routinely using storm overflows to dump sewage into the sea (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Since her daughter’s death, Julie has campaigned tirelessly and has worked with Surfers Against Sewage to create a safety guide for schools and families on knowing the risks of sewage pollution and how to stay safe.

She is urging families to check the Safer Seas and Rivers Service app (SSRS), developed by SAS, which provides real-time water quality data for the UK’s coastline and inland waters, alerting water users as to when there is a sewage discharge impacting water quality

‌



“It’s really important we raise awareness you have to check, check and check again to keep yourself safe,” says Julie.

“Check the app and check the water quality and be mindful that water is fluid, it changes, so how it was in the morning is not necessarily the same in the afternoon. Check where the combined storm overflows are.

View 5 Images Surfers Against Sewage says: 'Summer holidays should mean fun in the water, not a gamble with your health' (Image: Getty Images)

“Don’t assume this is just about bathing, it is all forms of contact with water, even rock pooling. Cover cuts.

‌



“And if you do have any illness following contact with water, don’t assume it’s food or something else. If you’ve got diarrhoea go to the doctor and let them know you’ve been in contact with water because a lot of cases are being missed because people are putting it down to other things.

“I don’t want people to not go on holiday. The seaside is a beautiful place to go, that’s why we took Heather. We never went abroad. It’s really sad that you can’t just get into the water, which children love to do, because of the actions of others, as it’s potentially dangerous.

“I’m also very angry because we shouldn’t be here. Is it going to take another death before people stop and think, ‘we need to change, this has to stop, it isn’t acceptable?'

“If sewage was being discharged in a public swimming pool, there would be public outrage, if it was being discharged on a playground, or a playing field, there would be public outrage. Someone would go to jail.”

‌



The root cause of Heather’s death will always remain a mystery because of the time before South West Water and the Environment Agency did not take samples from the water. However, the coroner’s recommendations included using ultra violet treatment at South West Water’s Dawlish sewage plant, and a suggestion to erect a sign to warn people of sewage outflows at the beach.

Julie supports bringing water companies back into public ownership but believes warning signs would help protect beach and river goers straight-away. “We need signage, live data on the beach to warn people, as they do in other countries,” she says.

Julie felt that, for a long time, her daughter’s death was forgotten by others, only for the Channel 4 film to bring fresh attention.

Yet the nature of Heather’s death stills haunts her: “It destroyed her kidneys, it destroyed her gut and it destroyed her brain stem” She believes water bosses and others in authority may act differently if they saw first hand what can happen to those infected. “They need to sit in an intensive care unit, watching someone die from this horrendous infection,” she said. “They might think twice about letting people go into the water. I get very animated and heated because these people must have families, have children, and yet they are allowing sewage to be discharged into water.”

‌



Julie spoke amid speculation Mr Burnham is considering some form of renationalisation of embattled Thames Water.

However, there is also anger around payouts to water bosses through “retention” perks after a ban on bonuses at failing firms. I want to know another job elsewhere where you can fail and still be paid,” is Julie’s view. "How do you get paid all that money when you are not succeeding? There’s also a moral aspect to it.”

Julie admits this is a time of year is particularly difficult, coming up to the anniversary of her death. But she is angry that, 27 years on, so little has changed. “Don’t make me do this again next year,” she said. “This needs to be done now. A little girl died.”

To Mr Burnham, she said: “That should be enough to make you think, ‘what can we do to prevent this? We’re going to put this right Julie’, that’s what I want to hear.”

‌



South West Water said in a statement: "The loss of a child is devastating, and we recognise the lasting impact this has had on those closest to her. At the time, there was an extensive and multi-agency investigation involving public health authorities, the Environment Agency and other relevant bodies. The Outbreak Control Team (OCT) report concluded that, despite intensive investigations, no cause for the outbreak was identified.

"The inquest documentation confirms that no definitive source of infection was established. The inquest report also noted that E. coli O157 is a bacteria commonly carried by animals, particularly cattle and dogs."

On Surfers Against Sewage's claims, it said: "We manage more than a third of England's designated bathing waters and helping to protect them is a priority for us. Storm overflows play an important role in preventing homes and communities from flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, but we're investing £760million to reduce their use across the South West and are on track to meet new Environment Act bathing waters standards by 2030, five years ahead of the national deadline."

Industry trade body Water UK said: "No sewage spill is ever acceptable, and water companies are investing £24billion to improve the environment by 2030, prioritising action at bathing waters and other sensitive sites. The quality of English bathing water remains high with 87% achieving a ‘good’ or ‘excellent’ rating. This is a stark contrast to the 1990s when less than a third of bathing waters would have met today’s standards."

News.title: Man found dead in jail six days after 'confessing to murder of his ex'
News.content:
Man found dead in jail six days after 'confessing to murder of his ex'

Lee Greenan, 46, reportedly confessed to killing his ex Vikki Soloman, 44, after he arrived at his local pub 'covered in blood' - he was in prison awaiting trial for his murder when he was found dead

View 3 Images Lee Greenan was found dead at HMP Edinburgh (Image: Collect)

A man who was in jail awaiting trial for murdering his ex has died in prison.

‌



Vikki Soloman, 44, died in the East Craigs area of Edinburgh on Monday, July 20.

‌



Emergency services responded to reports of a woman with serious injuries at a property on Craigievar Square at around 8.45pm. Despite best efforts of crews she was pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



Lee Greenan, 46, was arrested after heading into his local pub "covered in blood" and confessing to the killing, the Daily Record reports.

Greenan was remanded in custody ahead of trial after he appeared at Edinburgh Sheriff Court on Thursday, charged with her murder and two charges of assault.

View 3 Images Lee Greenan with his ex-partner Vikki Soloman (Image: Collect)

‌



The Scottish Prison Service confirmed he had been found dead at HMP Edinburgh on Sunday. It is understood Greenan died by suicide.

The property on Craigievar Square was cordoned off while forensics worked at while the Mid Yoken pub, just over a mile away, was also locked down and guarded by police as part of their investigation.

In a statement the pub said the police investigations were concerning an incident outside the pub and offered their condolences to Vikki’s family.

‌



A local who was at the Mid Yoken when Lee turned up told the Record: "Lee is well known locally. He played for the local football team, Clermiston Star, and loved his football.

"After killing Vikki, he walked into the pub covered in blood and said he'd murdered his partner. It was shocking, like something out of a film.

"It is tragic how this has played out. The families and friends of Vikki and Lee are in shock."

‌



View 3 Images Police at a taped off property on Craigievar Square Edinburgh (Image: Daily Record)

A woman's network Vikki was part of released a statement following her death about domestic violence.

It said: "Vikki was a member of our community and last night she was killed in her home. There are no words to describe how horrific this incident is, and the trail of devastation it has left.

‌



"Nearly half of women killed in Scotland are killed by a partner or ex-partner, and 89 per cent of domestic abuse happens inside the home, the place we’re supposed to feel safest.

"Police Scotland recorded over 66,000 domestic abuse incidents last year, and campaigners say that’s still only the visible part of it. If any of this feels close to home, if you’re scared, or something doesn’t sit right, reach out."

Vikki was described as "beautiful" and "a diamond" by those who knew her. Lisa Mullen said: "Thoughts to friends and family! You are a diamond, a beautiful person, until we see each other again. You will always hold a special place in my heart."

Article continues below

Arlene Mill added: "You were beautiful inside and out. I'm gonna miss our wee chats putting the world to right. Can’t take this in. Thoughts are with all the family."

A Scottish Prison Service spokesperson said: “Every death, whether in prison custody or in our communities, is a tragedy for all those who knew and supported the individual.

“Following the death of someone in our care, Police Scotland are advised, and the matter reported to the Procurator Fiscal. Fatal Accident Inquiries are held in due course.”

News.title: Reading town centre bomb scare sees man arrested after three suspicious packages found
News.content:
Reading town centre bomb scare sees man arrested after three suspicious packages found

Thames Valley Police said officers were called to the first package outside The Botanist bar and restaurant on King Street at around 6pm on Saturday

View 2 Images (Image: Get Reading)

Thames Valley Police have issued a major update after three suspicious packages were found in Reading town centre.

Officers confirmed a man has now been arrested after the discovery of the packages led to a major emergency response involving police and an Army bomb disposal unit.

Thames Valley Police said officers were called to the first package outside The Botanist bar and restaurant on King Street at around 6pm on Saturday (July 25). Two more suspicious packages were later discovered, the second outside McDonald's on Friar Street at about 9pm and the third outside The Hope Tap Wetherspoons pub on Friar Street at around 10.30pm.

Emergency services sealed off the affected areas while an Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) unit attended as a precaution. The suspicious objects were safely removed and the cordons have since been lifted.

Police confirmed a man has been arrested and enquiries are ongoing. Detectives believe the three incidents may be linked and are pursuing a number of lines of inquiry.

The response followed reports of a major incident in Reading town centre on Saturday evening, with roads around Jackson's Corner and the Simeon Monument closed for several hours while emergency services dealt with the situation.

In an update issued on Sunday, Thames Valley Police said: "Emergency services responded to an incident on Saturday evening, 25 July 2026, involving three suspicious packages in Reading city centre.

View 2 Images (Image: Get Reading)

"Police were made aware of the first package which was located outside The Botanist Reading bar and restaurant on King Street at around 6pm, a second suspicious package at around 9pm located outside McDonald's, Friar Street and a third suspicious package at around 10.30pm located outside The Hope Tap (Wetherspoons) pub on Friar Street.

"Officers from Thames Valley Police promptly attended all three scenes, where cordons were established, initially supported by an Explosive Ordnance Disposal unit as a precaution, and the objects were safely removed.

"The cordons have now been lifted. Some further disruption to traffic following road closures can be expected.

"An arrest has been made, and police are actively investigating the incidents. Officers are following several lines of inquiry. At this moment in time, police believe that all three incidents may be linked."

Superintendent Rachel Sykes said additional officers would remain in the town centre to reassure the public.

She said: "Additional patrols will be taking place in the area today to provide reassurance. The area is safe, but if you have any concerns, please speak to one of our officers while they are out on patrol.

"Thank you to those members of the public who contacted us and for the patience of those who were diverted from the area whilst our officers investigated these incidents."

Article continues below

No further details about the arrested man or the nature of the suspicious packages have yet been released. Police have appealed for anyone with information about the incidents to come forward as the investigation continues.

News.title: Mum plunges to her death during birthday party as balcony crumbles beneath her feet
News.content:
Mum plunges to her death during birthday party as balcony crumbles beneath her feet

Mum-of-two Lorenna Moraes had been celebrating with family and friends when part of a house's balcony gave way, causing the 35-year-old to plunge to her death

View 3 Images Lorenna Moraes was celebrating with her family and friends when the tragedy happened (Image: Jam Press)

A mum-of-two gym owner died in a horror birthday party plunge, after a balcony collapsed under her feet.

‌



Lorenna Moraes had been celebrating with family and pals when part of the house's balcony gave way on July 18. The 35-year-old plunged around four metres, suffering severe injuries and going into cardiac arrest twice.

‌



Emergency responders treated her at the scene in Uruçuca, Brazil, before she was rushed to a specialist hospital in nearby Ilhéus. Despite doctors' efforts to save her, she died later that night.

‌



Lorenna owned a gym in Ilhéus and was well known in the local fitness community. In the days before the tragedy, she had been sharing her excitement on social media about opening a new branch of her business, which was in its final stages of preparation.

View 3 Images The mum-of-two tragically died as a result of her injuries (Image: Jam Press)

Oliver Tree's memorial to take place next month following tragic helicopter crash READ MORE :

Instagram model’s heartbreaking final post as she shared cryptic message before she was found dead in Thailand READ MORE :

The cause of the balcony collapse is to be investigated by authorities. Photos from the scene appear to suggest the balcony railing gave way. Some local reports said Lorenna hit her head on the kerb after falling.

‌



Lorenna is survived by her husband, their son and daughter, and her mother. She regularly shared glimpses of her family life on social media. In a post from May, she wrote: "Holding my children's hands, hearing their laughter and creating memories that will last a lifetime is priceless."

Earlier that month, she wrote: "Being a mother has completely transformed me. It has taught me about strength, devotion and boundless love. And having a mother reminds me every day where my care, my courage and my way of loving come from.

View 3 Images Lorenna suffered a head injury (Image: Jam Press)

Article continues below

"I am grateful for the arms that once held me and for the arms that I can now open to my children." It comes after several people were injured in a balcony collapse at a wedding venue earlier this year.

The ceremony was taking place in the small town of Kaladhungi in India when the horror fall occurred. Several people fell from the balcony of a neighbouring house as the wedding started.

Local news outlets have reported that six people have been left in hospital after the incident. The collapse occurred just before the wedding procession arrived, leaving the bride and groom distraught.

News.title: Amanda Redman speaks out on homelessness and hostility to migrants - and her hopes for new PM
News.content:
Amanda Redman has spoken of her concern at worsening levels of homelessness and what she considers a lack of humanity towards those less fortunate in society.

The three-time BAFTA-nominated actor told how she is seeing more rough sleepers than ever on the streets of London, where she has lived for more than 40 years after growing up in Brighton. And she admits she has also been left upset by seeing protests and hostility towards migrants, including those who have made the desperate decision to risk their lives by travelling across the Channel on dinghies.

In an exclusive interview with the Mirror, Amanda, 68, said: "I don't think as a young person, I was really aware of homelessness. You can't help but be now for all sorts of socio-political reasons.

View 7 Images Amanda admits she wasn't really aware of homelessness when she was young, but now believes it is impossible to avoid (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Andy Burnham urged to create dedicated homeless unit in Downing Street to end rough sleeping READ MORE :

"It's something that just wasn't there when I first moved to London, it just wasn't there. And now it is, and you can't avoid it. And not just in central London, I think, also, on the outskirts and in the suburbs, everywhere. It seems to be a growing thing."

Amanda, who was awarded an MBE for services to drama and charity in 2012, has supported a number of organisations, including Ealing Soup Kitchen, which helps increasing numbers of homeless people with food and other services.

Official statistics from earlier this year showed a record number of people slept rough on the streets of England in 2025, representing the fourth year in a row that numbers have risen. An estimated 4,793 people spent the night in tents, doorways and parks on a single night in autumn 2025, up 3% year on year, and overtaking the previous peak of 4,751 in 2017.

Amanda is now hoping new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who vowed to end the problem after visiting homeless shelter The Passage last Monday, can make a difference.

‌



View 7 Images New Prime Minister Andy Burnham chops mushrooms as he helps prepare breakfast during a visit to The Passage Homeless Charity in London on July 20, (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

She said: "Good for him that he's decided to do something about it and let's wait and see with fingers crossed. If Andy Burnham is true to his word, then good luck to him, I think that would be amazing, wouldn't it? But it's a big thing to combat."

Amanda has previously travelled across the world supporting charities, including the British Red Cross and World Vision, in a bid to bring global attention to vulnerable children and adults, including following natural disasters.

Speaking about violent anti-immigration protests against migrants to Britain, including outside hotels, Amanda said: "I think we're in a very bad time at the moment. It saddens me hugely to see the lack of humanity towards people who have lost everything and in a way that we can't possibly comprehend.

‌



"You've got to be bloody desperate to do what they do to get somewhere, and who would blame them, you know? It really upsets me."

7 View 7 Images Amanda was awarded an MBE for services to drama and charity in 2012 (Image: Getty Images) 7 View 7 Images The actor has travelled the world supporting charities, including the British Red Cross

Amanda, who became a grandmother 18 months ago when her daughter Emily gave birth to a little girl called Cora, added: "It must be awful. I mean there's people with little ones. The idea of my baby granddaughter being put through that is just so horrifying... awful. I'd like to see people show more humanity. In the end, we're all citizens of the world."

‌



Amanda has enjoyed an illustrious career, which has included her playing Diana Dors in The Blonde Bombshell, Deedee Dove opposite Ray Winstone in gangster flick Sexy Beast, lottery winner Alison in At Home With the Braithwaites and Lydia Fonseca in The Good Karma Hospital.

She remains one of Britain's favourite actors, but is also now trying her hand at directing an immersive Shakespeare production at London's historic Middle Temple. Her production 'Walk the Bard' will transform the legal library's hidden gardens into a live theatrical adventure, including six curated scenes from Shakespeare’s most treasured plays over three days next month.

The audience will be wearing audio headsets as they move through the gardens, where the actors, including a classic Shakespearean fool, work around them in the venue, said to be where Tweltfh Night was first performed in front of Queen Elizabeth I.

View 7 Images Amanda during rehearsals for Walk The Bard, which is her first professional production as a director

‌



Amanda said: "I came up with this idea of a promenade around the theme of love, where we have a sort of generic type Shakespearean fool, who takes the audience round to different parts of the garden and then popping out from behind the bushes and behind the trees are the characters and all these different plays.

"I don't think it's been done like that before, so it's quite exciting. It's a new challenge, directing. I've directed for years at my theatre school, but I've never done professional productions before, so this is the first time doing that.

"It's a lot of responsibility and a lot of hard work, but I'm thoroughly enjoying myself. It is very different to doing TV. What you get back from the audience, the feedback is incredible. You don't get that back from a camera. In theatre, things go wrong and you have to deal with that and audiences often love that actually, because then they really do feel part of it."

As well as working, the mum-of-one, who bravely went public about suffering nine miscarriages and two ectopic pregnancies in her 40s and 50s, is also enjoying being a grandmother, which she says feels very different to being a mum.

‌



View 7 Images Amanda is enjoying the challenge of working as a director after an illustrious acting career

Amanda said: "It's fabulous, I love it. I didn't think I would, but I do with every bit of me, it's fantastic. It's different from being a parent - for a start you can give them back. So I get the best bits and as a result of that, actually, you've got more time to play with them and to give them your attention.

"You're not the mum having to worry about everything. If she wants to fling food or whatever all over my kitchen, I don't care. I would have done as a mum!".

Asked if she would like to see her follow in her footsteps by becoming an actor, she said: "My daughter says over her dead body would she become an actor! But I would want her to do whatever her heart and her passion dictates to her, and I'll support her 100% with whatever it is."

‌



To buy tickets to Walk the Bard, visit here

News.title: Burnham says he is prepared to call out Trump 'if right for Britain'
News.content:
Burnham said: "My strength is remaining close to people, close to the public, that will not change as prime minister."

Asked if he would call out Trump if it was the right thing, he said, "of course", going on to say: "You have to defend your own national interest before anything else. That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly."

Burnham also said he had had "concern" about the president starting the conflict with Iran, and he "wouldn't hold back from saying what I think is right".

Responding to Burnham's comments, Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: "Clearly, the US is a long standing ally. We need to have good relations with them but if they do something we disagree with, we should honestly say so."

The prime minister would not commit to a date when the government would spend 3% of GDP on defence. His Chancellor John Healey resigned from the previous government saying that unless a commitment was made to spend that amount by 2030, the country would not be safe.

But Burnham said: "I appointed my new chancellor very aware of what he had said about the critical importance of defence spending and the position that he had taken about that.

"The first challenge facing us both is to ensure that the defence investment plan is fully funded and that's the thing that's right in front of us and we need to work that through as we go towards the budget later this year."

News.title: Andy Burnham rules out early election in exclusive BBC interview
News.content:
In an exclusive interview with the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, Andy Burnham explicitly dismissed the idea of an early general election, saying "I'm going to rule it out... I don't think people want it."

Explaining his decision, the new prime minister suggested the majority of the electorate "voted for a manifesto" in the last election, and vowed he would "honour that manifesto" with the support of parliamentary colleagues.

Burnham went on to say, "I just think what I most need to do is get Britain focused on getting the country back where it should be, getting it working."

Andy Burnham: The Laura Kuenssberg Interview will be available across BBC News on Sunday and the interview will be shown in full on Panorama on BBC One on Monday at 20:00 BST.

News.title: Gatwick Airport left without running water after major outage
News.content:
Passengers at Gatwick Airport have faced long queues for toilets and closed restaurants and bars after a major water supply outage.

Both terminals at the UK's second busiest airport lost running water on Sunday morning after a power failure at a treatment works that serves the area.

People told the BBC of confusion and frustration as all bars and restaurants were shut, some were left with nowhere to sit and waits built up outside toilets.

Gatwick said it was still experiencing disruption and was handing out bottled water, while SES Water, the company that supplies the airport, said the power outage was fixed and water supplies were gradually returning.

The company, which also supplies parts of Kent, Surrey and south London, said complications caused by a power outage at Bough Beech treatment works meant some customers had experienced low water pressure or a temporary loss of supply.

A spokesperson had earlier confirmed that Gatwick Airport was affected.

On Sunday afternoon, SES Water said its treatment works were back up and running, but later added it would take time for the network to fully return to normal as it had been "a highly unusual and complex issue".

"We want to reiterate that our teams are working as quickly as they possibly can and we are grateful for everyone's patience," the spokesperson added.

Gatwick apologised and said the supply issue was continuing to cause disruption.

In a statement, it said: "There is currently no water supply in either terminal.

"Our staff are on hand to support passengers and provide assistance where needed, some restaurant partners have opened to provide additional seating."

Gatwick said additional teams had been deployed across both terminals to support passengers.

The airport added there had been no flight cancellations as a result of the supply issues and that it was working closely with SES Water to minimise the impact.

News.title: Meghan calls Harry 'a charmer' during MasterChef Australia appearance
News.content:
Early on in the episode, Meghan was asked what her favourite dish is to make at home.

She said it was "a tough one because I have a lot of palettes to appease", with her British-born husband favouring "meat, potatoes and cream sauce" while she preferred grilled fish.

Their two children, Archie and Lilibet, often help with meal preparation and are "great eaters", she said.

"We're really lucky on that front," she added.

She then urged the chefs to cook something they felt connected to. "What's the story behind it?" she asked them.

When Prince Harry dialled in later on during the episode, Meghan told them: "My husband's here," prompting cheers and shocked faces from contestants and spectators.

"I wish you could try these, these dishes are fantastic," she told him, before showing him the food. He signed off by telling her to go and enjoy, adding: "Very sorry to disturb you."

The duchessâs appearance on the latest season of the show was well received by Hello Magazine, external, which shared a video of the episode online and complimented Meghan for the way she interacted with the chefs.

"The Duchess of Sussex gave personal time calls to all the contestants, proving that she's always so effortlessly elegant," it wrote.

Writing in The Sunday Times, external, Charlotte Ivers was less impressed, saying her appearance on the show "told us nothing about what she likes or who even will leave the competition".

Social media users were also split, with one viewer writing that Meghan was "warm, gracious and a delight to watch" while another called Prince Harry's cameo appearance "cringe".

News.title: Norris wins his first grand prix of year in Hungary
News.content:
Verstappen was unhappy with his car for much of the race, with regular complaints on team radio, but Red Bull pulled a masterstroke when they fitted soft tyres to his car at his second pit stop.

The aim was to challenge Hamilton in the later laps after the seven-time champion made an early second stop with 40 laps still to go.

It was heading towards a tense climax when Piastri's retirement brought out the VSC.

That prompted a late round of pit stops, Ferrari bringing in both their drivers and putting them behind Verstappen.

Hamilton came out of the pits and passed Antonelli into the first corner, after the Italian stayed out under the VSC, but had to give the place back after the restart because the Mercedes driver had just passed the key line on the track in front.

Antonelli and Hamilton started chasing back towards Verstappen, but they were delayed while lapping Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto.

That looked as if it might be decisive, but in the end Verstappen was comfortably able to keep Antonelli at bay, crossing the line 3.6 seconds ahead.

Another key point in Verstappen's race had been his re-passing of Hamilton after the Ferrari had got briefly ahead following the first pit stops.

That gave him clear air and enabled the Dutchman to consolidate his race position in third place behind the McLarens, laying the foundations for Red Bull's late strategy call.

Hamilton will leave Hungary ruing another penalty - the one for speeding in the pit lane was his second in two days after behind penalised for blocking Piastri in qualifying, and follows two others at the previous two races in Belgium and Britain.

Behind him, Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was sixth, ahead of Russell, who dropped to 21st place on the first lap after his anti-stall kicked in at the start, and fought back strongly.

At Aston Martin, Lance Stroll finished in 13th, ahead of team-mate Fernando Alonso, their positions dictated to a degree by luck under the VSC and their divergent strategies.

But the key point was that Alonso, in particular, was able to fight with other cars for the first time, and he ran a long first stint on the soft tyres, before switching to the mediums, which was a bold strategy.

The long-awaited upgrade to their car, which was new apart from the front suspension, engine and gearbox, has reduced their lap times by about two seconds.

A Honda engine upgrade is due for the Dutch Grand Prix, the next race in four weeks' time after the summer break, which the team hope will elevate them further and potentially bring the possibility of the occasional points finish into the picture.

News.title: Teen charged over record crossing on 'mega dinghy'
News.content:
A teenager charged over a small boat Channel crossing was allegedly piloting a "mega dinghy" carrying a record 165 migrants from France to England, the National Crime Agency has said.

Sudanese national Chan Mathok Atak, 19, is accused of endangering another during a journey by sea to the UK on Thursday and is due to appear at Margate Magistrates' Court on Monday.

The number on the dinghy broke the previous record from July, when 128 crossed the Channel from France on one vessel.

According to Home Office figures, more than 13,000 arrivals have been recorded in 2026, which is 45% lower than this time in 2025 and down 18% on the same period in 2024.

Border Security Command was pictured towing a dinghy - estimated to be about the same size as a standard bus at 13m (42ft) long - when it arrived in Dover in Kent on Thursday afternoon.

Home Office figures showed 366 people arrived after crossing in three boats on Thursday during warm, sunny weather and calm conditions at sea.

On Wednesday, 172 people made the journey in three boats, bringing an end to an 11-day hiatus because of windy conditions in the Channel.

Refugee charity Care4Calais said the crossing route was becoming "more and more dangerous" because of the increasing number of people in each boat.

News.title: Ryan Gosling to join Marvel Cinematic Universe as Ghost Rider
News.content:
Ryan Gosling will join the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) as the titular character in a new Ghost Rider film, the company has announced.

Speaking during the surprise announcement at San Diego Comic-Con on Saturday, Gosling said it is a character he has "wanted to play for a very long time".

The film is due to be released in 2028, and will be the third about the motorcycle-riding anti-hero.

It will follow the 2007 film of the same name starring Nicolas Cage, and its follow-up, 2011's Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance.

Before making the big reveal on stage at San Diego Comic-Con, Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige said he had often been asked when Gosling would join the MCU.

Shortly after, the lights turned off. When they returned, the actor appeared on stage to cheers from screaming fans.

Speaking about the role, Gosling said: "Wow, is this really happening?"

He has previously spoken about his desire to take on the role. Appearing on Josh Horowitz's Happy Sad Confused podcast in March, he confirmed he was in discussions with Marvel.

Ghost Rider is the anti-hero identity of motorcycle stuntman Johnny Blaze.

The character's story begins when he becomes bound to the Spirit of Vengeance Zarathos after making a deal with villain Mephisto to spare his surrogate father, giving him superpowers.

The film will be directed by Shawn Levy, who Gosling described as the "only" director for the project.

Levy has previously directed Deadpool & Wolverine in the MCU, and is currently working with Gosling on Star Wars: Starfighter, which is due to be released next year.

Levy told the crowd that he and Gosling spent a lot of their downtime on set daydreaming about Ghost Rider and swapping ideas.

The director said: "As Ryan started talking about his vision for this character, we started riffing, and I finally said, 'bro, let's ride', so guys, we'll see you in 2028."

News.title: How rapper Aitch's sister inspired him to climb one of the world's toughest peaks
News.content:
He's skydived, eaten raw fish eyes on I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! and now Aitch has reached new heights - literally - by climbing Mount Kilimanjaro.

The Manchester rapper has been pursuing some of these tasks to raise awareness and money for the Down's Syndrome Association in honour of his younger sister Gracie, who has the condition.

Aitch tells BBC Newsbeat the 16-year-old is an "absolute legend in the streets of Manchester" and beyond.

"Everyone loves her. She's just a big bottle of light in every room," he says.

"She's everyone's best friend and she's just got such a positive outlook on the world.

"I just feel like everyone should be more like her."

The musician's journey up Kilimanjaro has been captured in an upcoming Netflix documentary, Aitch: Don't Be Afraid.

But he says the whole point of it was to share how having someone in his life with Down's syndrome is "one of the best things in the world".

However, the 26-year-old admits he does feel "a little bit of pressure" to up the scale and fundraising targets of his challenges.

"You've just got to think about the end goal, which is trying to raise the most money and make the most difference to what's going on," he says.

News.title: Iran's 'sabre-rattling' should not intimidate UK, Wes Streeting says
News.content:
When asked if Iran had the capability to attack the UK, Streeting said: "I think we shouldn't put too much stock in the sabre-rattling of Iran, and we certainly shouldn't be intimidated by what the regime has said this week".

He also repeated the UK's position from the outset of the US war against Iran saying "we have not joined and will not join offensive US military action in Iran.

"That's an area where we have not agreed with the United States, but when it comes to securing maritime freedom and free commercial shipping in the straight Hormuz, that's where we are absolutely aligned".
