Streeting said he is to meet with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth in the coming week after "kicking around" ideas for ways "to bring the countries together" and had been "delighted" to speak to Hegseth by phone already.

He also said that the UK is ready to lead a naval mission to help remove mines from the Strait of Hormuz "when the conditions are right".

Securing safe shipping routes through the area was important because of the impact the crisis is having on energy prices and the cost of living, he added.

Streeting also dismissed a Russian warship's recent live-firing exercise in the English Channel as "performative" but added it was a "reminder of the frankly unsafe and unprofessional way in which they have been conducting themselves".

Branding the Channel incident "irresponsible", Streeting said Russia posed a threat to UK security, adding that the public does not see "the enormous efforts that take place every day to counter Russian aggression".

News.title: Another UK heatwave looms after cooler end to weekend
News.content:
Sunday will be a cooler day for the whole of the UK as temperatures fall widely by a couple of degrees.

A few locations will finally mark the end to their third heatwave of the year, including Usk in Monmouthshire and Exeter in Devon.

Both places are forecast to see temperatures drop beneath the heatwave threshold for the first time in 21 consecutive days.

Temperatures will largely be in the mid-20s Celsius for the south-east of the UK and in the mid-teens Celsius further north.

For many, the relief from the heat will be short-lived as high pressure is set to build close to the south of the UK next week.

This will stall rain-bearing weather fronts and any wet weather will become confined to northern and western areas - especially north-west Scotland.

In southern parts of the UK, temperatures look set to climb once again.

Tapping into the heat over the near continent, the UK is likely to enter another heatwave, with temperatures in England and Wales forecast to peak around 25-32C for much of next week.

Yellow heat health alerts will come into effect for Yorkshire and Humber, the West and East Midlands, the East of England, London, south-east and south-west, at 9:00 BST on 28 July 2026 and last until 9:00 BST on 31 July.

The UKHSA warns that heat is expected to cause minor impacts for health and social care services, with an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

News.title: What a week's work experience taught these Year 10s about their futures
News.content:
When Kelsey first arrived at secondary school, she said she wanted to be almost anywhere else but there.

She struggled with friendships, clashed with teachers and often tried to avoid coming into school.

But after a week's work experience placement at Whipsnade Zoo, in Bedfordshire, her outlook could not be more different.

She said it made her a "completely different person" - more confident, with a "good group of friends" and a greater sense of purpose about where her education could lead her.

Children across the UK are strongly encouraged to do work experience while at school. In England, the government published new legal guidance in June for schools to deliver two weeks of "in-person and immersive" work experience in future, one between Year 7 and Year 9, and one between Years 10 and 11.

But not all work experience placements are equal, and finding the right one can be tricky.

Organisations like the Sutton Trust and the Social Mobility Foundation said some students could be limited by the availability of placements in their area, or a lack of family connections with local employers.

BBC News spoke to three Year 10 pupils, one year ahead of their final GCSE exams, about how they decided what areas of work they were interested in, their experiences of trying to find the right placement, and what it taught them about their future education and ultimate career goals.

News.title: My entire family went on a boat trip that they never returned from
News.content:
"It's something you don't get over - you learn to live with it."

Sixty years ago, Peter Watts' entire family was killed in a boating tragedy that shocked the nation.

His nine-year-old sister Angela, 10-year-old brother David, mother Doreen and father Frederick George, along with 11 others, died when the Prince of Wales pleasure boat sank on the Mawddach Estuary in Gwynedd on 22 July, 1966.

Now, a memorial recalling the names of the 15 people who lost their lives has been unveiled.

It was another chance for Peter to travel from the village he grew up in, near Milton Keynes, to the picturesque estuary where the catastrophe unfolded.

News.title: Residents allowed to return after Cairngorms wildfire evacuation
News.content:
Residents of the village of Nethy Bridge, near the wildfire that has been burning in the Cairngorms, have been told they can return to their homes after being evacuated on Friday night.

The fire was declared a major incident due to a change in weather, but that has now been stood down by Police Scotland.

First Minister John Swinney said the government and emergency services will continue to treat the blaze with the utmost seriousness until the last flames are out.

Locals have criticised the handling of the wildfire, which has been burning for 10 days, saying the move to declare it a major incident came too late and the government had been slow in scaling up their response.

In a statement on Saturday night, Police Scotland said "after an extensive multi-agency response to a large fire within Cairngorms National Park, residents of Nethy Bridge are being advised that they can now return to their properties".

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service's deputy assistant chief officer, Kenny Barbour, said the decision to stand down the major incident followed a detailed assessment by emergency responders.

He added in a statement: "The extensive work carried out over recent days, including the creation of effective fire breaks, has significantly reduced the risk to nearby communities, allowing evacuated residents to safely return home."

Supt Judy Hill added that the "ongoing multi agency response remains a high priority, with significant partnership resources and volunteers working tirelessly and in challenging circumstances, to support our efforts to extinguish the fires".

Firefighters will continue to maintain a significant operational presence until the incident is safely concluded, with 75 remaining on the ground on Saturday, police said.

At a meeting of the Scottish government's resilience room on Saturday evening, the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said there had been "good progress" in strengthening fire breaks to protect residential areas and said the number of fire hot spots was reducing.

First Minister John Swinney welcomed the lifting of the evacuation notice but stressed that "the Scottish Government, the emergency services and all relevant authorities will continue to treat this wildfire, as has been the case since its onset, with the utmost seriousness and necessary resources until the last flames are out."

News.title: Man in critical condition after sea rescue
News.content:
A man is in a critical condition in hospital after three people got into difficulty in the water near an Essex pier.

Emergency services were called to an incident at Clacton-on-Sea shortly after 16:30 BST on Saturday.

A man aged in his 50s is in a critical but stable condition, Essex Police said.

Two other people, a man aged in his 20s and a teenage girl, remain in hospital but are "recovering well", the force added.

All three people knew each other.

News.title: 'It was like a movie - I looked up and an exploded barn rained on me'
News.content:
The photographer was driving to his studio for a meeting when he realised the fire on the horizon was at the farm where it was based.

"It was about 150 metres (492ft) from my front door, and I quickly cancelled the meeting and thought, 'I'm not happy with where the wind is going on this'," he said.

Johnson began removing some of his more expensive kit from the studio and was putting it in the van when the explosion took place.

A unit housing fertiliser had exploded.

He said: "It blew me into the door and I just ran to the van, dropped the bit I went back in for - maybe it saved my life, I don't know."

As it happened: Twenty firefighters taken to hospital after major Essex explosion

The photographer was shocked to see his studio roof had completely caved in.

Having driven to a safe distance, "I pulled over, and I was just in shock and started to shake", he said, although he was reassured after an ambulance crew checked him over.

Johnson managed to cover his wedding booking on Saturday, praising his "amazing assistant" James Musselwhite for driving from Portsmouth to help him out.

"I'm in a little bit of shock still, to be honest," he said.

"I'm completely unscathed apart from a bit of a dodgy ear from the pressure - but how I've got away with it unscathed I have no idea."

News.title: Tourists describe their escape from France wildfires
News.content:
Families have relived how their tranquil holidays in France turned into a race to escape raging wildfires.

Tourists told the BBC of emergency alerts in the middle of the night, desperate drives just metres from six-storey high flames and the sight of people flocking to beaches with their suitcases.

Huge forest fires in south-west France and central Spain have displaced more than 220,000 people, with the French military drafted in to help and the Spanish government declaring a national emergency.

Winds and continued heat are still helping to fan the flames with some tourists reporting smelling acrid smoke like a "bonfire" far outside the affected areas.

Flights to Bordeaux and Madrid, the closest cities to the blaze-hit regions, are currently not affected. Earlier on Saturday, a French foreign minister described the fires as a "tragedy" but urged tourists not to cancel their travel plans.

Among those caught up in the crisis is Zac Morrison, who arrived in Cap Ferret - a popular peninsula blanketed with pine trees 40 miles (65km) south-west of Bordeaux - on Thursday.

The 21-year-old from London, who is on holiday with 10 members of his family, woke up to two text alerts at 04:00 and 06:00 local time ordering him to evacuate "by all means necessary".

Lando Norris admitted it was “good to be back” after securing the first win of his world championship defence at Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Norris surrendered the lead to McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri following a sloppy start from pole position.

However, the reigning world champion took advantage of Piastri’s bizarre collision with backmarker Carlos Sainz midway through the race to seize the initiative and cross the line a comfortable winner.

It marked Norris’ first triumph since November’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix, and he said: “My pace today was probably some of the best I’ve ever had.

“The car was beautiful to drive and I felt very confident. I’m just happy to be back and see the number one again. I want to believe we can carry this form forward and we can win more races.”

After losing the lead, Norris, clearly the faster of the McLaren drivers, was hot in his pursuit of Piastri and challenged the pit-wall to order his team-mate out of the way.

But in the end he did not need the order. Piastri’s afternoon unravelled on lap 38 of 70 when Sainz, preoccupied in his duel with Fernando Alonso for 15th, rammed a mystified Piastri off the road.

“Get out of the f****** way you idiot, oh my God,” yelled Piastri. The Australian could not believe what had unfolded in front of him but for Norris it was the ideal opportunity to snatch the lead. He did not hesitate to change tyres and rejoined ahead of Piastri.

open image in gallery Norris was smiling after a first win of the season (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

“Oscar, that’s Sainz that cost us that,” said Tom Stallard, Piastri’s race engineer. “Oh mate, just don’t even f****** talk to me,” he replied.

It would get worse for Piastri when his gearbox expired with 14 laps remaining. A Virtual Safety Car was deployed, and Norris was able to dive in for a third pit-stop and retain the lead.

He took the chequered flag 15 seconds ahead of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen following a commanding drive. He is 91 points adrift of Kimi Antonelli with 12 rounds left.

For George Russell, it marked another chapter in his bad-luck story. His new Mercedes engine went into anti-stall as the lights went out, leaving him 19th at the end of lap one. He recovered to seventh but is now 59 points off the title pace.

“I am past the point of disappointment now,” he said. “If I continue to be disappointed with everything that goes on, I will just be disappointed every day of the week.

“I’ve got to stay positive. Another technical issue which completely ruined the race, but my pace was as strong as anyone out there. It is unbelievable the list of things that have gone wrong for me this season.

“We are not the only ones, but it feels like it is happening substantially more to me than others. Hopefully it swings round. I don’t wish any bad luck on anyone but I haven’t had a season like this in my entire career.

“The pace was fine but the result was s***. I usually don’t feel like I need the summer break but this year I definitely do.”

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal’s shock move for Vinicius Jr hits hurdle, Liverpool told Bradley Barcola fee
News.content:
Arsenal are plotting an audacious move for Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr and want to sign the Brazil winger this summer. The Premier League champions have yet to make contact with Real Madrid over the move for the 26-year-old, who has just one more year on his contract, while incoming boss at the Bernabeu, Jose Mourinho, would need to sanction the transfer.

It could be a busy few weeks for Mikel Arteta’s side as they also look to sign Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes and add another centre-back, with England internationals Ezri Konsa and John Stones both of interest. Newcastle manager Eddie Howe confirmed that he wants to keep Guimaraes, but added that his future at the club is out of his control.

Elsewhere, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has set out his targets for the transfer window and has confirmed the Reds “definitely need to sign a winger”, while France international Bradley Barcola is reportedly open to leaving Paris Saint-Germain this summer. PSG, who are set to miss out on the signing Yan Diomande to Real Madrid, would demand a record fee, however.

Manchester United are still interested in adding another midfielder and have “reached an agreement in principle” with France international Manu Kone, according to reports in Italy. Aurelien Tchouameni remains a target, too.

Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu said Sunday that New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani is “fomenting hate” by calling the prime minister a war criminal who should be arrested over the war in Gaza if he visits the city for the United Nations General Assembly.

Netanyahu said he intends to be in New York in September to address the annual U.N. gathering of world leaders, despite the mayor's suggestion that he is not welcome. Mamdani said last week that while New York City does not have legal authority to execute an arrest warrant issued by the world's top war-crimes court, he encouraged the federal government to do so.

“He’s supposed to be the mayor of all New Yorkers — Jews, Christians, Muslims, everyone,” Netanyahu said on Fox News Channel's “Sunday Morning Futures” with Maria Bartiromo. “But he’s trying to turn one group against the other.”

The prime minister has become an increasingly polarizing figure over Israel's war in Gaza, which was ignited by the Oct. 7, 2023, deadly attack on southern Israel by Hamas militants. Israel also joined the U.S. in starting the war against Iran on Feb. 28 before launching a ground invasion in southern Lebanon in response to fire from the Iranian-backed Hezbollah group.

Netanyahu on Sunday dismissed the International Criminal Court's war crimes charges against him as “bogus.” He pointed to sexual misconduct allegations against the ICC's top prosecutor, who was removed from that post on Friday, and said the warrant was an attempt to divert attention.

The mayor’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment Sunday.

Bipartisan U.S. support for Israel at risk, Netanyahu says

Netanyahu said he was concerned that once-bipartisan political support for Israel in the U.S. is at risk, particularly as progressive and far-left Democrats aligned with the Mamdani wing of the party splinter.

He also warned against rising antisemitism in the U.S. and other Western countries, saying that when he talks to people in New York City, home to the second-largest Jewish population in the world, "Jews feel very uncomfortable.”

“And I think it’s wrong. The whole thing is wrong,” he said.

Throughout his mayoral election campaign last year, Mamdani said he would seek to order the city’s police to execute the ICC’s arrest warrant over Netanyahu's role in the war in Gaza.

But Mamdani acknowledged last week that his city did not have the legal authority to arrest Netanyahu and called on federal authorities to step in.

“I want to be equally clear, Benjamin Netanyahu is not welcome in New York City, nor is any other war criminal at large,” he said in a video message.

He told New Yorkers that he understood their frustration and that expressions of protest is something the city would “always respect.”

The Hague-based court has accused Netanyahu, his former defense minister and the late leader of Hamas of crimes against humanity. The Palestinian territory’s Health Ministry says over 73,000 people have been killed in Israel’s offensive — roughly half of them women and children. Some 1,200 people, most of them civilians, were killed in the initial Hamas attack on Israel.

Trump has assured Netanyahu he won't be arrested

Trump told Netanyahu in a social media post Monday that he “will not be arrested, in any way, shape, or form, while in the United States of America.”

Netanyahu is expected in Washington this week to meet with Trump and attend funeral services for the late Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina.

Graham, a leading defense hawk and strong supporter of Israel, died suddenly two weeks ago of a likely torn aorta. The prime minster called him an “extraordinary American patriot.”

___

Associated Press reporter Anthony Izaguirre in New York contributed to this report.

Lewis Hamilton said he will seek an explanation from Ferrari about the team’s strategy at Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix which left him ruing a “missed opportunity” in his bid for a record eighth world championship.

As Lando Norris cashed in on McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri’s bizarre collision with a backmarker to secure the first win of his title defence, Hamilton finished fifth in a Ferrari which undoubtedly had the speed to carry him to victory.

Kimi Antonelli, the Italian teenager he is attempting to hunt down in the standings, started two places behind Hamilton in a Mercedes which has been so dominant all season but was out of sorts at the Hungaroring.

However, Antonelli still managed to cross the line two places ahead of Hamilton in third to extend his title advantage over the British driver from 45 points to 50.

Hamilton was aggrieved that a “communication error” contributed to him blocking Oscar Piastri in qualifying and serve a three-place grid drop from second to fifth.

Hamilton was then running in second place in Sunday’s race when Ferrari elected to surrender track position – at a venue where overtaking had proved largely impossible – by pitting their driver for a third time during a late Virtual Safety Car period.

He was gazumped by Max Verstappen and Antonelli, and was then hit with a five-second penalty for pit-lane speeding, dropping him behind team-mate Charles Leclerc and a subsequent 11-point championship swing.

In an emotive post after qualifying, Hamilton stressed how “every point counts”. And when asked after Sunday’s race whether he had missed an opportunity in the title race, he replied: “Yes. I’m not really sure why we stopped at the end.

open image in gallery Hamilton passes Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar into turn one (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

“I got the call right at the pit-lane entry and I didn’t have time to debate it. You put your faith in the team.

“I would never have stopped if it meant I’d give up track position. We should have stayed out. I need to go and see why the team pulled me in.

“We probably would have lost out to Max because he was on fresher tyres. But I may have been able to hold on to second. We’ve lost a whole bunch of points. It was pretty bad, pretty frustrating.”

In his haste to emerge from his third stop ahead of Antonelli, Hamilton broke the 80kph limit by just 0.1kph.

It marked his fourth penalty across the three most recent rounds with his two sanctions this weekend coming after a false start at Silverstone and a collision with George Russell in Belgium. Hamilton said over the radio that the stewards were “handing out penalties like crazy”.

He continued: “Silverstone was my fault at the start. At the last race, even the driver I collided with said it was a racing incident, and they gave me a penalty. That was not needed. And that’s cost me a lot of points.

“Yesterday was unfortunate. I take responsibility, I should have looked in my mirrors. It was a communication error.

“I will work hard to come back, and reset. I have to make sure I don’t give them a reason to give me any more penalties.”

The sport heads for a three-week summer shutdown before the next round in the Netherlands on August 23 – the first of 12 scheduled races still remaining.

And Hamilton, 41, concluded: “We have to keep on pushing. From my side, the second half is usually a much stronger period for me, so I will take this time to come back stronger, fitter and better.”

News.title: Trump’s border czar admits he doesn’t know whether ICE agents behind fatal shootings are still on active duty
News.content:

Donald Trump’s “border czar” was pressed by a CNN host about recent fatal shootings by ICE agents on Sunday and admitted that he wasn’t sure about the status of the agents involved in those shootings.

Two deadly incidents in Maine and Texas within a week caused Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to temporarily halt traffic stops and reassess their tactics, according to multiple news reports. In one case, the victim had legal residence within the United States.

Tom Homan was interviewed on CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday and said that while it was general policy for agents involved in such incidents to be placed on administrative leave, he wasn’t tracking the cases and couldn’t say whether that policy was being followed.

“I don't know specifically. I haven't been involved with the investigations,” he told CNN’s Dana Bash. He added: “I've said from day one I won't comment on an investigation, but I can tell you I haven't specifically tracked these cases, but I can tell you, per policy, they're usually put on administrative leave pending the investigation, pending sworn statements, internal affairs interviews and the entire investigation.”

The Independent reached out to DHS to clarify if proper administrative leave policies were followed in the wake of the Maine and Texas shootings. Homan went on to face questions about whether an ICE agent involved in the shooting of a 25-year-old Colombian national living lawfully in the U.S., Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, should have been on the force at all. A Maine newspaper, the Portland Press Herald, reported on Saturday that the agent identified in the press as having shot Guerrero, David Brouillette, is now in protective custody.

open image in gallery A poster calling for a national day of action against ICE hangs near a makeshift street-side memorial for Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, a driver who was fatally shot on July 13 ( Reuters )

“Court documents reveal one of the ICE officers connected to the fatal shooting in Maine was accused of abuse by two ex-wives. One of his ex-wives told my colleague Erin Burnett that she experienced severe domestic violence in her marriage and that he always displayed violent behavior, and even that, if anything ever happened to her, he'd be the one to look at,” Bash told Homan.

She continued: “I should say he denied the allegations. But, at one point, a judge ordered him to temporarily relinquish any firearms. Should someone with those issues be an ICE agent?”

Homan flatly denied that such an individual, in his eyes, should have made it through the vetting process.

His remarks come amid a time of troubled leadership for America’s immigration authorities, whose positions have been transformed under the second Trump administration into a rapid deportation machine. The White House has set quotas for daily arrest totals as high as 3,000 nationwide as the president and his team hope to achieve previously unprecedented levels of detentions and deportations.

open image in gallery Border Czar Tom Homan speaks to reporters outside of the White House on July 20, 2026 ( Getty )

The border czar went on to say that increased training being implemented by ICE’s new acting director would address issues of officer conduct that have riled Democrats and even some Republicans on the Hill. But it’s not clear how much of that training will apply to ICE agents already in the field, or how soon it will be implemented.

open image in gallery White House official Stephen Miller, architect of Trump's deportation agenda, has set a goal of 3,000 immigration arrests per day ( Reuters )

It’s also unclear whether the agency is doing anything to address vetting issues now identified by Homan himself, and previously highlighted by lawmakers in Congress.

An ex-wife of Brouillette told The Independent this past week that investigators charged with vetting new ICE hires, who carry firearms on the job, never got in contact with her despite having been involved in court proceedings with him over domestic disputes in the past.

“This could have been 100 percent preventable,” she said.

This is the second time in less than a year that fatal shootings by Trump’s immigration authorities have spurred reassessments of strategy by those in charge in Washington.

open image in gallery The scope of Donald Trump's deportation agenda has spurred protests, including this one outside an ICE detention facility in Newark ( AFP/Getty )

Previously, the shootings of two Americans in Minneapolis led to authorities scaling back a federal immigration enforcement surge in that city and eventually contributed to the ouster of DHS Secretary Kristi Noem and Greg Bovino, ICE’s commander.

DHS officials have declined to confirm the names of any of the agents involved in the shootings.

“We will never confirm or deny attempts to dox our law enforcement officers,” a spokesperson told The Independent. “Doxxing our officers put their lives and their families in serious danger. Our law enforcement officers are on the frontlines arresting terrorists, gang members, murderers, pedophiles, and rapists. Now, thanks to the malicious rhetoric of sanctuary politicians, they are under constant threat from violent agitators.”

President Donald Trump shared an AI-generated image of CNN’s Kaitlan Collins seemingly morphed with transgender actress and influencer Dylan Mulvaney — days after comparing the two with a bizarre joke during the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner.

The 80-year-old president went after Collins, a frequent target of his wrath, during his speech at the Correspondents’ Dinner, which was rescheduled for Friday after a shooting disrupted the original April event.

Trump congratulated Collins for winning the 2026 WHCA award for broadcast for her coverage of Trump’s contentious meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in February 2025, saying that she “shouldn’t get the award. It was a fake, but I didn’t mind.”

He then compared Collins with Mulvaney, who drew national headlines after her 2023 campaign with Bud Light prompted a conservative boycott of the beer brand.

“She never smiles,” Trump said of Collins during his speech Friday. “I said, ‘Kaitlin, do you ever smile?’ Smile. You have a nice position. You’re at CNN fake news. You should be a happy person. So smile, Kaitlan. Just smile.”

President Donald Trump shared the bizarre, seemingly AI-edited image of Collins’ face plastered on top of Mulvaney’s body, on Truth Social Sunday ( @realDonaldTrump/Truth Social )

Trump continued, saying that he thought Collins had “made it big with a major new sponsorship, but then I informed her that it wasn’t her on the Bud Light can, it was Dylan Mulvaney.”

The president appeared to compare Collins with Mulvaney again on Sunday, sharing a seemingly AI-generated image featuring Collins’ face on Mulvaney’s body. The original image was of Mulvaney during her partnership with Bud Light in 2023, and was widely circulated online at the time during the backlash.

This is a breaking news story, check back for updates...

News.title: Norris cashes in on Piastri collision to claim victory at Hungarian Grand Prix
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix from the Hungaroring. This is the 40th anniversary of the race at this track and the 41st edition. I think over the years this track has had a bit of an unfair reputation but we have certainly had some interesting and exciting races over the years. Even over the last few years.

The nature of the track means it is a bit of an outlier. And that means you often get results that go away from the norm of the season. Mercedes took a couple of poles here in the ground-effect era whilst Charles Leclerc did so last year. We have had a handful of first-time winners at this track, too: Damon Hill, Fernando Alonso, Esteban Ocon, Jenson Button and… errr Heikki Kovalainen.

So far that has been true this weekend. Although McLaren and Ferrari have been closing in on Mercedes, the SIlver Arrows have usually had the edge or found it when it comes to qualifying. That was not the case yesterday: Lando Norris took the first non-Mercedes grand prix pole of the season, pipping the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012sec.

Hamilton, though, takes a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in Q3. Kimi Antonelli, who had qualified fourth, takes the same penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. It was Ferrari who had been expected to be the team to beat but they were the team that dropped the ball. In fairness Norris, in the upgraded McLaren had looked competitive throughout qualifying and was simply able to deliver when Ferrari could not.

The grid is slightly mixed up because of the penalties. George Russell’s season did not get any easier after qualifying seventh but he at least moves up because of those grid drops. The Mercedes’ race pace is expected to be strong but will it be enough to put them into contention with the McLarens and the Ferraris? And let’s not forget Max Verstappen in fourth, either…

We find out at 2pm BST, when the race gets under way.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

News.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after settling for bronze
News.content:
Afterwards, Ramsay-Peaty, whose alleged dispute with his own family became a major distraction during his marriage earlier this year, was visibly emotional as he criticised the media which he insisted had written “rubbish” about his personal life.

“I know the s--- I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, to be honest,” said Ramsay-Peaty, who lost his 100m breaststroke crown two years ago at the Paris Olympics. “But it does take a toll. The choices I’ve made over the last few months have been hard ones. But I’m happy at the same time that I can get here. I didn’t quit in Paris, but I deserve more.”

He added: “You don’t know who I am and people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror,” Ramsay-Peaty told a group of reporters.

“You can’t hurt me. For me, it’s about my family and that does come at a cost. Being able to ignore that and being able to focus on my job – that hasn’t played a part in a sense of what we’re experiencing today.

“I’m still happy with that result. There’s some sense, but it has to, it has to stop. You know, look how many, how many athletes, how many people have to go for this until the media learn [a] lesson?”

Referencing Nowacki, the 18-year-old sensation from Jersey who has long been regarded as Ramsay-Peaty’s breaststroke successor, he added; “You have to learn and do better. You know, and for me, you know, I don’t want a young Filip one day to go through something like that, or these younger athletes.

“For me, that’s part of what I have to go through. I’ve got no control over that. But I think enough is enough. This is away from sport – it’s just about being decent people.”

After receiving his bronze medal, Ramsay-Peaty approached his wife, with whom he is expecting a child in December, and kissed her baby bump.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton hit with penalty in blow to Hungarian GP hopes
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s hopes of significantly denting Kimi Antonelli’s championship lead were dealt a blow after he was given a three-place grid penalty for Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Hamilton looked to be the man to beat heading into qualifying at the Hungaroring and was on course for a record 10th pole position here before a messy final few minutes cost him.

Ferrari were well placed to end Mercedes’s run of having taken pole position for every grand prix this season. Instead, defending champion Lando Norris snuck in and took a superb pole for McLaren with a lap of 1min 17.207sec.

A poor final lap from Hamilton was compounded by a grid penalty for impeding the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, meaning the seven-time world champion will start fifth for the race at one of his most favoured circuits. The only consolation was that Antonelli was also given a three-place grid penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. The Italian will start seventh while Charles Leclerc, Hamilton’s team-mate, will be alongside Norris on the front row.

Heading into the final runs in Q3, Hamilton was 0.101sec ahead of Norris, but did not improve his time. Yet Norris, who was fastest in Q1 and Q2, and was the last of the top three across the line in Q3, had no problem, beating Hamilton’s time by 0.012sec.

Hamilton was critical of his Ferrari team for sending him out first, a decision he said “shocked” him.

“I don’t know why we went first, that was a bit of a shock to me and I definitely wouldn’t have chosen to go first,” Hamilton said. “I had a clean out-lap and when I started my lap and already in turn one I had a snap [of oversteer], I was already a tenth down. The last lap was the worst lap of all... we clearly had the car to be on pole.”

Worse was on the way for Hamilton. The stewards later confirmed the three-place grid penalty to add to the disappointment of missing out on pole.

Replays showed a frustrated Piastri gesturing to Hamilton for blocking him at turn one, ruining the Australian’s final flying lap. Hamilton said he was unaware that Piastri was there, which was proved by video evidence that showed how much he impeded the McLaren. It would have been an easy decision for the stewards to make.

News.title: ‘Always in bloom, a visit really makes one’s day’: Your favourite garden centres
News.content:
Bryan, 86, from the South East, has been a customer of Henry Street Garden Centre in Arborfield, Berkshire for decades: “My wife and I often used to browse and purchase plants and garden furniture.”

But his favourite memory was watching his wife’s “delight at their incredible Christmas displays of decorations. Lights, live reindeer even and the wonderful family atmosphere all around you,” he describes. “It’s still a magical place for me where I can get close to her memory.”

For Mary, 79, from the South East, “a garden centre is special if the plants are in season and healthy and there is great choice of both plants and compost”. She nominates family-run Grovewell Garden Centres at Swingfield near Folkestone, which has three other branches based in Kent.

Not only are their plants “always beautifully displayed”, she explains, they have “an amazing choice of garden supplies, cards and gifts, as well as a nice little coffee shop”. Her favourite memory, however, was at Christmas time a few years ago. “They have a couple of beautiful, nodding and interacting reindeer with a sofa in front of them. We were admiring them and an older guy on the staff asked if we wanted a photo taken, which was so sweet of him.”

“He took my husband’s phone and got a really happy little snap of us and the reindeer, which our girls thought was hilarious,” she says. “Service with a smile.”

Community spirit

News.content:
Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. News.title: How to choose a sports bra, with advice from a netball player, bra fitter and scientist
News.content:
How do you tell if a sports bra is the wrong size?

One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make is assuming that if a sports bra feels tight, that’s enough. In reality, support comes from the right fit rather than simply compressing your chest.

Cardwell advises thoroughly testing a sports bra by moving in it in the same way as you will during the sport you will be doing. “Your breasts don’t just move up and down,” she says. “They move all around – circles, up, down, left, right. We want to try and restrict that as much as possible, but not to the extreme where you’re not able to breathe.”

What is a high impact sports bra?

High-impact sports bras are designed for activities where your breasts experience the greatest movement, such as running, HIIT, tennis and netball. Their job is to minimise breast movement in every direction, helping reduce discomfort while allowing you to move more efficiently.

To measure how high-impact a sports bra is, Wakefield-Scurr asks women to run in a laboratory, both without a bra and while wearing different sports bras. “For a bra to be classed as high support, it has to reduce breast movement above certain thresholds,” she says. “If your breasts move 10 centimetres without a bra and five centimetres in a sports bra, that bra has reduced breast movement by 50 per cent.”

In the lab, Wakefield-Scurr and her team found that “if you run in low support compared with high support, you reduce your stride length by four centimetres. Four centimetres might not sound like a lot, but over the course of a marathon, those four centimetres add up to around a mile.” This proves that wearing a high-support bra doesn’t just keep you comfortable, but it can improve your athletic performance.

Cardwell, who wears a double G cup, says high-impact support has improved dramatically in recent years. “There has been a lot more research into high-impact sports bras, especially for larger-chested women.” She also warns against assuming that every sports bra offers the same level of support. “If it’s the same material as a smaller cup size, it’s probably not going to be sufficient for someone like me with double Gs.”

How often should you replace your sports bra?

There’s no set rule for replacing a sports bra, according to Wakefield-Scurr. This is because its lifespan depends more on how you care for it than how often you wear it. “The lifespan of a sports bra is affected more by how you wash and dry it than by how often you wear it,” she says. In one of her team’s studies, support dropped by around a third after 25 washes. “Always follow the washing instructions,” she advises. “You’d be surprised how many sports bras should be hand washed or washed at a lower temperature.”

Looking after your sports bra properly will help it last longer, but no bra lasts forever. Once the underband loses its elasticity or the support noticeably decreases, it’s time to replace it to ensure you have the right level of support.

Sports.title: How Man Utd can have perfect transfer window with three more signings and Marcus Rashford leading exits
Sports.content:
ENGLAND’S 6-4 win against France last week was paradoxical: a game so entertaining it provided more proof that the World Cup third-place match should be scrapped.

Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee scored a goal akin to Jude Bellingham’s against Rosenborg by embarking on a sprint, dummying a Rosenborg defender and then the goalkeeper before rolling the ball in.



No right-minded United fan would now be clamouring for Zirkzee to be kept on the strength of the goal. Zirkzee barely celebrated his fine solo effort as he knew how insignificant it was.

Five-a-side games on 5G pitches would be more intense than United’s 5-0 thrashing of Rosenborg. That game, and the 1-0 loss to Wrexham in Helsinki, will be cause to reassess future pre-season schedules.



Steep ticket prices for an underwhelming fixture with World Cup participants still absent resulted in a half-empty crowd in Trondheim on Friday. United visited the Norwegian city two years ago, too.

The club’s first visit to Helsinki in 61 years against Wrexham did not draw out a bumper crowd, either. A little over 20,000 fans clicked through the turnstiles.



United are playing one more pre-season game than last year when they had a full squad available. The sole reason for that is money but supporters are not going to pay through the nose en masse to watch Zirkzee.

Ideally, United would jettison Zirkzee and bring in a replacement. But while Benjamin Sesko is building up his fitness and United wait for their World Cup internationals to return, Zirkzee is needed.

United are three signings short but if the transfer window was to suddenly close tomorrow they could argue that they have an adequately-sized squad.

Three goalkeepers, two right backs, two left backs, five centre backs, four central midfielders, two left wingers, two right wingers, a playmaker and two strikers. That 23-man list excludes Marcus Rashford and Manuel Ugarte.



Add three more recruits, shift Rashford and Zirkzee, and a 25-man list is a more complete number of senior players for a season back in the Champions League.

The Red Devils have been strongly linked with a move for Aurelien Tchouameni with Real Madrid looking to raise money to sign Rodri.

Whoever the manager or coach is, United’s squad management is constructed with academy talents in mind. Four of them scored in Trondheim and two have merit in Carrick’s core squad.

Harry Amass is one of the two aforementioned left backs. The 19-year-old has not played since a hamstring injury ended his 2025-26 campaign in January but he had impressed in the Championship and is champing at the bit for more opportunities.

Amass had his issues with Ruben Amorim but Amorim also gave him his full debut against Wolves. Amass offered more than anyone in a red shirt in that 1-0 defeat in April 2025.



The United academy lads loaned to the Championship are the ones the club feel have a chance of returning to the first team. The second half of Amass’s 2025-26 season was a write-off but he is the right choice to compete with Luke Shaw on the left.

Shea Lacey, another left-footer, opened the scoring in Norway and has spent most of the past year with the United squad. He looked lively in his four first-team cameos.

Lacey, 19, is behind Bryan Mbeumo and Amad in the right-wing pecking order but he has earned a permanent promotion to senior squad member status. His direct dribbling threatened an equaliser at Aston Villa last December and he smacked the woodwork within seconds of his introduction at Burnley in January.

Ethan Williams and Jacob Devaney were both on the scoresheet against Rosenborg. The pair were on loan at Scottish Premiership sides Falkirk and St Mirren last season.



The prospect that they could make the leap to the Premier League is about as fanciful as Scotland ever emerging from a World Cup group.

Not that long ago, Scotland had become a graveyard for United academy misfits. Matty Willock, Demetri Mitchell, James Wilson and Charlie Scott headed across the border to St Johnstone, Hearts, Aberdeen and Hamilton Academical in one calendar year alone.

United youngsters do not struggle for cheerleaders these days. Coverage of the academy has increased in recent years – an undeniable positive – and the social media crowd fuels and falsifies many players’ actual ability.

Emerging young players’ parents are also at an age where social media has long been the norm for them, so there are instances of very public parental campaigning.



Williams scored against Bournemouth in Chicago on tour with United last year, having fared well during four months on loan at Cheltenham in League Two. Devaney, a Barnsley-born Republic of Ireland Under 21 international, seems ready for a Football League loan.

They will have to enjoy this while it lasts. Come United’s training camp in Dublin in two weeks, Carrick will not be accommodating a plethora of academy professionals on the plane as he did in Trondheim and Helsinki.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Some will be allocated a boarding pass. Amass and Lacey should be while midfielder Jim Thwaites was in Ireland for the April camp.

United play Leeds at Croke Park in the middle of their training week. That may be more competitive than England-France.

Sports.title: DAZN presenter Diletta Leotta shows off curves in barely-there bikini as fans say ‘beautiful, beautiful, beautiful’
Sports.content:
DAZN presenter and footie Wag Diletta Leotta has stunned in a tiny bikini on holiday.

The Italian has been chilling after her World Cup work and left fans amazed at her body.

Diletta, the mother to former Liverpool goalkeeper Loris Karius‘ kids, also put up pics from their vacation.



In one she is sunbathing and another has her mid-workout by the water in a revealing sports bra.

Blonde TV ace Diletta also took a window selfie in her swimwear and heels.

She was snapped taking a dip in an ice bath and also dressing up for days out.

The social media star has over 9.4million followers on Insta and some of her fans were in awe.



One wrote: “Bella bella bella (beautiful beautiful beautiful)”.

She was caught taking a bite of pizza in another.

Sports.title: Man Utd make Shea Lacey transfer decision after winger, 19, nets in Rosenborg friendly
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED plan to keep Shea Lacey in their first team squad for the first half of the season.

Lacey, 19, scored the opening goal in United’s 5-0 thrashing of Rosenborg on Friday to underline his first-team credentials.



The winger made his debut last December and Lacey has made three more appearances, with his only one under Michael Carrick coming on the final day of last season at Brighton.

Sources say Carrick wants to keep Lacey in his squad until the January transfer window, at the earliest.



United and Lacey’s advisers are prepared to reassess his situation in the new year to decide whether he remains at the club or heads out on loan for the first time.

Lacey is under contract at United until 2029 and has enjoyed an encouraging 12 months after numerous injury problems at academy level.



The Scouser’s inclusion at the expense of Jack Fletcher was the sole change to the United side against Rosenborg in Norway and Lacey scored the only goal of the first half.

The teenager had impressive impacts off the bench in his first two games for United in the winter at Aston Villa and Burnley, where he hit the woodwork within seconds of coming on.

Lacey was sent off in the 2-1 FA Cup third round defeat to Brighton in January and he had to wait four more months for more minutes.

His 62nd-minute introduction at the Amex Stadium marked Lacey’s longest outing for the United first team.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

United already have Bryan Mbeumo and Amad ahead of Lacey on the right-hand side but Carrick has often used Mbeumo up front.

Lacey is also an out-and-out winger and United’s two main choices on the left under Carrick – Matheus Cunha and Patrick Dorgu – are a playmaker and full back by trade.

Sports.title: Dean Henderson holidays with bikini-clad wife Millie in Mykonos as goalkeeper sends message to England pals
Sports.content:
DEAN HENDERSON and his wife Millie have taken to Mykonos in Greece for their holidays after the World Cup.

And he had a fun message for his former team-mates while on his travels, too.



While Henderson sat with his bikini-clad wife in one picture, he also did the Jesse Lingard celebration – making a J and an L with his fingers – on one slide.

Of course, he was team-mates with Lingard at Manchester United and for a season at Nottingham Forest.





Lingard also commented on the post with a love heart and a fingers crossed emoji.

He also did the fake John Stones injury that duped boss Thomas Tuchel at the World Cup.

The free agent defender pretended to have a hurt shoulder in the changing room after England‘s triumph over Mexico, but when his manager came to check on him, he started pumping his arm and dancing.

The other picture was a close up selfie of his wife Millie, whom he married in 2022.



Their ceremony took place in Rome’s Villa Miani hotel, which included a performance from Lewis Capaldi.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The pair have two children together, but Millie is a very private person with no social media accounts.

She travelled to support Henderson throughout Euro 2024 and did the same this summer.

When the goalkeeper made his first start for England away to Finaldn in 2024 on short notice, he found a private jet so Millie and his family could watch the game.



Henderson did see some action in North America this summer. The Crystal Palace goalkeeper was in the sticks for England’s Bronze medal winning game against France, which they won 6-4.

The only players who failed to see any action during the World Cup were James Trafford and Kobbie Mainoo.

Sports.title: Unemployed Jadon Sancho, 26, receives ‘game-changing’ free transfer offer after finally ending Man Utd hell
Sports.content:
JADON SANCHO could be set to receive a career lifeline just weeks after becoming unemployed.

The 26-year-old former Borussia Dortmund phenom became a free agent after the expiry of his Manchester United contract earlier this month.



And after lacklustre loan spells with Chelsea and Aston Villa, it seemed uncertain how long the winger would have to wait before a club decided to make a swoop for him.

But now FootMercato claim he has received an offer from Qatar.



They say Al-Rayyan have offered him a contract to try and kickstart his career in the middle east.

The outfit also employ former Fulham star Aleksandar Mitrovic up front.

They most recently drew 3-3 with League Two side Rochdale in a preseason friendly last week.

Sancho, a Manchester City academy graduate, has experienced a turbulent few years since making his return from Germany.

The then-teenager lit up the Bundesliga during his time at the club, scoring 54 goals and creating 45 assists in 188 matches.

The return cemented him as one of the greatest young prospects in the game, and earned him a £73million move to United in 2021.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

But things did not go as planned for the star, who failed to have the same level of impact in the English game.

He proceeded to head out on a number of loans, including one back with Borussia Dortmund.

But after failing to earn a spot in Michael Carrick‘s plans or stiff enough interest from a suitor, he now finds himself scrambling for a new home.

A change of scenery, and level in Al Rayyan’s case, could do the star good – though it was reported earlier in the year that he was holding out hope for a move to a top European side even if that meant taking a pay cut.

Sports.title: English World Cup wag shows off gifts from Lionel Messi including personalised handbag and golden mate tea set
Sports.content:
LIONEL MESSI got the entire Argentina World Cup squad a set of presents – and one Wag has shown them off.

Kelci-Rose Bowers, Marcos Senesi’s girlfriend, revealed the gifts from footie’s Goat and took fans through his flashy spending spree.



Posting on TikTok, she opened up a caramel coloured bag with her partner’s name on.

The Argentina badge and World Cup logo are also on the front along with a light blue zip and a set of straps.



She explains: “This is a personalised bag that Marcos got from the camp.”

It is for mate, a popular South American drink, and Messi didn’t stop there.

He also included a GOLDEN Stanley cup with his own logo on.

With a screwable cap also acting as a container, there was a separate bigger cup for the drink as well.



Bowers, who met Senesi at Bournemouth during her three years there as a player for the women’s team, has been told to look after the bag and set.

Sat on a bed with her blonde hair tied up whilst wearing an Argentina top and pink trousers, Bowers added: “Marcos gave me it to keep safe and take back to Miami.”

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

She was also given some herbs and a mate straw (bombilla) if she wanted to try it out.

Bowers described it as a “pretty cool gift” and said it was “pretty cool that I’ve got it.”



Messi and Argentina were beaten finalists in America as things ended in tears.

They were edged out by Spain in New York after extra-time – but barely laid a glove on their opponents.

Messi was crying on the pitch at the end as his dream of back-to-back World Cup titles ended in fighting between the sides.

Bowers, despite being English and a junior Lionesses international, was cheering on Senesi and Argentina throughout.

Sports.title: ‘This may look a strange decision’ – York City SACK manager Stuart Maynard despite promotion to EFL with 108 points
Sports.content:
YORK CITY have confirmed the exit of manager Stuart Maynard just months after he guided the club back into the English Football League after a decade away.

York won the National League in dramatic circumstances in April, scoring an equaliser in the 103rd minute to draw with title rivals Rochdale – who would have been champions themselves had they won.



But Maynard won’t get to see the fruits of his labour. The club says they had a “difference in direction and vision for the football club,” with Maynard.

A club statement read: “York City Football Club can confirm that Stuart Maynard will be leaving his role as First Team Manager, with immediate effect.



“This has not been an easy decision, and it is not one the board has taken lightly.

“Ultimately, it comes down to a difference in direction and vision for the football club. We recognise that, from the outside, this may look like a strange or difficult decision to understand.



“But we believe that in the long term, the football club will be in a stronger position because of it, another step towards the vision we, as custodians of this club, believe will deliver sustained success.

“Like every one of you, we love this football club, and we would never make a decision we didn’t believe was in its best long-term interests. We hope our track record of improving year on year has earned us a degree of trust, and we understand that not everyone will agree with, or fully understand, this decision right away.

“We would like to thank Stuart for his contribution to York City FC and wish him well for the future.”

The club have not left themselves long to figure things out.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

York host Crawley Town in a Carabao Cup preliminary-round tie on Monday, 3 August and their first League Two arrives 12 days later against Bristol Rovers.

Maynard, who had a semi-professional playing career scattered around the south-east that finished with Hemel Hempstead Town, had been at the club for just one solitary season.

Prior to that, he had fallen short with Notts County in the League Two playoffs during an 18-month spell in charge following good work during his three years in the Wealdstone hot seat; his first post.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick meets Ole Gunnar Solskjaer after beating Man Utd legend to manager's job
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick meets Ole Gunnar Solskjaer after beating Man Utd legend to manager's job

Michael Carrick is currently in the midst of preparations for his first full season as Manchester United boss and has been reunited with another former Red Devils manager

View 2 Images Michael Carrick served as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's assistant at Old Trafford (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick was reunited with Ole Gunnar Solksjaer in Norway this week, just months after beating him to the manager’s job at Old Trafford. The Premier League side have been in Norway over the past few days as part of their pre-season preparations.

‌



The Red Devils took on Rosenborg on Friday and secured a 5-0 success, with Shea Lacey, Joshua Zirkzee, Jacob Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams all finding the net.

‌



Away from taking on the Norwegians, United boss Carrick also had more on his mind. As per the Manchester Evening News, he met up with former head coach Solskjaer.

‌



The pair are thought to have a close relationship, despite Carrick having beaten the former forward to the top job at Old Trafford last season. It was suggested that Solskjaer was in talks regarding a second stint in charge.

But Red Devils chiefs opted for Carrick instead and he was handed the job on a permanent basis after 12 wins from 17 games - form that was good enough to see United seal a spot back in the Champions League.

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Carrick’s reunion with Solskjaer comes after he admitted that he had sought after advice from the Norwegian ahead of officially taking the reins at Old Trafford.

‌



Speaking earlier this year, he said: “Yeah, yeah I’ve spoken to him. We’re close, we’ve been through a lot together. He’s been fully supportive, as you’d expect. He’s some man, I respect him an awful lot. He wished us all the best, and he was happy that we got the right result.

“I think, friendships, you have conversations… I’ve got a lot of friends in places that I can pick on if I need to. I’m not that one that bothers a lot of people to be honest, but… He’s certainly there if ever I need.”

Speaking after United’s emphatic victory against Rosenborg, Carrick said: “Clean sheet, scoring goals, and everyone, by the looks of it, coming through injury-free is what you want at this stage, really.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick has met with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer during United's time in Norway (Image: Getty Images)

“As much as we want everything to improve and performances to be better all the time, I think keeping players fit and progressing through pre-season is as important as anything.

“So, two games in, two weeks in, I think we can take where we are and we’re pretty happy. The second half, the younger players coming on, I thought they were fantastic. They played as a team really well and deserve what they got second half.”

‌



He added: “It’s important to build through this pre-season, some players need more minutes than others as they go and we’re managing some players a little bit more than others. I've said it before the game, it's never going to be perfect, two weeks in and you're kind of building towards that.

“So, I thought there was a lot of good things, some of the goals were fantastic goals and it’s just as pleasing to keep a clean sheet. So yeah, we’re moving forward nicely.”

Sports.title: Arsenal's two conditions for Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Gunners set to make next move
Sports.content:
Arsenal's two conditions for Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Gunners set to make next move

Arsenal are reportedly set to hold further talks with Newcastle United over a deal to sign Bruno Guimaraes

View 2 Images Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes has been linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

Arsenal are reportedly about to move a step closer to securing the signing of Newcastle United star Bruno Guimaraes. The Brazil international has been heavily linked with a move away from St James’ Park, with the Gunners mentioned as the most likely destination.

‌



The 28-year-old remains under contract at Newcastle until the summer of 2028, and there has been speculation for several weeks that Arsenal could make an official bid to try and bring Guimaraes to the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Midfield has been an area of the squad that Arsenal are looking to bring in reinforcements this summer, and now there has been a fresh update on their pursuit of Guimaraes.

‌



Transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano has revealed that Arsenal are expected to make an offer exceeding £70million in an attempt to sign Guimaraes in the coming weeks.

Arsenal learn fee and transfer conditions to sign Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid READ MORE :

The report suggests that the Gunners will conduct further negotiations with Newcastle regarding a prospective agreement for the Brazilian within the next few days, with Arsenal already understood to have reached personal terms with the player.

It has additionally been stated that the resolution surrounding whether or not Guimaraes becomes an Arsenal player will hinge on whether or not Newcastle will approve a departure, alongside what valuation they would place on the player.

‌



The development follows reports that surfaced on social media claiming that Arsenal had lodged a bid exceeding £80m in an effort to secure Guimaraes' services.

However, ChronicleLive has reported that no such offer was submitted by Arsenal, with it also emerging that the Gunners would be unwilling to meet an £80m asking price to prise Guimaraes away from Tyneside.

Sports.title: Liverpool identify Bradley Barcola transfer alternative as ‘contact made’ with agent
Sports.content:
Liverpool identify Bradley Barcola transfer alternative as ‘contact made’ with agent

Liverpool are among the clubs linked with Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola as they attempt to find a replacement for Mo Salah but a deal could be very costly, forcing the Reds to look elsewhere

View 2 Images Liverpool have been told to pay £140m for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool are looking at Juventus star Francisco Conceicao as an alternative to Bradley Barcola, who could cost as much as £140million. The Reds are keen to add to their wide options this summer following Mohamed Salah’s exit a year before the end of his contract.

‌



Liverpool completed a deal for Spanish wideman Victor Munoz for £34.5m last month, albeit they still want to sign another forward. Bayern Munich’s Michael Olise has been linked, albeit the German giants are not keen on selling.

‌



Leipzig’s Yan Diomande was also an option but he now appears set for a move to Real Madrid. Paris Saint-Germain’s Barcola has also emerged as a priority target, but the French club’s £140m price tag is putting the Merseysiders off.

‌



That has forced Liverpool to look elsewhere. According to reports in Italy, Juventus’ Conceicao is seen as a cheaper option and they have already got in touch with his representatives regarding a deal.

Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

As it stands, Juventus are not keen on selling, having only spent £27.3m to sign him permanently last summer following an initial loan move from Porto. But it is thought that an offer in the region of around €50m (£42.6m) could be enough to seal his services.

It is not the first time that Liverpool have been linked with a swoop for Conceicao. His name was also mentioned during last season but the Portuguese international remained tight-lipped on his future.

‌



He said: “I know people talk about a big club, but I play for a big club where I am happy. At the moment I am only focused on these two games with the national team and then I will focus on the final stretch of the season to help my club as much as possible.”

View 2 Images Francisco Conceicao has been linked with Juventus on a number of occasions (Image: Getty Images)

“I am at a big club where the pressure to win is very high. I just have to keep working and contribute with goals and assists.

‌



“My objective is to help with goals and assists, that is what I try to do. I must continue every day to show that I have the ability to help the national team and be helped by them to keep improving.”

Conceicao, 23, has made 82 appearances for Juventus in all and has scored 11 goals in all competitions. His contract with the Italian giants is set to run until the summer of 2030.

Sports.title: Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star
Sports.content:
With the Premier League on course to smash its spending record, it's worth reminding them that you don't always have to splash out on signings. Sometimes the best transfers cost nothing - well, bar a hefty a signing-on bonus.

From Ruud Gullit to Chelsea and Sol Campbell to Arsenal, to James Milner to Liverpool and Zlatan Ibrahimovic to Manchester United, the Premier League has seen its fair share of excellent free transfers down the years.

So who could be next? There are plenty of stars from around the world who find themselves without a club, some of them more familiar to English sides than others.

As the final month of the summer transfer window nears, let's build an XI of free agents.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

Goalkeeper: Stefan Ortega

Perhaps the least stacked position in this team, former Manchester City and Nottingham Forest star Stefan Ortega looks the standout goalkeeper available on a free. Ex-Brighton shot-stopper Matthew Ryan is another looking for his next move, while former Aston Villa man Orjan Nyland will hope that his World Cup performances convince someone to come knocking.

Right-back: Dani Carvajal

Arguably the best right-back of his generation, Dani Carvajal left Real Madrid this summer after two spells covering 23 years in which he won 27 major trophies. The Spaniard has reportedly received proposals from the Saudi Pro League, Major League Soccer and Inter Milan, but he remains out of work.

Centre-back: John Stones

John Stones was a somewhat surprise inclusion in the England squad after making just 38 appearances in his final two seasons with Manchester City, but he ended up starting both the quarter-finals and semi-finals in a show of faith from Thomas Tuchel. His experience and quality on the ball makes him an attractive prospect for clubs willing to take a risk on his dubious fitness, with Chelsea and Arsenal linked.

‌



Which club should sign John Stones? Have your say in the comments section.

View 5 Images John Stones was released by Manchester City (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Centre-back: David Alaba

Another departure from Madrid, David Alaba's last three years have been ravaged by injury, missing a total of 126 games for club and country. The ex-Bayern Munich star still managed to be a starter at the World Cup, so that may well convince another European giant to snap him up.

Left-back: Oleksandr Zinchenko

Two clubs, 12 games and one serious injury - that was the story of Oleksandr Zinchenko's season. Following a disappointing loan spell with Nottingham Forest, Arsenal sold him to Ajax for just £1.3million.

‌



But the Ukrainian was only given a short-term deal before suffering a knee injury which is set to rule him out for well into the new season. Zinchenko has proven himself in the Premier League, but will his rehab put clubs off signing him this summer?

View 5 Images Injury ruined Oleksandr Zinchenko's spell with Ajax before it got going (Image: Roy Lazet/Soccrates/Getty Images)

Centre midfield: Franck Kessie

Franck Kessie knows all about getting a big move on a free transfer. The Ivorian moved to Barcelona after his contract with AC Milan expired in 2022, and he memorably scored the goal that won Xavi Hernandez's side the La Liga title in his one and only season.

Kessie was then sold to Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli, where he spent the past three seasons. But now he's without a club and tipped for a return to Italy with Juventus.

‌



Centre midfield: Leon Goretzka

After eight years and 15 trophies with Bayern Munich, Leon Goretzka is another free agent with serious pedigree to offer. The German went to the World Cup but has been tipped for an immediate return to the United States, with Chicago Fire heavily linked with what would be their second marquee signing of the summer after acquiring Robert Lewandowski.

View 5 Images Leon Goretzka went to the World Cup with Germany (Image: Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images)

Centre midfield: Julian Brandt

Staying in the Bundesliga and Julian Brandt has left Borussia Dortmund. The versatile playmaker is said to have offers from Leeds and Ajax, while Arsenal, Aston Villa and Barcelona have also been linked.

Midfield is where some real bargains are to be had. Other options include Yves Bissouma, Dani Ceballos, Fabinho and Lorenzo Pellegrini.

‌



Right wing: Mo Salah

No doubt the most high-profile name in this team, Mo Salah still hasn't found a new club three months after his departure from Liverpool was announced. For a player of his stature and still impeccably fit at 34 years old, that's a surprise.

But factor in the World Cup and it's understandable that the Egypt captain has had other priorities. Speculation over his next destination has been building in the past fortnight, though, with Sporting Kansas City lining up an ambition move and cash-rich Saudi clubs also keen.

According to reports, his priority to stay in Europe. Could a Premier League club offer him a deal?

View 5 Images Mo Salah has left Liverpool after nine years (Image: Jack Thomas/Getty Images)

‌



Striker: Dusan Vlahovic

When Juventus paid £66m for Dusan Vlahovic in 2022, few doubted that he'd become one of Europe's most prolific No.9s. But fast forward four years and he's without an employer.

Barcelona continue to be linked with the ex-Fiorentina marksman while there's been speculation that Juventus could resume talks over a new contract, having failed to agree on an extension before the end of the season. Watch this space.

Left wing: Jadon Sancho

Finally, a name more than familiar to English fans. Jadon Sancho's deal with Manchester United ran out last month and Aston Villa, who he spent last season on loan with, don't want to sign him permanently.

A return to former club Borussia Dortmund has long been rumoured, having also had a loan spell there in 2024. Sancho is still just 26 and has plenty of magic to offer if he can find the right landing spot this summer.

‌

Sports.title: Liverpool and Arsenal alerted after Bradley Barcola transfer call as PSG seek record fee
Sports.content:
Liverpool and Arsenal alerted after Bradley Barcola transfer call as PSG seek record fee

Liverpool and Arsenal have both been linked with Bradley Barcola, who will be allowed to leave PSG this summer provided his £140m price tag is met

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola's price tag has been set by PSG (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

PSG have slapped a mammoth £140million price tag on Bradley Barcola as it looks increasingly like he will leave the Champions League winners.

‌



The winger has been the subject of interest from the likes of Liverpool and Arsenal this summer but his place at the Parisians is in jeopardy and an exit in expected over the coming months. He's confirmed he won't signed a new deal and PSG want to maximise their profits if he does depart.

‌



Real Madrid and PSG are battling to land RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande, who is also on Liverpool's radar, but a move to Paris would further push Barcola down the pecking order.

‌



His refusal to sign a new deal, even though he's under contract until 2031, has seen PSG willing to see him leave provided their huge price tag is met, reports the Evening Standard.

PSG believe their huge valuation, which would make Barcola their most expensive sale ever, is fair given what they've seen elsewhere in the market. The winger has ultimately helped deliver successive European Cups and is still only 23. The Parisians have watched Morgan Rogers and Elliot Anderson move for £117m and £116m respectively.

Barcola caught the eye with an impressive World Cup campaign as France made it to the semi-finals, scoring three times. Liverpool are thought to be in pole position to sign Barcola with Diomande preferring other destinations and Arsenal looking to prioritise a move for Vinicius Jnr.

‌



Last term he scored 13 times, which came after a year where he found the net 21 times, even though he was not a guaranteed starter under Luis Enrique.

View 2 Images PSG want to land Yan Diomande, which would push Bradley Barcola further down the pecking order (Image: Getty Images)

Last year the PSG boss had to warn off rivals from signing Barcola, insisting he was crucial to his plans. He was utilised throughout last season, but ultimately sits behind the likes of Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in the pecking order.

Article continues below

Liverpool are on the lookout for a man to replace Mohamed Salah, who left after almost a decade at Anfield. They've shown in recent years that they are prepared to spend big on players, but landing Barcola could see them break their own British transfer record.
