Sports.title: Arsenal learn fee and transfer conditions to sign Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Arsenal learn fee and transfer conditions to sign Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid

Real Madrid are reportedly demanding big-money for Vinicius Jr this summer, with Arsenal exploring a move for the Brazilian winger

View 2 Images Arsenal are interested in signing Vinicius Junior (Image: Getty Images)

Real Madrid are reportedly demanding at least €160million (£137m) for Vinicius Junior amid Arsenal's interest. The Gunners are considering a swoop for the winger, with Real Madrid determined to avoid losing the Brazil international on a free transfer when his contract runs out next summer.

‌



The 26-year-old is viewed as an option to strengthen Arsenal's left flank as they seek to cement their position as Premier League champions under Mikel Arteta. The forward notched 22 goals and registered 14 assists in 53 outings for Los Blancos last season - despite the Spanish giants experiencing a disappointing campaign.

‌



And with negotiations over fresh terms at the Santiago Bernabeu having reportedly hit an impasse, it could present an ideal chance for Arteta's side to secure one of the game's premier attacking talents.

‌



Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update READ MORE :

However, Spanish publication SPORT claims that the Gunners will be required to shatter the British transfer record to capture him. Alexander Isak's £125m switch from Newcastle United to Liverpool last summer stands as the current highest sum.

Should Arsenal meet the reported £137m asking price, they would eclipse that record by a minimum of £12m, though Real may demand more. The report in SPORT also indicates that the La Liga club will refuse to enter discussions unless the figure is satisfied.

It's understood that the 15-time Champions League champions wish to establish a sufficiently high threshold to discourage speculative enquiries regarding any transfer, including add-ons tied to performance and silverware secured.

‌



View 2 Images Vinicius Jr only has a year or so left on his contract at Real Madrid (Image: Photo by Alex Pantling - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It's reported that the player and club arranged to convene at the conclusion of July to explore a potential contract extension - with Arsenal certain to monitor developments closely should negotiations falter.

‌



Real manager Jose Mourinho has allegedly made his position clear that he desires Vinicius Jr. to stay at the Spanish capital outfit. The Telegraph reports that Mourinho would oppose the notion of the Brazilian departing the Santiago Bernabeu to finalise a switch to Arteta's side.

However, Real may require raising capital, as reports indicate they are contemplating a £102m pursuit of RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande. Arsenal are also understood to have lodged an enquiry for the Ivorian. Yet if Diomande opts for Real, that could heighten the likelihood of Vinicius Jr. arriving at the Emirates Stadium this summer.

Despite astonishment surrounding a potential acquisition of the Los Blancos star, Arteta has demonstrated an ambition for the club to compete for the world's elite talent.

In 2024, when Kylian Mbappe was poised to depart Paris Saint-Germain upon expiry of his contract, Arteta was direct in his answer when questioned whether Arsenal needed to enter the race for such players. "Exactly," he replied.

Sports.title: Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief
Sports.content:
Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief

Michael Olise's future has been a hot topic throughout the summer transfer window, with Liverpool in the queue of clubs who would like to sign him from Bayern Munich

View 2 Images Michael Olise is a man in demand (Image: Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

Bayern Munich sporting director Christoph Freund has told Liverpool to forget about signing Michael Olise, as he 'will' be playing in Germany again next season. Olise, 24, has been strongly linked with a move to Liverpool amid their search for a wide forward to replace Mo Salah.

Real Madrid are also interested in signing the Frenchman, who was superb at the World Cup. Olise provided seven assists in eight games, building on an outstanding season with Bayern.

The winger racked up 48 goals and assists in 52 games as Vincent Kompany's side ran away with the Bundesliga title and won the DfB Pokal. It's no wonder that Bayern want to keep Olise are reportedly preparing to offer him a bumper new contract.

‌



But as for his immediate future, Freund is relaxed. Asked specifically about Real's interest and claims that Olise is desperate to join Los Blancos, the Bayern chief replied: "This is absolutely not an issue for us.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"We're delighted that Michael is back from his holiday. He'll play an important role for FC Bayern this season, just as he did last season, too."

Freund was speaking after a youthful Bayern side lost 2-1 against third-tier Wehen Wiesbaden in a friendly. Big-name stars such as Olise and Harry Kane are expected to feature later in pre-season.

Last month, it was reported that Real had submitted a £130million bid for Olise. However, the Spanish giants issued a statement saying that there had been no 'direct or indirect' with the 24-year-old.

Should Michael Olise leave Bayern Munich? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Christoph Freund insists that Michael Olise is going nowhere (Image: S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images)

Part of the statement read: "Real Madrid also wishes to highlight the excellent institutional relationship it maintains with Bayern Munich -- with whom it shares a long history of mutual respect, collaboration, and admiration -- and regrets the circulation of speculation which does not reflect reality."

Given Bayern's firm stance, both Liverpool and Real have been forced to identify alternatives to Olise. One of them is RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande, who Real are said to have bid £85m for this week.

Leipzig rejected the offer and are demanding a fee of at least £100m. Liverpool are also looking at Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola and Monaco's Maghnes Akliouche to bolster Andoni Iraola's squad.

Sports.title: Norris wins first race of 2026 as Hamilton suffers more penalty pain
Sports.content:
Lando Norris won his first race of 2026 after an early squabble with McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Pole-sitter Norris lost out to Piastri in a feisty opening lap but eventually used his stronger pace to retake the lead after the second round of pit stops, as Piastri made contact when lapping Williams' Carlos Sainz.

However, Piastri later retired when running in second due to a gearbox issue which caused a late Virtual Safety Car with 14 laps remaining.

Ferrari elected to pit Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc from second and fifth but it turned out to be the wrong call for Hamilton as he sped in the pit lane, so was given a five-second time penalty, and could not overtake Max Verstappen or Kimi Antonelli who both did not pit.

Verstappen hung onto second after a stunning final stint as Antonelli fended Hamilton off on the track to extend his championship lead to 50 points over the Ferrari driver and 59 points to George Russell, who stalled at the start then fought back to seventh.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen shocks Lewis Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Hamilton's penalty demoted him to fifth behind Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc while Red Bull's Isack Hadjar finished sixth.

The seven-time world champion will rue another missed opportunity to challenge for the win as Ferrari did not optimise their strategy and he lost time early on when battling Verstappen, who made a great move on Hamilton into Turn 1.

Racing Bulls duo Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad had a race-long scrap with Audi's Nico Hulkenberg with Lawson coming out on top from Hulkenberg and Lindblad in the final points-paying positions in the last Grand Prix before the four-week summer break.

Hungarian GP Result: Top 10 1) Lando Norris, McLaren



2) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



3) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



5) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



6) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



7) George Russell, Mercedes



8) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



9) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi



10) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls

Norris wins after early team orders dispute

McLaren's big upgrade package for Hungary vaulted them to the front and Norris had been in flying form throughout the weekend.

But, Piastri got a tremendous start and capitalised on a wide moment from Norris at the second turn to take the lead and claim track position on a circuit which is tricky to overtake at.

Norris clearly had more pace in hand but was unable to find a way through and became increasingly frustrated on the radio, asking if he could pit first before the second round of pit stops.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Oscar Piastri take the lead from Lando Norris as George Russell has a race start to forget at Hungaroring in Budapest

The reigning world champion was told he could not, so McLaren pitted Piastri just before half distance of the 70-lap Hungarian Grand Prix while Norris stayed out.

Despite having old tyres, Norris was able to slightly outpace Piastri who got caught out by lapped traffic, including Sainz who did not see the Australian at Turn 2 so the pair made minor contact.

Norris pitted on Lap 40 and came out ahead of his team-mate and went on to dominate the remainder of the race, while Piastri was on course for second, only to suffer a gearbox failure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri has a technical failure and stops out on track in Budapest

"My pace today was probably some of the best pace I've ever had. The car was beautiful to drive and I felt very confident, so a great race," said Norris.

"And to get it back in terms of going long, which is certainly not what I was expecting, but the pace was so good I could always extend the stints, and fresh tyres then always won me the race."

Missed chance for Ferrari and Hamilton?

Having qualified on the front row on a track Ferrari were expected to be strong at, things looked promising for Hamilton at the end of Q3 only for him to be demoted three places for impeding Piastri in qualifying.

Nevertheless, starting fifth, there were still opportunities for Hamilton and he made a strong start on his new softs to move into fourth, crucially ahead of team-mate Leclerc.

He was all over arch-rival Verstappen during the first stint but could not make an overtake, so Ferrari pitted him early to undercut the four-time world champion.

Image: Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton battling at the Hungarian GP (AP Photo/Darko Bandic)

It paid off, only for Verstappen to make a stunning move down the inside at Turn 1 after a blistering out lap so Hamilton was stuck behind the Red Bull driver again.

He pitted for a second time on Lap 30 and was on a charge, effectively in third place behind Norris and Piastri as Red Bull chose to run Verstappen long.

After Piastri's retirement, Hamilton was on course for second and to make inroads into his championship deficit to Antonelli but Ferrari, with hindsight, made the wrong decision to pit the British driver under a late Virtual Safety Car.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Davidson analyses Lewis Hamilton's speeding in the pit lane that handed him a five-second time penalty

Hamilton dropped from second to fourth, just behind Antonelli on a close pit merge but was deemed to speed in the pit lane.

He couldn't find a way by Antonelli and his five-second time penalty for speeding dropped him to fifth on a day Ferrari probably had the pace to at least fight Norris for the win.

Sports.title: Greaves beats Sherrock to claim record third Women's Matchplay crown
Sports.content:
Beau Greaves won the Women's World Matchplay for a record third time with a 6-5 last-leg victory over Fallon Sherrock at the Winter Gardens in Blackpool.

After Sherrock forced the contest the distance, Greaves held her nerve with a crucial 180 before a brilliant 145 left 56 for the title. She coolly pinned double 10 to seal victory once again.

The win adds to Greaves' 2023 and 2024 triumphs in this tournament. It was Sherrock that Greaves met in the 2024 Women's Matchplay final in which Greaves took the spoils in a 6-3 win.

It adds to an already impressive year for 'Beau and Arrow' in which she became the first woman to win a Pro Tour event at Players Championship 11. She also hit a nine-darter on the Tour and became the first woman to qualify for the European Tour.

The win for Greaves consigns Sherrock to runner-up at the Women's Matchplay for a third year in a row, losing to Greaves in 2024 and 2026 plus Lisa Ashton in 2025.

"I'm not one to celebrate but it was relief in the end. Fallon is a great lass and an even better darts player. I knew I had to play well but to hit that last dart was an outpouring of relief," Greaves told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Beau Greaves was delighted to lift the World Matchplay trophy for a third time but says she still has to make improvements before the Grand Slam of Darts and World Championships.

"Just so happy to win. I knew playing the women is a bit different because I play the men now. Chuffed just to get the win.

"I was nervous, but that kind of pressure is a privilege.

"I just love my life. love playing darts. I can't get enough of it. I'm addicted to it in a way and just love my life and even supporting the women's game is a massive thing.

"I love darts and it's good enough for me. My goal is to just play better."

Image: Fallon Sherrock and Beau Greaves came up with big moments in a close final

It was billed as a close and enthralling contest between the two most successful players in women's darts, and it certainly lived up to expectations on the Winter Gardens stage.

Sherrock made the brighter start to the final, breaking throw in the third leg. But, in typical Greaves fashion, she hit back immediately to restore parity at 2-2 before producing a sensational 120 checkout in a 12-dart leg to move ahead.

From there, the contest developed into a gripping nip-and-tuck affair. A tense eighth leg eventually went Greaves' way as she pinned double two to secure a crucial break of throw and move within one leg of the title.

Sherrock, however, refused to go down without a fight. Some superb scoring left her on 36 after just nine darts, and she wrapped up an 11-dart break of throw. She then followed it with a classy 70 checkout on double 16 to force a deciding leg

That was when Greaves found her brilliant best once again with a maximum then silky 145 leaving her 56 for the title. On 56, she took double 10 to ensure the trophy was coming home with her.

Greaves' route to final: Brilliance and a battle!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Beau Greaves made a blistering start to the Women's World Matchplay as she took out 148 and 144

Greaves had to battle hard to make it into the final in a 5-4 nerve-wracking victory over Gemma Hayter.

Greaves got off to slow start and Hayter made sure to capitalise, levelling the game at 2-2 with a break of throw on tops and then finding another crucial break with an 83 checkout on double 16 to take the game to a last-leg decider.

However, just when she needed it, Greaves came through with a massive 104 checkout to book her spot in a third Women's Matchplay final.

Greaves made it through to the semi-finals with a 5-1 victory over Kirsi Viinikainen, starting in imperious fashion with a 148 then 144 checkout to get the contest going.

Sherrock route to the final: One leg dropped!

Ashton's title defence came to an end when she ran into a clinical Sherrock who pulled off a 5-1 win to make her third straight Matchplay final in a row.

Indeed, it was a replay of the 2025 Matchplay final, but this time Greaves was firmly in control. Having dropped just a single leg en route to the final, she sealed her place in the showpiece match by pinning double 16.

Sports.title: Sooryavanshi stars again as India knock England off top spot in T20I rankings
Sports.content:
Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi struck his second fifty in three innings as India sealed a 3-0 T20I sweep of Zimbabwe to knock England off top spot in the rankings.

Sooryavanshi's 81 from 49 balls in Harare featured four sixes and eight fours and followed his maiden half-century for his country - a 19-ball 50 - in Thursday's series opener at the same venue.

The left-hander - who lit up the 2026 IPL with 776 runs in 16 matches for Rajasthan Royals at a remarkable strike-rate of 237.30 - first played senior cricket for India during the recent 4-0 T20 thrashing in England, registering scores of 14, 13 and 15.

Score summary - Zimbabwe vs India, third T20I, Harare India 192-5 from 20 overs (elected to bat): Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (81 off 49 balls), Ishan Kishan (29 off 26), Shreyas Iyer (27 off 18), Rinku Singh (25no off 14); Brad Evans (2-41) Zimbabwe 157-7 from 20 overs (target 193): Ryan Burl (54no off 43), Wesley Madhevere (28 off 25); Mayank Yadav (3-29), Shardul Thakur (2-45) India sweep three-match series 3-0.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sooryavanshi was twice dismissed by Jofra during India's 4-0 T20 drubbing in England, including for 15 in the penultimate match in Bristol

India's heavy defeat in the UK had seen Harry Brook's men overtake them as the No 1 T20I team before they returned to the summit after seizing a 2-0 lead against Zimbabwe.

They would have slipped back to second had they lost the finale but ran out 35-run winners despite some sloppy fielding.

Sooryavanhsi's innings - which ended when he was superbly caught by a diving Brad Evans - propelled Shreyas Iyer's side to 192-5 and Zimbabwe could only make 157-7 in reply, with Ryan Burl (54no off 43) top-scoring.

Image: Sooryavanshi (left) shared half-century stands with Ishan Kishan (right) and India captain Shreyas Iyer on Sunday

India are next in action in August as they visit Sri Lanka for a two-match Test series, before returning to white-ball cricket across September and October when they host West Indies for three one-day internationals and five T20 internationals.

England will look to move back top of the T20I standings when they welcome Sri Lanka for three fixtures from September 15.

The series opener is at the Utilita Bowl in Southampton before further games at Sophia Gardens in Cardiff (September 17) and Emirates Old Trafford in Manchester (September 19) ahead of a three-match ODI series between the sides.

Like India, England also play Test cricket next, with the first of three red-ball clashes against Pakistan starting at Headingley on August 19, live on Sky Sports and contract-free with NOW.

Sports.title: Shin stutters to win in Scotland as players prepare for Women's Open
Sports.content:
Jenny Shin stuttered over the line at the ISPS HANDA Women's Scottish Open to secure her first LPGA Tour title in a decade with England's defending champion Lottie Woad finishing tied-37th as players prepared for next week's AIG Women's Open.

South Korean golfer Shin ended two strokes clear of compatriot A-Lim Kim on nine under par after bogeying two of her final three holes on Sunday to sign for a three-over 75, having begun round four with a five-shot advantage over Thailand's Pajaree Anannarukarn.

The 33-year-old suffered three bogeys in a row from the sixth but her birdies at 10 and 12 proved crucial following her sluggish end to the round as Kim's four-under 68 came in vain at Dundonald Links.

Shin was emotional as she clinched her first trophy since the Volunteers of America Texas Shootout in May 2016 - she is the first woman in 30 years to go a full decade between LPGA Tour wins - and can now switch focus to the major at Royal Lytham and St Annes.

She said: "My first title didn't really feel like a win at the time. I didn't feel like I deserved it. It felt very accidental. But this one definitely feels a lot different, feels like I earned it. I worked hard for it."

Image: Lottie Woad finished tied-37th in her Scottish Open title defence

How did the British and Irish stars fare?

Woad - whose victory in Ayrshire last year was her first as a pro and came a few weeks after she had won the Women's Irish Open as an amateur - closed out her week with a one-over 73 to finish on seven over, with most of the damage done by a six-over 78 on Saturday.

Charley Hull, who started her tournament with a 78, ended up in a share of 44th place on 10 over after shooting 74 on Sunday.

Image: England's Charley Hull finished 10 over for the tournament in Ayrshire

Ireland's Leona Maguire claimed a top-10 finish on one under after a final-round 70 took her into the red, with Alice Hewson, on three over, the highest-placed British golfer in a share of 19th spot.

What about some of the other big names?

Reigning Women's Open champion Miyu Yamashita - who triumphed by two strokes from fellow Japanese Minami Katsu and England's Hull at Royal Porthcawl in 2025 - finished tied-fifth on three under in Scotland ahead of her title defence in Lancashire from Thursday.

Image: World No 1 Nelly Korda has won two majors this year, the Chevron Championship and the US Women's Open

World No 1 Nelly Korda will be aiming for a third major title of the year and fifth of her career after victories at the Chevron Championship and US Women's Open this term.

The American will head to Royal Lytham & St Annes following a finish of tied-16th at the Scottish Open, shooting her best round of the week on Sunday - a three-under 69 - to end on two over par.

This year's other double major winner - Women's PGA and Evian champion Haeran Ryu - did not play at the Scottish Open.

Watch the 2026 AIG Women's Open live on Sky Sports from Thursday to Sunday. Coverage from the opening day begins at 9am on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event. Stream with NOW.

Sports.title: England 'far off their best' in netball defeat to Australia in Glasgow
Sports.content:
England suffered their first defeat of the Commonwealth Games after going down 66-47 to reigning champions Australia in Glasgow.

The Vitality Roses trailed 18-11 after the first quarter and 35-24 at half-time before a series of handling errors helped Australia stretch their lead to 56-35 with 15 minutes left.

England won the final quarter 12-10 but the damage was already done as they were unable to back up their opening 83-34 victory over Northern Ireland on Saturday.

England, for whom Olivia Tchine scored 23 goals, face Malawi on Monday before further Group A games against Tonga on Wednesday and South Africa on Thursday.

The top two sides in Groups A and B after all the sides have played the others in their pool once each will advance to the semi-finals.

Image: Australia are two from two in Glasgow after also beating Tonga on Saturday

Williams says England can take lessons from defeat

The Vitality Roses took Commonwealth Games gold on the Gold Coast in 2018, beating host nation Australia in the final, but did not medal in Birmingham four years ago.

Speaking after Sunday's defeat to Australia's Diamonds, England captain Fran Williams said lessons would be learned: "That's definitely not the result that we came for but it's also not the performance.

"We were far off our best and never really got momentum. It's really tough when a game blows out like that in the second half.

"You've got to make sure that you're still going after those small wins and little fights. That's why I'm so proud of the last 15 minutes in terms of getting a quarter win at the end when it was tough.

"It's great we've had that exposure against a team that's probably setting the standard in the competition. We've got the learning from the experience so we can move on.

"There's no point dwelling on it. It's about taking what we need from it and bringing it into [the Malawi match]. That will help us drop any disappointment. You've got to look forward."

Sports.title: Fury vs Joshua: Everything you need to know
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua both won over the weekend to keep themselves on course for a blockbuster heavyweight showdown – here is everything you need to know about the proposed fight.

Fury and Joshua have shared eras, headlines and negotiating tables without ever sharing a ring. A fight was previously announced for August 2021 in Saudi Arabia and terms were accepted again for a December 2022 date before both collapsed without a punch being thrown.

This weekend's return to the ring for both men is expected to be the final box-ticking exercise before it happens for real this time.

What happened in Fury and AJ's warm-up fights?

Fury claimed a seventh-round TKO over Mariusz Wach at the Max Muay Thai Stadium in Thailand on Friday, with Wach signalling to his corner to wave the fight off before the officials ended it ahead of the eighth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dev Sahni reveals how Tyson Fury toppled Mariusz Wach in a non-TV fight in Thailand

The bout was not televised and fought in front of around 1,500 spectators in Pattaya and was the 37-year-old Fury's second since ending his latest retirement, following his points win over Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April.

Joshua's night in Jeddah was far more dramatic. He was floored inside 20 seconds by Kristian Prenga, hit the canvas twice in the first round, then knocked out the Albanian with right hands in the second.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment Anthony Joshua sealed victory over Kristian Prenga with a huge second round knockout (Courtesy of DAZN)

It was AJ's first outing since he was a passenger in a December car crash that killed his friends Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele and his first fight since stopping Jake Paul last December.

When will the pair fight?

The calendar has been circled for November and the warm-up double-header was arranged to align with that timeline.

Contracts are signed and the pair are now set to meet, though a precise date has not been announced – although Fury said after beating Wach that he hopes the fight is signed "next week".

Where will the fight be?

No venue has been announced.

Turki Alalshikh, who is promoting the fight, has said he wants the fight to suit a global audience and that he will talk to London authorities over a later-than-usual start time.

Sky Sports revealed, though, that Brent Council had not yet been contacted about extending Wembley Stadium's usual 11pm curfew.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has revealed that the USA is now the preferred venue for Alalshikh, but highlighted that the current signed contracts state that the fight must be in the UK.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn hit back at Fury's claims he was worried about a potential bout against AJ falling through

"That doesn't tally up with the contract that we signed," he said. "Until we're happy, we expect every point of that contract to be followed. I feel like this fight should be taking place in the UK.

"If they want to change the contract, then we have to renegotiate the contract. Which, by the way, is not a problem but it's a conversation we have to have."

Wembley has been championed by Barry Hearn, Eddie's dad, while Cardiff's Principality Stadium has been rumoured but Croke Park appears not to be an option despite earlier suggestions of talks about moving the bout to Dublin.

"There's two or three different places it could be but there's still objections to a few of them and the one man who's going to make the decisions is Turki Alalshikh, and Netflix," said Spencer Brown, Fury's manager.

"They're going to make the decisions. They both want the fight, so there's going to be a bit of chopping and changing."

What has AJ said?

"I am going to rip his heart out," Joshua said after beating Prenga. "All jokes aside, I respect everything he has done and achieved but we are here now.

"I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat."

He also dedicated the win on Saturday to his late friends, adding: "It's more than just punch power, it was spirit."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Anthony Joshua dedicates his win over Kristian Prenga to his late friends who died in December's car crash (Courtesy of DAZN)

Joshua has also insisted the contract states the fight must be in the UK.

What has Fury said?

Fury got his shots in after beating Wach and questioned whether Joshua has the "guts" to face him, referencing his rival declining to enter the ring after the Makhmudov fight in front of 70,000 at Tottenham.

"The biggest test of it all is how big his ***** are," said Fury.

"I think he's a big s********. In Tottenham in front of 70,000 people, he never had the guts to get in the ring and face me.

"Let's see if he ever does, I'm not convinced."

Fury then reeled off Vegas, New York, Ireland, London, Belfast and even Pattaya as possible venues.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spencer Brown says Tyson Fury's presence at ringside for Joshua vs Prenga was never discussed and he's not convinced AJ will be in favour of fighting The Gypsy King in New York

That followed his Sky Sports News interview in fight week, where he said "I don't care if I ever see him again in my life" and vowed not to travel to Saudi Arabia for a face-off.

Despite voicing his concerns, Fury did say he hopes the next big fight is signed next week and his management confirmed that they are looking to definitely get it done within the next fortnight.

"When the fight is announced, which we anticipate we will do in the next couple of weeks," said Brown. "There's still a couple of contractual things that we need to get through, i.e. where it's going to be, when it's going to be, how it's going to be, but I've been assured that we'll be sorting it out in the next couple of weeks."

Who is the favourite according to the experts?

Former middleweight world title contender Matthew Macklin believes that the 'Gypsy King' is the clear favourite.

"I think Tyson Fury is favourite," said Macklin. "I think because he's got a style and assets that age better. I think AJ is more athletic but as you get older those athletic qualities diminish.

"I think his punch resistance probably has gone now. Dubois, it was a bad knockout, and he's had that fight against Jake Paul since.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barry Hearn backs Anthony Joshua to beat Tyson Fury when the British rivals finally meet later this year, insisting Wembley Stadium is the ideal venue for fans.

"I don't think his punch resistance will be anywhere near what it once was, and also his reflexes won't be what they were, so it's like a double whammy.

"Fury, his reflexes won't be what they were either so it's not like it's all AJ on the decline. He's not the fighter he was. Neither of them were, but I think we all know that and accept that.

"It's still a level playing field because they're both past their best, so it's still going to be an intriguing battle."

As for Sky Sports Boxing expert and former WBO Cruiserweight champion Johnny Nelson, he said: "There's a word called 'mercurial' and that describes Anthony Joshua.

"He's got so much talent but it's a case of which version of him turns up on performance night.

"The talented fighter we know, he wasn't there [on Saturday]. The guts, the heart, he was there, because after 20 seconds he got put down and had to get back up again. He was still making rookie mistakes. I'm thinking, you shouldn't make those mistakes at this stage in your career.

"Listen, I'm an AJ fan, but I'd have to lean towards Tyson Fury's fluidity, his boxing ability – because of that vulnerability from Anthony Joshua, getting caught by that sneaky little uppercut on the inside, getting caught again.

"These are natural shots from Tyson Fury. When it comes to heart, determination, desire and want, I put that in the corner of Anthony Joshua.

"But on last night's performance and on Friday night's performance, I'd have to lean towards Tyson Fury, from what I've seen."

What next?

The date and venue announcement is the key piece of outstanding information but, given the November window, that confirmation is expected within weeks.

For reference, tickets for Joshua's fight with Dubois went on sale a little under three months before that event.

The plan once both men came through the weekend was a joint press conference to formally announce the fight, though Fury's refusal to share a stage with Joshua makes the shape of that uncertain and there is also the venue conundrum to answer.

Fury expects a signing within days before fans can look forward to what will be one of the most eagerly awaited British boxing matches of all time.

Sports.title: Chiesa wants ‘new chapter’ with Iraola after frustrating time under Slot at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa has said he wants “a new chapter” at Liverpool with Andoni Iraola following a frustrating time under Arne Slot and claimed the club were lucky to qualify for the Champions League last season.

The Liverpool forward has been linked with a return to Italy this summer having struggled for minutes during his two years at Anfield. Chiesa made 36 appearances for Slot last season, a healthy return on paper, but only five were starts.

He started one Premier League game last season despite Liverpool’s problems in attack with injuries to Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitiké, and his last start came in the FA Cup fourth-round win against Brighton on 14 February. A change of head coach, Chiesa hopes, will herald a change in fortune as a Liverpool player.

“It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year,” said the 28-year-old, who produced a fine finish in Liverpool’s 4-2 friendly defeat of Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. “Maybe there have been too many fresh starts [for him]. But I don’t care, I am trying to do my best for this new manager.

“Last season under Arne Slot, I was trying to do my best. Last year I felt ready for a bigger role, then it depended on the coach whether he wanted me to play or not. Of course I wanted to play more but it is what it is. The gaffer had his gameplans, he took his decisions, I have nothing to say about that. It is football. This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that.”

Chiesa admits he has not discussed his future with Iraola since the Basque coach succeeded Slot in June. “The only conversations I had were about pressing and tactics,” he said. “He put me striker against Sunderland and he wants me there.”

But the Italy international, who has two years remaining on his Liverpool contract, claimed his priority is to prove himself to the head coach rather than seek a return to Serie A. Como and former club Juventus have been linked with a move for the forward.

“Right now, at the moment, I am happy here at Liverpool,” said Chiesa. “I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything. I am doing the best I can to have a chance here. And then we will see. At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool.”

View image in fullscreen Federico Chiesa scored for Liverpool against Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. Photograph: George Walker IV/AP

Liverpool secured Champions League qualification on the final day of a troubled season in May in what proved to be Slot’s final game in charge. Chiesa insists that was no cause for celebration at a club of Liverpool’s stature and there must be improvement next term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The forward said: “Liverpool deserves more. Two years ago, we were Premier League champions. Last year, we almost went out of the Champions League spots. We were battling for fifth, which was enough at the time but as we know usually only four go in. We were lucky.

“It was a tough season last year and this season we need to do better, in the Champions League as well. We went out to PSG. We want to go further in that competition and then we want to do even better in the Premier League as well.”

Chiesa also hopes to reclaim his place next season in the national team, now searching for a new head coach having failed to qualify for the World Cup under Gennaro Gattuso, having missed out on several squads recently.

He explained: “The situation is that I spoke to the manager a few times, Gattuso, and I was not ready physically at the time. When I got back in March, unfortunately I got injured. But I am looking forward to playing for the national team. I have won with the national team [the European Championship]. It is always nice to play and win for your national team.”

Sports.title: Régis Le Bris says Chelsea’s pursuit of Sunderland captain Xhaka is ‘closed’
Sports.content:
Régis Le Bris has declared Chelsea’s pursuit of Granit Xhaka “closed” and insisted there is no prospect of Sunderland selling their influential captain this summer.

Xhaka played a major role in Sunderland qualifying for the Europa League on their return to the Premier League last season, prompting Chelsea to make an £8m bid for the 33-year-old this month. Xabi Alonso, the new Chelsea manager, is keen to be reunited with his former midfielder at Bayer Leverkusen.

Sunderland, however, immediately rejected Chelsea’s bid and their head coach has emphatically denied that a deal could be revisited before the end of the transfer window.

“No, this topic is closed,” said Le Bris after Sunderland’s 4-2 pre-season friendly defeat by Liverpool in Nashville on Saturday. “He has been really clear about his future. He loves Sunderland, he wants to stay in Sunderland. He wants to make the future of Sunderland. He is a good captain. Great leader.”

Despite the added demands of European football next season Sunderland have been quiet in the transfer market, signing only the experienced Belgium defender Thomas Meunier on a free from Lille so far. Le Bris anticipates further additions but admits this summer will be nothing like the rebuilding work before Sunderland’s return to the top flight 12 months ago.

The Sunderland head coach added: “It’s going to be quiet. Under the radar, right? I won’t give you information. Because I think we are working hard behind the scenes, and it’s really important to be quiet because otherwise it’s a mess. And we are looking at probably a different transfer window if you compare with last season. We had to sign 14 new players. It won’t be the case this year. We’ll see what will happen.”

Sports.title: ‘We want to win the league’: Arsenal’s new recruits ink in WSL success
Sports.content:
Georgia Stanway looks at her arms and then down at her legs on day one of Arsenal’s pre-season. “As you can see, I’m covered in tattoos,” she says. “I only see the bare skin, the space, so I need to keep collecting more.”

Tattooing and being tattooed is her creative outlet, her way of expressing herself off the pitch. But seeing space is key to the 27‑year‑old England midfielder being exceptional on the pitch.

Stanway’s unveiling video, after her move from Bayern Munich, showed a delicate, cursive script reading “whatever the weather” tattooed on her arm. It was a bold statement to get the lyric from North London Forever, Arsenal’s anthem, etched into her skin before she has stepped on to the Emirates Stadium pitch in red and white. “It shows I’m going to give absolutely everything for this club. I want to hit the ground running, play my game, connect with my teammates, connect with the fans and look forward to an exciting future at the club.”

Stanway is emblematic of Arsenal’s summer of change, one of seven signings so far. Meanwhile, Lotte Wubben-Moy, a lifelong fan who joined Arsenal’s academy at 13, represents the core and culture that is a point of focus at the club. It is a culture players want to be a part of, so much so it leads to getting a tattoo on day one of being there. “She has set a very high bar,” says Wubben-Moy, with a grin. “That’s Georgia. She goes all in and I like that.”

Wubben-Moy is ready to stake a claim in Arsenal’s starting XI after struggling to nail down a position in defence despite having performed exceptionally well when covering for injured players. “I’ve always felt ready,” says the 27-year-old. “When I get my moment, I deliver. Historically, as a club, we’re built on defensive solidity. If we have a solid defence, it allows us to create and score. That should be the stepping stone towards victories. So I will continue to contribute to the defensive solidity in whatever way, shape or form that is. But I want my spot.”

View image in fullscreen Lotte Wubben-Moy lifts the Champions Cup trophy during the Arsenal trophy parade in May. Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

There was widespread recognition that Arsenal’s squad needed a revamp, that the age needed to be lowered and changes made if they were going to take the next step. That meant big names leaving, most notably Beth Mead and Katie McCabe. “They’re both absolute legends of the game and we have so much respect for them,” says Jodie Taylor, the former Arsenal striker who became the club’s technical director in January. “But we always knew this window was going to come with some changes.”

“Change is inevitable in women’s football,” says Wubben-Moy. “If you speak to a player and they don’t say they’re nimble, you’ve got someone that’s not built for the game. We’ve become a nimble team, a team that can move with the ebb and flow of women’s football.

View image in fullscreen Beth Mead left in a busy summer for Arsenal. Photograph: Rhianna Chadwick/PA

“That’s not just within the playing group, it’s something replicated within the staff, the boardroom, the commercial team, the comms team. Everyone is so willing to move and to dictate what we want.

“If you’d asked me about change four or five years ago, I’d have been a bit intimidated, but now I know what to do and I’m part of the driver of it. The opportunity we have and that I see for us as a team, as a collective, is something that really excites me.”

Arsenal’s approach to Stanway’s recruitment was a contributing factor to her wanting to join the club. “Arsenal came in early doors,” she says. “I really enjoyed they were super loyal from the beginning and wanted me even when I wasn’t available. It’s a nice feeling being wanted.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The last four years in Munich were unbelievable, but I knew I wanted to take the next step and I felt at Arsenal there was an opportunity for me to be able to progress, to make my game better and to play with world-class players.”

Arsenal have done most of their business early, with Stanway joined by experienced internationals Selina Cerci, Géraldine Reuteler, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodríguez, as well as young talents Lisa Baum and Isabella Damm. No major international tournament and seven signings in for day one of pre-season is a big boost for Renée Slegers and her coaching staff, particularly after two seasons of slow starts to domestic campaigns.

“The market is not easy, though, it’s constantly changing and the pool of elite talent is small and several clubs are fishing from it,” says Taylor. “You try and plan as much as you can, but you also have to be reactive in the market. We’re always trying to keep an eye on the future, but we have to be quite agile.

“We can talk about positional needs, qualities, ages and succession planning, but if a player’s not available or they just don’t exist, it can be like trying to fit square pegs and round holes. As well as looking at current needs and positional profiles, we talk a lot about our core style of play, but we also want to play with variety, be unpredictable and have different qualities in players too.”

View image in fullscreen Former Arsenal striker Jodie Taylor, now technical director, is leading the strong recruitment this summer. Photograph: Zuma Press/Alamy

The players who have come in have brought energy, says Wubben-Moy, who was on an emotional rollercoaster during Arsenal men’s Premier League and women’s Champions Cup-winning parade, with the bus looping past Highbury Corner, where she filmed her contract renewal video, and past Islington town hall, where she got married to cyclist Tao Geoghegan Hart a few weeks later.

“I like to focus on what they’re entering,” says Wubben-Moy, “which is a culture that has been created by history, by players and staff that are the core of this team and who have all lived through the changes to different degrees: Kelly [Smith], Renée, myself, Leah [Williamson], Kim [Little], Jodie too. We’ve been privy to lots of different things but all of us are holding on to and releasing, in a healthy way, the things we know we need to. It’s efficient, we’re focused, we know what we do next.

“It’s like you’re cooking the most beautiful recipe and then you add the final small ingredients that make the marginal difference, that elevate, and you create something that’s beautiful and that you can relish and enjoy. That’s what we’re in the process of now with a beautiful long pre-season. I’m desperate to get it out of the way so we can then serve what we’re cooking to the fans and be like: ‘Let’s eat and we’ll all eat together for the whole year.’”

The average attendance of more than 34,000 fans for WSL games at the Emirates last season and the club’s pioneering history in women’s football, as well as the Champions League win in 2025, are huge selling points, and all concerned at Arsenal want more, including a first Women’s Super League title since 2019.

“We’re in a great place,” says Taylor. “But we would have liked to have won more trophies last season and that is our huge ambition coming into this year. I’ll flat out say it: we want to win the league. We are an ambitious club and with the signings we’ve made we feel like we’re in a great place to do that.”

Sports.title: How the death of Jayden Adams shook a community: ‘Being on the pitch was his happy place’
Sports.content:
For Jayden Adams, the South Africa midfielder who died this month at the age of 25, football was a “safe space”. Those words, used by Adams’s junior coach Steve Barker at his memorial service 10 days ago, tell you everything you need to know about his life beyond the pitch.

Adams’s battles were bestowed on him almost from birth. Though he was born into newly democratic South Africa, by the early 2000s the revolution was well on its way to being betrayed. The vote was extended to all, but few could make full use of the freedoms available to them because socioeconomic circumstances in the country had barely changed. Stellenbosch, where the Adams family were based, is a perfect example.

Its facade is a tourist dream: a university town nestled among vineyards, Cape Dutch architecture and indie boutiques. Most visitors never venture beyond the town centre or into its suburbs, which are home to the far less privileged and are havens of neglect. Those areas are classic apartheid hangovers, where the wealth has been preserved for a historically advantaged elite and those on the margins, working-class communities of people of colour, are all but invisible.

Ironically, that is how Adams is most often described. He moved in the shadows, both of society and the sport in which he excelled. “Jayden was a guy of very few words. He was quiet, very shy and the smallest among his teammates,” Brendine Johnson, an Adams family spokesperson, says. “Initially, a lot of people missed his football qualities because of his size, but he had a very good fighting spirit. It just wasn’t always on display.”

Adams loved the game dearly and his aunt Monica Thaoge recalled how, as a child, he would kick anything round – “even onions” she said at his memorial. His parents, Juanito and Candice, previously mentioned potatoes as their son’s football of choice. Nobody in the family talks about lacking in financial means because theirs was a community striving to make life better. But there were absences, especially early on.

View image in fullscreen Members of the Mamelodi Sundowns football club carry Jayden Adams’ coffin at the funeral service for the player on Saturday. Photograph: Esa Alexander/Reuters

“Everybody in areas like that is just trying to make ends meet,” says Roger Telemachus, the former South Africa cricketer who grew up on the same street as Adams’s father in Cloetesville. “For the kids, they may not have noticed so much because they were occupied, mostly with playing sport. Some fathers, like Juanito, really encouraged their kids and everyone used to play everything on the street: tennis, football, rugby, cricket. It was also the best way of staying out of trouble.”

Problems were there for everyone to see and, according to Telemachus, have got worse “in the last 20 years”. They include gangsterism, substance abuse and crimes that range from petty to serious. Adams was able to escape from that life when he moved to the slightly more affluent area of Ida’s Valley, but still he did not have a life of luxury. For a period, the family of six, which included four children, lived in a two-bedroom place. At other times, they were with his maternal grandmother, Marianna. “He basically grew up in her yard,” says Johnson.

Things started to change for Adams when he was picked for the Stellenbosch Academy Under-18 side at the age of 15. “The environment was tough, especially if you are not big or tall enough, but when physicality was no longer the most important thing, people saw that Jayden was technically very good,” says Johnson.

His coaches agree. Barker, the nephew of South Africa’s Afcon winning coach, Clive, and the current coach of Simba in Tanzania, gave an emotional assessment of Adams’s skills shortly after his death. “You get many good footballers but you get few great footballers. Jayden was great,” he told Newzroom Afrika.

“Jayden had three attributes that set him apart: an incredible first touch, his weight of pass – I’ve never seen anything like it – and he loved the game so much. Being on the pitch was his happy place. He didn’t pass the ball, he used to caress the ball. He was special and his football intelligence was just outstanding.”

View image in fullscreen Jayden Adams played in South Africa’s World Cup group game against Czechia despite the death of his grandmother the day before. Photograph: Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images

It was under Barker that Adams blossomed. He became the first player from the Stellenbosch Academy to play in South Africa’s top flight, the Premier Soccer League. Five years and an international call up later, the country’s richest club, Mamelodi Sundowns, came calling. This year, at the start of his second season with them, Adams shaved his head, in what he joked was a sign of maturity and called himself a “grootman” (big man). The nickname stuck.

Adams never said it, but he may also have realised how much he had grown up. By then, he had been picked, played for and dropped from the national side after arriving late at a training camp and irking the head coach, Hugo Broos. He had also lost two of his academy teammates, including a close friend.

In February 2023, Oshwin Andries, who was 19, died from stabbing injuries he sustained in Paarl, which is 16km north of Stellenbosch. Three years later, Jeandre Gaffoor, 20, drowned in the Krom River.

When Sundowns won the CAF Champions League in May, Adams dedicated his medal to Andries. To lose so much has weighed on the town, but through Adams they have had reason to celebrate.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Fortnightly Sign up to The Hotspot A new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisis Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Members of Adams’s family, including his father, Juanito (centre left), and mother, Candice (centre right), at his memorial service last week. Photograph: Rodger Bosch/AFP/Getty Images

His role in Sundowns’ continental victory and a call-up to the World Cup squad suggested Adams’s career trajectory was rising. After a first season at Sundowns when he was often playing off the bench and his place in the side was questioned, he had become integral to the team. At Adams’s memorial, the Sundowns senior coach, Steve Komphela, called him “the heart of our team and the heartbeat of our playing style” who “understood the game like a coach and played it as a player”.

In the past year, Adams was playing to the potential people who knew him well had seen years ago and surprising others with his courage and drive to succeed. South Africa’s captain, Ronwen Williams, recalled an incident at this year’s Africa Cup of Nations when the tiny Adams took on a tall Mali opponent with some choice local words. Williams asked Adams if he knew the size of the player he was sledging, but Adams shrugged it off and replied that the Malian wouldn’t understand anyway.

“That was the character he had,” Williams said at the memorial, smiling through his tears as he bade farewell to the teammate he called “my ma se kind” (my mother’s child, a term of endearment used in South Africa).

As his star rose, Adams was careful not to advertise his achievements. “Jayden knew what he had, but he never wanted to voice it. He was very competitive, but he would never brag,” says Johnson. “You get people who are very good verbally on social media. Jayden was not like that. And he wanted to give back. After every game, he would be giving away shirts and boots to kids who asked.”

He also concentrated on providing for his family because he “always promised them he would change their financial situation”.

View image in fullscreen Jayden Adams signs a South Africa shirt for a young Mexican fan who arrived at the team’s World Cup hotel. ‘He wanted to give back.’ Photograph: SAFA

At the World Cup, Adams played for them, even through immense pain. His grandmother Marianna died the day before South Africa’s match against Czechia and Adams opted to remain with the squad. He played that match and appeared in good spirits afterwards and called the 1-1 draw positive, even if he was feeling the opposite way.

He also played the next game against South Korea, which South Africa won to reach the knockouts for the first time. Post-game footage showed him sitting on his own while the rest of the squad celebrated with a signature song and dance.

At the memorial, Komphela offered the Adams family a Bible verse as a comfort, but it may as well be a summary. Psalm 23:4: “Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.”

They will know Adams took that walk many times over his short life and he did not fear. He leaves behind his parents, three siblings, a partner, two children and a community who have gone through what no neighbourhood should. In all that, he has gone from not wanting to be known, to entering the footballing world’s spotlight. A minute’s silence was observed at several World Cup games in Adams’s memory. That is not the way his family would have pictured him coming to global attention, but it has shown them that, in football, he was always far more valued than anyone thought.

“I don’t think the community knew how big he was and how people enjoyed his football,” says Johnson. “It’s a huge shock.”

Sports.title: Inter enter talks with Tottenham over signing captain Cristian Romero
Sports.content:
Inter have entered talks with Tottenham over the potential signing of Cristian Romero. The Spurs captain helped Argentina reach a second straight World Cup final this month, but could leave this summer for a significant fee after an eventful five-year spell.

The centre-back has made 156 appearances since he joined Tottenham in 2021 and guided the club to Europa League success last year, but served four separate suspensions during a difficult 2025-26 campaign.

With Jan Paul van Hecke signed for £52m from Brighton and Marcos Senesi joining as a free agent in June to boost the defensive options of Roberto De Zerbi’s side, Spurs will let Romero depart and his representatives have been in Milan for talks with Inter this weekend.

Inter’s sporting director, Piero Ausilio, told Sky Italy: “It’s definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club. These things take some time but there’s definitely interest. Let’s see.”

Sports.title: Tottenham begin tour with victory over Auckland FC in front of record crowd
Sports.content:
Dane Scarlett and Richarlison were on target as an under-strength Tottenham opened their pre-season tour with an entertaining 2-0 win over the A-League champions, Auckland FC, on Sunday.

Roberto De Zerbi rested most of his top players but the Premier League side dominated a match played in damp conditions. The 40,112 who packed into the All Blacks’ famed rugby ground formed the biggest crowd to watch a men’s football match in New Zealand. It surpassed the previous best of 37,034 for a New Zealand World Cup qualifying match against Peru in 2017. They were treated to a fast-paced contest, even if both sides were missing several of their best players.

Tottenham have embarked on an aggressive summer of spending after narrowly avoiding relegation last season, when they finished 17th. However, the only notable new signing to take the field was the former West Ham midfielder Mateus Fernandes, who scored in the 1-0 win over MK Dons in London on Wednesday.

De Zerbi said he would ease others into the tour, with Tottenham to play games in Sydney next week against the A-League side Sydney FC and their London rivals Chelsea.

“It’s a chance for the young players,” De Zerbi told TVNZ before kick-off, declaring Jan Paul van Hecke, signed from Brighton, and the former Liverpool stalwart Andy Robertson not yet up to speed. “After a very long trip, we can’t take a risk with the players who are not ready to play yet.”

The cecord club signing, Sandro Tonali, was not considered because the former Newcastle midfielder had suffered an unspecified injury – “one small problem” – before the team left London, De Zerbi added.

Fernandes came on with half an hour remaining and Spurs bagged their second goal shortly afterwards through the work of two other substitutes. Mathys Tel burst into the box and set up a tap-in for Richarlison.

Scarlett, one of several Spurs academy players in action, opened the scoring in the 12th minute, pouncing after the Auckland goalkeeper Michael Woud parried Manor Solomon’s shot.

Sports.title: Arsenal make shock approach to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Arsenal are exploring a shock deal to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid. Arsenal have inquired about the Brazil international, who has one year remaining on his contract at the Bernabéu.

It is believed any move for Vinícius – who scored 22 goals for Real last season and four for Brazil at the World Cup – is at a formative stage as Mikel Arteta seeks a marquee signing to build on the club’s first Premier League title in more than two decades.

The 26-year-old Vinícius fits that bill, with Atlético Madrid’s Julián Álvarez, RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain also on their radar.

Arsenal bolstered their attacking options with the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge this week. Morgan Rogers had also been identified as a target, but it is believed Arsenal were not prepared to pay more than £80m for the England international, who has joined Chelsea in a £117m deal – a British record fee.

Vinícius’s future at Real is uncertain after José Mourinho’s return and the club could cash in on the player, rather than risk losing him for nothing in a year’s time.

Mourinho, who has signed a three-year deal at the Bernabéu, was criticised for comments he made after Vinícius accused Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni of racially abusing him during a Champions League tie in February. Mourinho, Benfica manager at the time, said “something happens, always” in matches where Vinícius plays. Prestianni was banned for six matches after he admitted to using homophobic language towards Vinicius.

Tzolis followed Piero Hincapié – who turned his temporary deal into a full-time switch – and the goalkeeper Illan Meslier, who was out of contract at Leeds, as Arsenal’s third addition.

Bruno Guimarães could also move to the Emirates with Arsenal keen on signing the Brazil international. After Newcastle’s 1-1 pre-season draw at Gateshead on Saturday, Eddie Howe said: “We don’t want to lose our best players. I’ve spoken to him [Guimarães] as I would do. Bruno is just a fantastic person. We’ve had some really good conversations, both before the World Cup, during the World Cup and after the World Cup.

Sports.title: Japan football great ‘King Kazu’ Miura, 59, scores first competitive goal in four years
Sports.content:
The Japanese football legend Kazuyoshi Miura scored his first competitive goal ⁠in nearly four years on Saturday, finding the net at the age of ⁠59 as ⁠Fukushima ​United thrashed Iwaki Furukawa 7-0 to advance in the Emperor’s Cup.

Miura, affectionately known ⁠as King Kazu, struck in the 52nd minute to put Fukushima 5-0 ahead, capping a trademark ⁠run into the box by meeting a teammate’s ​cutback with a first-time ‌finish at 59 ‌years and 149 days.

The goal sparked celebrations among teammates ‌on the pitch and the bench before the veteran forward was substituted three minutes later.

It was Miura’s first competitive goal since November 2022, when he scored for Suzuka PG, now Atletico Suzuka, in ‌a Japan Football League defeat by FC Osaka.

The former Japan international is preparing for ​a remarkable 42nd season as a professional after extending his loan spell with third-tier Fukushima United until June 2027.

Miura joined the club from Yokohama FC in ⁠December and will remain with Fukushima after making six ​appearances ​during a shortened 2026 ​campaign.

With Japan’s professional leagues set to switch ​from a ‌spring-to-autumn schedule to ​an ​autumn-to-spring calendar, Miura will enter his 60s next February still playing professionally, adding another chapter to one of football’s most enduring careers.

Sports.title: Newcastle in for new goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek after James Trafford blow, Wrexham look at Crystal Palace defender as they plot Premier League promotion push... and Leicester face race against time for new No 9: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Blackburn bag Finley after trial

Blackburn Rovers have signed former Brighton goalkeeper Finley Taylor after he impressed on trial.

The 18-year-old was a free agent having left Brighton, where he had been for five years.

Taylor said: 'At the end of last season, I came on trial, played against Manchester United and it was a good game. A tough game against obviously one of the best teams in England.

'After that, I found out I got signed. It was just a phone call, and it was a massive relief because, obviously, when you leave a club before, it's quite nerve-racking; you don't know what to expect. So, to get that call was a massive relief.'

Newcastle turn to Hornicek after he rejected Hull move

Newcastle United have switched sights to Sporting Braga goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

The 24-year-old Czech Republic international was the subject of a failed bid by Hull City earlier in the window and Benfica have been making enquiries in the past week.

Hull even matched his £25.9m release clause but Hornicek turned down the move.

'We even had one [a concrete approach]. The player himself, Hornicek, refused. There was a proposal from England, from the Premier League, but the player felt he shouldn’t go to that club and we were happy for him to stay,' the Braga president António Salvador confirmed to Portuguese media.

Lukas Hornicek went to the World Cup with Czech Republic and has a £29.5m release clause at Braga

Hornicek was back in action in midweek as he starred in Braga's 1-0 win at Serbian side Zeleznicar Pancevo in their Europa Conference League qualifier.

Newcastle had been pursuing Manchester City's James Trafford but he is set on moving to Leeds United in a deal worth around £45m as he discusses inserting a release clause into his contract.

They had also held a meeting over Brighton keeper Carl Rushworth but ultimately Newcastle had reservations about his lack of top flight experience. Rushworth remains a target for Coventry City, where he was on loan last season. They have had bids worth £25m rejected so far.

Newcastle have now asked about Hornicek and the deal could be agreed quickly if all parties wish to proceed.

Wrexham in for Palace's Imray - but face competition

Wrexham have joined the clubs showing interest in Crystal Palace full-back Danny Imray.

The 22-year-old, who had loan spells with Blackpool and West Bromwich Albion last season, is wanted back by Albion while Stoke City have also posted interest.

Wrexham, though, are continuing to push the bar on their targets as they try to take that next step up into the Premier League.

They also remain in the chase for Leicester City's Harry Souttar. The Australia international has asked to leave but the Foxes want £10million which is deterring suitors such as Sheffield United, Stoke City and more.

Danny Imray

Leicester in race against time for No 9

Leicester City are clear favourites to gain promotion from League One but are still to sign a striker - with barely three weeks to go until they kick-off the season against Notts County.

Manager Russell Martin may have overseen a 3-3 draw against La Liga side Malaga in Marbella on Saturday but that didn't mask what he thought the former Premier League champions were missing.

'The topline, both wide positions and a No 9, I think it’s really clear,' said the Foxes' boss when asked about priorities.

They have tried and failed to agree terms with former West Ham striker Danny Ings and, despite his appearance at first-team testing, Jamie Vardy is not planning a return. He still has aspirations to finish at the top.

Jamie Vardy has been training at Leicester but has his sights on a higher level than League One
