Sports.title: Jamie Gittens reveals why he is relishing a rivalry with Chelsea's £117m signing Morgan Rogers and the message Xabi Alonso has given him
Sports.content:
Jamie Gittens reveals why he is relishing a rivalry with Chelsea's £117m signing Morgan Rogers and the message Xabi Alonso has given him

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jamie Gittens is not peeved that he now has left-wing competition at Chelsea from Morgan Rogers, purchased from Aston Villa at a cost of £117million, the most money ever spent on an English signing.

Rather, he sees this record-breaking acquisition as a step towards this club taking titles again.

‘We want to win everything – that is our ambition, to win the Premier League, the FA Cup, win anything that we’re in,’ Gittens told us, standing pitch-side at the Allianz Stadium in Sydney. ‘Bringing in a player like Morgan will hopefully raise the bar to win titles.’

Gittens is relishing the friendly rivalry with his fellow Manchester City academy alumnus in Rogers, and it was during our interview that this 21-year-old Englishman earned an enormous cheer from the 4,500 Chelsea fans in attendance for their open training session.

The reason was a kid had invaded the pitch to try to get Estevao Willian’s autograph. As security led the young man back towards his guardians in the stands, Gittens paused our conversation to sign his shirt, with the supporters watching on appreciating that gesture.

Gittens has not got to hear too many cheers from Chelsea fans. His first season at the club after being signed for £52m from Borussia Dortmund was written off in January following a hamstring injury. He is itching to return, and as revealed by Daily Mail Sport, he scored in both of their behind-closed-doors friendlies versus Crawley and Bromley last week at their Cobham training base.

Jamie Gittens has welcomed Morgan Rogers arrival at Chelsea despite added competition on the left wing

Gittens views the signing of Rogers as a step towards Chelsea winning major honours again

Gittens, who scored in two behind closed doors friendlies, has his own set of objectives for next season

‘I feel at 92 per cent,’ Gittens said when asked if he is at 100 yet. ‘I’m feeling much better, more confident now my body is better, the hamstrings are good, so I’m waiting for the season to start.

‘I was training every day (over the summer), in Portugal, in Marbella, training myself to the maximum to get ready for the season. It was hard, because this was the first muscle injury I’ve had. I’ve never had hamstring injuries before. Never with the hamstring.

‘It was a challenge at the start, but I’m better now so I feel more confident. It was hard for me, but I’m here now and hopefully I can get back and tell myself that I did good in the situation.’

Gittens has his own objectives for the next season. He has written them down on a piece of paper at home. He did not want to reveal them to us when asked, but did continue: ‘This is such a big club. I want to succeed here. I need to show people what I can do. I’ll keep working hard. I’ve shown glimpses, I would say. Small bits. But this season will be a good season.’

Among the drills practised in Chelsea's training session in Sydney was crossing from the left and the right. From the left wing, we had Gittens, Cole Palmer and academy graduate Landon Emenalo whipping in the ball. From the right wing, we had Estevao, Marco Palestra and Aaron Anselmino, who was then replaced by Cobham representative Reggie Walsh.

Soon, Chelsea should have a new set-piece specialist in Austin MacPhee overseeing such routines. Like Rogers, he is in line to arrive from Aston Villa, with Bernardo Cueva revealed by Daily Mail Sport to be switching to a role behind the scenes and away from the pitch.

Chelsea have friendlies versus Western Sydney Wanderers and Tottenham in Sydney before moving on to touring Asia, and Alonso was extremely involved in training here, often demonstrating how class is permanent as he set up players in drills.

‘He wants me to keep being positive, to keep on taking on players, to keep on creating chances and to keep on pushing myself to the maximum,’ Gittens said on the message to him from Alonso.

Gittens debut season at Chelsea came to an end in January after he suffered a hamstring injury

New Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has told Gittens to keep being positive, to keep on taking on players and keep on creating chances

‘He's a very nice guy. He talks to us individually, speaks to us about what we can improve on, what we can do better. As a player, that's all you want. I think (his style can suit him as a winger). Last season was a 4-3-3 as well with two wingers which is always good, so let’s just see. Our quality is there, for sure, as a team and we have individuals on the pitch who can do amazing things.’

Alejandro Garnacho is now being moved on by Chelsea after a single season in which he failed to impress on the left wing following his £40m arrival from Manchester United. He had less leeway than Gittens, given his injury. ‘To be honest, I just look at myself,’ the man staying at Chelsea said when asked about Garnacho leaving. ‘I don't look at anyone else. I just focus on myself and try to be better.’

Gittens played against Alonso’s Bayer Leverkusen with Dortmund. He knows how good of a tactician the 44-year-old Spaniard can be. Now he hopes to excel under him at Chelsea and earn his place in their side, even with a £117m signing in Rogers as his competition.

Sports.title: Hands off Granit Xhaka! Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris sends definitive message to Chelsea and insists 'the topic is closed' after Xabi Alonso's side made shock swoop for former Bayer Leverkusen star
Sports.content:
Hands off Granit Xhaka! Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris sends definitive message to Chelsea and insists 'the topic is closed' after Xabi Alonso's side made shock swoop for former Bayer Leverkusen star

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris has issued a hands-off warning for his captain Granit Xhaka and told Chelsea to forget about signing him this summer.

The Swiss international was instrumental as the Black Cats finished in the European spots on their return to Premier League football last season – and Chelsea have tried to buy him. But boss Le Bris says there is now no chance of Xhaka leaving.

‘No, this topic is closed,’ said the Frenchman when asked about Xhaka.

‘He has been really clear about his future. He loves Sunderland, he wants to stay in Sunderland. He wants to make the future of Sunderland. He is a good captain. A great leader.’

Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this month how Chelsea had an £8m bid rejected and dismissed as insulting. Although the 33-year-old was attracted by the prospect of reuniting with Xabi Alonso - having enjoyed a successful spell under him at Bayer Leverkusen - Xhaka reaffirmed his commitment to Sunderland following discussions with the club.

Chelsea have been told 'the topic is closed' after their approach for Granit Xhaka was snubbed

New Blues boss Xabi Alonso was looking to reunite with his former Bayer Leverkusen star

Xhaka's strong rapport with Sunderland supporters and his connection with the club also played an important role in his desire to continue his journey at the Stadium of Light.

Sunderland signed 14 players this time last year as they overhauled their squad upon promotion from the Championship – but Le Bris has told fans to be patient this time around.

They have made just one signing in experienced full back Thomas Meunier, the Belgian international who joins on a free transfer from Lille.

Le Bris added: ‘It’s going to be quiet. Under the radar, right? Because I think we are working hard behind the scenes, and it's really important to be quiet because otherwise, it's a mess.

‘And we are looking at probably a different transfer window if you compare with last season. We had to sign 14 new players. That won't be the case this year. We'll see what will happen.’

Sports.title: Federico Chiesa admits Liverpool were LUCKY to reach the Champions League after dismal campaign... as he targets 'new chapter' under Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Liverpool forward Federico Chiesa admits the club are fortunate to be in the Champions League next season - and sees sees the upcoming campaign as a chance for a ‘fresh start’ after two frustrating years spent largely on the substitutes’ bench.

The Italian, who was rated as a future world-beater when he won the European Championship with his nation in 2021, signed for £10million from Juventus two years ago but has failed to make a lasting impression.

Many expected Chiesa would leave this summer – a situation that still could happen if they sign a forward, with movement expected on their pursuit of Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola this week.

But Chiesa, who scored in the Reds’ 4-2 win over Sunderland in Nashville, said: ‘Right now, I am happy here at Liverpool. I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything. I am doing the best I can to have a chance here.

‘And then we will see. At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool.

‘It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year. Maybe there have been too many fresh starts. But I don’t care, I am trying to do my best for this new manager. Last season under Arne Slot, I was trying to do my best.

Federico Chiesa scored Liverpool's third goal in their win over Sunderland in Nashville

‘Last year I felt ready for a bigger role, then it depended on the coach whether he wanted me to play or not.

‘Of course I wanted to play more but it is what it is. The gaffer decided to do so, he had his game plans, he took his decisions, I have nothing to say about that. It is football. This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that.’

Chiesa made 26 league appearances last but only one of those was a start and fitness continued to be an issue. He made the unusual step of turning down an Italy call-up from Gennaro Gattuso but insists he is keen to get back in the fold under their new boss.

Asked to reflect on last season, which saw Slot pay with his job, Chiesa said the team were lucky to even get in the top five. He added : ‘Liverpool deserves more. Two years ago, we were Premier League champions. Last year, we almost went out of the Champions League spots.

‘We were battling for fifth, which was enough at the time but as we know usually only four go in. We were lucky. It was a tough season last year and this season we need to do better, in the Champions League as well.’

Liverpool are sweating on the fitness of Joe Gomez who had to be substituted in a friendly against Sunderland here in Tennessee, with the Reds already short on defenders for the new season.

Sports.title: How Leicester City are still chasing a specialist No 9 to kickstart promotion bid... after failing to land Danny Ings and Jamie Vardy return off the cards
Sports.content:
How Leicester City are still chasing a specialist No 9 to kickstart promotion bid... after failing to land Danny Ings and Jamie Vardy return off the cards

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Leicester City are clear favourites to gain promotion from League One but are still to sign a striker with barely three weeks to go until they kick-off the season against Notts County.

Manager Russell Martin may have overseen a 3-3 draw against La Liga side Malaga in Marbella on Saturday but that didn't mask what he thought the former Premier League champions were missing.

'The topline, both wide positions and a No 9, I think it’s really clear,' said the Foxes' boss when asked about priorities.

They have tried and failed to agree terms with former West Ham striker Danny Ings and, despite his appearance at first team testing, Jamie Vardy is not planning a return. He still has aspirations to finish at the top.

The scramble is on to find a proverbial horse for the course. Yet League One had an extremely rich seam of forwards to mine from last season and competition is fierce.

Manager Russell Martin has identified the key area he needs to fill for Leicester to make good on their tag of title favourites

Leyton Orient's Dom Ballard is one forward with League One pedigree on Leicester's radar

Leicester's initial focus fell on Plymouth's Lorent Tolaj - with 17 League One goals last season - but he wanted a Championship club. Preston North End tried but big-spending Bristol City succeeded.

The Ashton Gate side have also been courting Leyton Orient finisher Dom Ballard for two months, another on Leicester's radar, but a fee has still to be agreed. Exeter's Jayden Wareham, scorer of 19 league goals last season, is viewed as an alternative.

With time of the essence Martin knows Leicester need to be decisive and soon.

Aribim Pepple, the other half of Plymouth's prolific strike partnership last season, is another who has piqued the interest of analysts, with justification.

Pepple, who just missed out on making Canada's World Cup squad, had the second highest goals per minute ratio last season. One goal every 135 minutes; 16 goals in 35 league games. Wolves are among those looking to pounce there.

As concerns rise among supporters that the club is once again leaving it too late to do the crucial part of their summer trading, Martin countered: 'I'm hopeful we can get what we want before the season begins. We have a clear idea on the list we have and it's important to find the right character.'

Being runaway favourites to win League One will mean little to many of those supporters. Last summer they were eyeing a return to the Premier League. They ended with relegation to the third tier - though a six-point deduction was crucial given they finished five points off safety.

It's been a tumultuous 10-year ride since that Premier League title. Pivotal now is finding that Fox in the box to ensure they find that path back to the top.

Sports.title: Female referee left concussed after being knocked over by brawling men's players during melee in match in France
Sports.content:
Female referee left concussed after being knocked over by brawling men's players during melee in match in France

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A female referee reportedly suffered a concussion after being knocked to the ground during a melee in a men's friendly match in France.

Referee Mathilde Demoncay had taken charge of the friendly between Ligue 2 French side Metz and their Dutch opponents Fortuna Sittard on Sunday.

Demoncay had blown for a free kick to Fortuna Sittard in the 39th minute, after a Metz player had pulled the shirt of a breaking attacker.

The fouled Fortuna Sittard player was then seen squaring up to two Metz players following the incident.

This led to Demoncay racing over in an attempt to break up the incident, while players from both teams also ran in as the melee grew.

Footage showed Demoncay, 26, being knocked over backwards as more players pushed into the melee.

Referee Mathilde Demoncay suffered a concussion after being knocked to the ground during a melee between players during a friendly in France

Demoncay had attempted to intervene in the brawl but was knocked down as more players got involved

One player was seen signalling for medical attention with Demoncay appearing to have hit her head on the ground after falling

While unclear on the footage, Demoncay appeared to hit her head on the ground after falling.

One Fortuna player was quick to notice the stricken referee, as they stood by the official and motioned for medical staff to come to her aid.

Medical staff, assistant referees and security came onto the pitch, with Demoncay receiving assistance.

The footage showed Demoncay sitting up as medical staff began to assess her, while players appeared to have become concerned by the incident.

Demoncay was ultimately unable to continue the match, with one of her assistants forced to step in.

The incident, which played out with a sign in the background reading 'respect the referee', led to two players being booked.

Fortuna Sittard had described it as a 'remarkable moment' on the club's website.

Metz, who had been leading 1-0 at the time, went on to win 3-1 in the friendly.

Sports.title: Lucky Lando Norris WINS the Hungarian Grand Prix after team-mate Oscar Piastri's spectacular capitulation - while Kimi Antonelli gains the upper hand on title rivals Lewis Hamilton and George Russell
Sports.content:
Lucky, lucky, Lando. Not that world champion Norris was other than the fastest man in the Hungarian Grand Prix and should have won it on his own.

But he was helped, first, by a bizarre incident befalling his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri handing him the victory chance his pole position deserved and his poor first lap did not.

This first of two pivotal moments in Norris’s triumph came on lap 38 when Piastri, who had pitted for a second time, was trying to make progress back to the front. In front of him, Williams’ Carlos Sainz – the villain of the piece – was fighting with Fernando Alonso for 15th.

Distracted by this, Sainz was oblivious of Piastri behind him. It was a blue-flag time. The Spaniard should have made way. He did not. Piastri fumed: ‘Get out of the f***ing way. You idiot.’ They banged tyres. ‘Oh, my God!’

All this was delaying Piastri, obviously, while Norris was making hay out on his own. After Norris was called in at the end of the following lap, he emerged in front of the other papaya car. Job done.

Piastri was furious. Obviously with Sainz. But also, it seemed, with his McLaren team for granting Norris freedom to open up an advantage for seven laps after his own stop.

Lando Norris returned to the top step of the podium with a dominant win in Hungary

The British driver was stunned by team-mate Oscar Piastri but wrestled back control

Piastri’s race engineer Tom Stallard came on the radio, to pacify him, saying: ‘Oscar, it’s Sainz that cost us. Target is to get to the end on this tyre.’

Piastri rejoined: ‘Oh, mate, just don’t talk to me now.

‘Nice of you guys to factor that one (the traffic) in by the way, thanks.’

If he believes the team pull for Norris, their hand-reared champion, this state of affairs will hardly have put his mind to rest.

The second and final piece of luck working for Norris came as Piastri, who looked set to finish second, conked out with a gearbox problem, his race over on lap 56 of 70. Thus, without any concerns at all, Norris went on to claim the first win of his title defence, indeed since the Sao Paulo Grand Prix last November.

Now more drama ensued as a virtual safety car was enlisted. Lewis Hamilton, on a unravellingly disappointing weekend for him given what riches it promised, had succeeded the stricken Piastri in second place.

Ah, but this was not to last. Norris came in for new tyres and so did Hamilton. For Norris, fine, back out at the front. But Hamilton emerged from the pits virtually level with third-placed Kimi Antonelli, and, although the seven-time world champion pushed himself ahead of the Italian into and out of the first corner, it was not legit, given the VSC limits in place.

Was he speeding in the pits in desperation? He was placed under investigation for the offence and handed a five-second penalty a few minutes later. ‘They are handing out penalties like crazy,’ said Hamilton.

He had already been told by his pit wall to hand the place back to Antonelli, but that is not quite how it stayed: yes, Norris was first, Max Verstappen second (because he did not need to stop under the VSC, being on newer tyres than Hamilton) and Antonelli third. But Hamilton’s penalty dropped him below team-mate Charles Leclerc and into fifth place.

Norris benefitted from Oscar Piastri's spectacular capitulation on Sunday afternoon

Lewis Hamilton fell further back in the championship race to Kimi Antonelli

What a headache for Hamilton. Instead of clipping Antonelli’s championship lead by two points, as he was due to do prior to Piastri’s departure, he fell five points back. He is 50 behind Antonelli heading for the summer break.

Why didn’t Ferrari slow Leclerc down? Do the fools want to win the title?

George Russell, seventh on the day, is now 59 adrift, nine points down on his starting position. Not great for the Briton, but not the worst outcome given how he watched the field fly by him at the start as anti-stall kicked in on his Mercedes. He had gone down to 19th at the end of lap one, but, helped by a new engine fitted between qualifying and the race, came through the midfield.

There was little overtaking on display, though Verstappen made a brilliant pass on Hamilton at the first corner – named after his (Verstappen’s) de facto father-in-law Nelson Piquet. He caught the Briton by surprise, a typical Max mugging. It was the move of the day.

Piastri did not need to exert such virtuosity as an old Norris habit came to haunt him, his weakness on first laps that has repeatedly cost him race wins from promising starting positions, especially in 2024 when he had an outside chance of claiming the title.

He was very smartly away from pole and took the first corner in command. But he drifted wide at the second corner, named after Hamilton, and that allowed Piastri to assume the lead.

Norris seemed to have more pace than his team-mate and harried him, but Piastri held track position until his afternoon unravelled. Norris finally streaked away, finishing 15 seconds up the road and out of sight.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's Inter Miami teammate suffers horrifying head injury before leaving the field in an ambulance and being rushed to hospital
Sports.content:
An Inter Miami forward needed to be rushed to the hospital after a disturbing aerial collision caused him to lose consciousness and begin seizing on the pitch.

German Berterame is recovering in the hospital after taking contact to his head in a Saturday night game against CF Montreal.

In the 70th minute at the Saputo Stadium in Canada, Berterame collided with Montreal defender Efrain Morales - who made the contact from behind the player as they both jumped for a header - and landed awkwardly on the pitch.

Broadcast cameras caught an open-eyed Berterame convulsing on the ground after training staff rushed over to attend to him.

The match was stopped for ten minutes as Berterame was taken off the field on a stretcher, never appearing to re-gain consciousness.

He was eventually placed into an ambulance and was rushed to a nearby hospital.

Inter Miami's German Berterame was knocked unconscious after a collision against Montreal

Berterame needed to be transported to the hospital, where he has been recovering

Miami was awarded a penalty that was scored by Luis Suarez, who held up Berterame's shirt

After the match, Inter Miami manager Guillermo Hoyos said his striker was 'recovering right now,' adding, 'He's fine, conscious.'

'His family is aware of everything,' Hoyos said. 'They're calm. The most important thing is that he's OK, and right now he is OK.'

Due to the collision with Morales, Inter Miami was awarded a penalty. Teammate Luis Suarez converted the chance, which proved to be the only goal on the night. Suarez held up Berterame's shirt in honor of the striker.

'We were alarmed at first because the blow was very strong. On the play, it’s obvious there was an elbow, which is why a penalty was awarded, he fell like dead weight,' Hoyos recalled.

'I think he might have already been unconscious given the severity of the impact. He took that elbow and hit the ground hard.

'It was a moment of great desperation and deep sadness, because it went beyond football, and all that. It’s about human life, that’s what matters most. So, we just hope everything turns out well.'

Berterame, the Mexico international, has bagged seven MLS goals for The Herons since moving from Monterrey in January.

With the victory, Miami now sit just two points behind league-leaders Nashville SC. They next face the Columbus Crew.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury's X-rated two-word response to Anthony Joshua with fight on
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury's X-rated two-word response to Anthony Joshua with fight on

After Anthony Joshua came close to losing his must win fight against Kristian Prenga, Tyson Fury only had two words for the bout

View 2 Images Tyson Fury has made his thoughts onrival Anthony Joshua's recent performance clear (Image: YouTube/Boxing King Media)

Tyson Fury only had two words after seeing Kristian Prenga deal Anthony Joshua one of the biggest scares of his career - "Wow, wtf?"

‌



Fury commented those words on social media after Ring Magazine chief and Zuffa boxing co-founder Turki Alalshikh uploaded a highlights package of Joshua's win over Prenga. The Albanian scored two huge knockdowns over AJ in the first round, the biggest of which coming in the opening exchanges.

‌



Prenga stepped inside Joshua and caught him with a perfect uppercut which sent the two-time unified heavyweight champion tumbling to the canvas, before catching him with another huge shot later in the round. However, Joshua got his bearings and knocked the 35-year-old out in round two with a vicious combination.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Oleksandr Usyk, whose team has been training Joshua since December, breathed a huge sigh of relief after Joshua's victory was confirmed. Meanwhile, Fury only let his thoughts be known on Instagram by commenting "Wow, wtf?" on the video on Alalshikh's post.

At present, that's the Gypsy King's only comment on Joshua's brush with disaster against Prenga. The Olympic gold medallist needed to be victorious to ensure the blockbuster clash with Fury would take place.

‌



The night before, Fury held up his end of the bargain by easily stopping Mariusz Wach in their non-televised clash in Pattaya, Thailand. The 46-year-old Pole gave up on his stool at the end of the seventh round after his team decided he had taken enough punishment from Fury.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The boxing world held its breath in anticipation for Fury to turn up ringside in Jeddah to confront Joshua. The latter also instantly looked for Fury in the arena straight after beating him, only for him not to be there.

‌



Channelling his inner Mike Tyson, Joshua took the microphone and said: "Wait a minute - have we got Tyson Fury in the room? Wait, wait, wait, to more important matters - is he here or not? Fair do’s.

"Im'ma rip his heart out. I'm the meanest and vicious champion's ever been. Listen, all jokes aside, you see, there’s two sides of this thing. One is fire. You have to have that vim, that grrr. But also respect.

View 2 Images Joshua was knocked down twice in the first round (Image: Matchroom Boxing/Getty Images)

‌



"I respect everything he has done. And everything that he has achieved. As someone who who has been calling for the fight for a long time, we're here now. Shout out to his Excellency. Shout to Eddie Hearn for making these opportunities possible, and I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat.”

Joshua's promoter Hearn has insisted all of the contracts have been signed, but a date or location is yet to be confirmed. UK boxing fans have been hoping for the clash to be in London, but Madison Square Garden in New York has also emerged as a potential venue.

Newsboy's horseracing tips for Monday's five meetings including Windsor NAP

There are four meetings in Britain plus the Galway Festival opens in Ireland and our tipster has selections for all the cards with his double from Windsor and Ripon

View Image Newsboy's Nap runs at Windsor (Image: Getty Images)

HARRY KNOWS's (6.20, NAP) wait for an overdue first victory can come to an end at Windsor tonight.

‌



The Richard Hughes-trained youngster has been nothing but consistent in four starts this season, finishing second three times and fourth on his other appearance.

‌



Three of his defeats came as a short priced favourite but the 6f novice race on the banks of the Thames represents his best chance yet to open his account. He has gone down by a head in two runs under Oisin Murphy and the return of the champion jockey and the fitting of first time cheekpieces can make the difference.

‌

The three-year-old recorded his only win at Listed level last season but has been well beaten in three appearances this season, but if the surgery has done its job and help settle him down, George Scott’s challenger could make his presence felt.

Sports.title: Real Madrid told to approve Arsenal's Vinicius transfer because 'they cannot rely' on him
Sports.content:
Real Madrid told to approve Arsenal's Vinicius transfer because 'they cannot rely' on him

Arsenal are keen on Vinicius Jnr and Real Madrid have been encouraged to consider a culture reset and cash in on the forward, whose contract is winding down

View 2 Images Vinicius Jnr has been linked with a Real Madrid exit

Real Madrid have been told that selling Vinicius Jr can allow them to reset the dressing room with PSG's success showcasing how a team ethic will outdo quality individuals.

‌



The Brazilian has become the subject of one of the summer's biggest transfer stories to date with Arsenal weighing up a move. No bid has yet been tabled, but internally they are keen on the forward, whose contract continues to wind down.

‌



Vinicius has been at Real since 2018 and become a leading light, helping them twice win the Champions League. He's on mammoth wages and is seeking parity with Kylian Mbappe, but negotiations are being done off the back of a second successive trophyless season at the Bernabeu.

‌



Real's fortunes have nosedived and Emmanuel Petit believes ridding of one of their biggest names could allow them to change the culture - citing the success PSG have enjoyed since losing Mbappe and adopting a more collective approach.

Real Madrid president has already made Vinicius Jr to Arsenal stance very clear READ MORE :

He told the Evening Standard: “Something has to be rebuilt in Madrid. It started with the manager in the dressing room, but also with the players on the pitch. You cannot rely all the time on the brilliance of Mbappé or Vinícius, they have to stop that.

“Spain and PSG have sent strong messages over the last two seasons that the team matters. It's not based on the individual, it's about the team's unity. You can have the best players in some positions, but it doesn't mean you're going to win the games and the competition.

‌



“Mourinho wants to get strong and reliable players, and I'm pretty sure he's putting pressure on Florentino to spend the money wisely. I know some big players are targets. If they can do that, it could be a very good season for Mourinho and for Madrid.”

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho has already landed four new faces at Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

The Special One has signed Ibrahima Konate and Bernardo Silva on free transfers whilst also bringing in Marc Cucurella and Denzel Dumfries.

Article continues below

Arsenal are looking to bolster their forward line after narrowly missing out on a Premier League and Champions League double. They were edged out in the European Cup final with their lack of firepower cited as an area where they can improve their squad. They have now discussed addinfg Vinicius, who would be among the most blockbuster signings they've ever made.

Sports.title: Wolves release statement after player involved in viral England under-16 fight video
Sports.content:
Wolves release statement after player involved in viral England under-16 fight video

Footage of two England under-16 players fighting inside a hotel room as their team-mates watched emerged on social media this week, and now Wolves have confirmed that one of their academy prospects was involved

View Image The two England players were filmed fighting

Wolves have issued a statement confirming that a member of their academy was one of the players filmed fighting a team-mate during an England under-16 camp in Turkey last year. Footage emerged on social media this week showing the pair scrapping in a hotel room, as other players watched on.

‌



Several of their team-mates were filming the incident and could be heard encouraging them. The FA issued a statement saying that the fight was caused by an 'internal matter' and was 'quickly resolved'.

‌



Championship club Wolves have now addressed the viral video in a statement published on their website, saying that the footage only captures part of a 'broader sequence of events'. It read: "Wolves are aware of footage from a previous England youth camp involving one the club's academy players which has recently resurfaced on social media.

‌



"The club is satisfied that the widely shared footage captures only part of a much broader sequence of events and does not reflect the full circumstances surrounding the incident, during which the young player had been subjected to repeated behaviour that caused him significant distress.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Trent Alexander-Arnold's pick for England manager has just taken different job READ MORE :

"Wolves staff are disappointed by those continuing to share the footage in question and condemn, in the strongest possible terms, those who have sought to identify, threaten and abuse the young person involved. Instances of extreme abuse and threats have already been shared with police."

‌



A one-minute clip of the fight showed a boy wearing official England training gear grab a phone from another boy who was lying on the bed of a hotel room. The two can be seen grappling over the phone before punches and kicks were thrown.

The boy who tried to take the phone then attempts to put the other in a headlock. He subsequently dragged him around the room before throwing him on the floor.

In the statement, Wolves academy director Jonathan Hunter-Barrett added: "Whilst the academy does not condone violence under any circumstances, it is important to recognise that this footage captures only the final moments of a much longer sequence of events. It does not reflect the repeated behaviour this young player had been subjected to, the significant distress he had experienced beforehand, or the circumstances that led to the incident.

‌



"Those of us who know this young man understand that the footage is not an accurate reflection of either his character or the circumstances he found himself in. He is respectful, humble and has consistently demonstrated the standards and values we expect from our academy players, earning the respect of both staff and teammates through the way he conducts himself every day.

Woking chief hits out as Jermain Defoe leaves first management job after just four months READ MORE :

Jude Bellingham's parting shot to Argentina referee in unseen World Cup footage READ MORE :

"Like all young people, Academy players learn and develop through both positive and difficult experiences. We are incredibly proud of the person he is today, and of the way he has responded to this distressing incident and the subsequent attention it has received, both when the footage first emerged in 2025 and again in recent days.

"This has been an extremely difficult period for him and his family. Our priority is their welfare, and we will continue to provide them with the care and support they need.

‌



"We would also encourage people to consider the impact of sharing and commenting on footage involving minors and young people. Behind every video is a person and a family, and their wellbeing should always be at the forefront of our minds.

"As a club, we do not tolerate bullying, intimidation or abuse in any form. Supporting and protecting the welfare of our young people will always be our priority, and our commitment is to continue supporting young players in their development, both as footballers and, more importantly, as people."

Sports.title: Spanish media share Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer truth and if deal will happen
Sports.content:
Spanish media share Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer truth and if deal will happen

Vinicius Jr has been linked with a sensational move to the Premier League to join Arsenal

View 2 Images (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Spanish media have given their say on the possibility of Vinicius Jr joining Arsenal. The Real Madrid winger is wanted by the Gunners but talks between the clubs have yet to begin.

‌



The 26-year-old is in the final 12 months of his contract and if Real can't secure an extension, they could be open to selling in order to avoid losing him for free next summer. A number of Spanish newspapers have weighed in on whether the transfer could actually happen.

‌



Sport claims that Real president Florentino Perez has set a non-negotiable fee of £136million (€160m). The media outlet understands that the club will not bat an eyelid at a figure below this for Vini's signature.

‌



Real are considering this fee to be an initial purchase with a number of add-ons, including performance bonuses and trophies won. Should Arsenal meet these demands, Sport sees no reason as to how the deal couldn't go through.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update READ MORE :

Arsenal have trump card to beat Man Utd in £40m Ollie Watkins transfer race READ MORE :

Marca aren't as confident that the transfer will happen though. The Spanish newspaper states that Vini is demanding at least £25m (€30m) per season to bring his salary close to Kylian Mbappe's.

They believe the contract extension negotiations are entering a "delicate phase" and if these conditions aren't met, it is unclear what the future holds for the winger. Cadena SER believes that the arrival of Yan Diomande could be the end of Vini in Spain.

View 2 Images Vini Jr wants a similar salary to Kylian Mbappe (Image: Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

The media outlet claims that Real's pursuit of the Ivory Coast international showcases the club's movement into a new era. The La Liga giants saw a £85.4m bid rejected by RB Leipzig and are now submitting an improved offer, believing that a deal can be done.

The pair would be competing for the left wing spot and Real's growing interest in Diomande is a hint to the media that Vini Jr is on his way out. They did admit that there is a world where both wingers remain in Spain but Vini's recent links to Arsenal could mean the 19-year-old is his replacement under Jose Mourinho.

Sports.title: Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update
Sports.content:
Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update

Arsenal want Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior and are exploring a move for the Brazil international, but have already agreed to sign another player this summer

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are adding another player to their academy (Image: Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Cardiff City's youngest-ever player, Axel Donczew, is set to sign for Arsenal next week.

‌



The Gunners have agreed a deal for the Wales under-19 international, who Fabrizio Romano claims has already had a medical.

‌



Donczew, 16, debuted for the Bluebirds as a second-half substitute during their EFL Trophy match against Newport County in October, aged 15 years and 234 days. He broke a record that his team-mate Rob Tankiewicz set barely an hour earlier by starting the group stage game.

‌



Aaron Ramsey had previously held the record for 18 years. He was also the last player Arsenal signed from Cardiff.

The Gunners spent £7million on a 17-year-old Ramsey in 2018. That move came after the midfielder made 22 appearances across all competitions for Cardiff, whereas Donczew has played just twice.

The Telegraph initially reported that the Gunners were keen on the teenager, who is expected to join their academy.

‌



News of the deal surfaced less than 24 hours after Arsenal's interest in Vinicius Junior emerged. Real Madrid's winger would likely cost a record-breaking fee for the Gunners to sign, but they are believed to be exploring the possibility.

Jose Mourinho is reportedly reluctant to lose the Brazilian, but his lack of a new contract at the Bernabeu means Real could cash in this summer.

In terms of Donczew, he has been missing from Cardiff City's pre-season activities this summer following interest from Premier League sides. Fulham had previously expressed interest in the right-footed left winger, who can also play centrally as an attacking midfielder.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City's former Elite Development Sqyad head coach Brian Barry-Murphy believes Axel Donczew is a brilliant player (Image: Ryan Hiscott, Getty Images)

Donczew last played for Cardiff in December, making another substitute appearance during an EFL Trophy round of 32 tie against Wimbledon. A fortnight later, Donczew was included in the matchday squad for their EFL Cup quarter-final against Chelsea, but did not feature.

Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy said late last year: "I think if they're good enough, and he clearly is, then they're old enough for us with Axel. The former Manchester City youth coach hailed Donczew as a "brilliant player".

‌



He has already earned recognition as a Wales under-19 international. Donczew has represented his national side since the under-15s.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The youngster has racking up 11 appearances across various age groups, and also holds eligibility to feature for Poland. Wales senior side head coach Craig Bellamy, however, is said to be an admirer of the youngster.

‌



Under-21s coach Darren Purse told WalesOnline: "I think Axel came into fruition because I think Craig Bellamy really liked him as an Under-16 playing for Wales. I think that came through him and the gaffer's (Barry-Murphy) conversations."

CAA (Creative Artists Agency) Stellar represents Donczew. The prominent agency's lengthy list of clients also notably includes two current Arsenal academy players: Angelinou Pedro and Theo Julienne.

Sports.title: Jeremy Jacquet's Liverpool absence explained as summer signing left OUT of pre-season squad
Sports.content:
Jeremy Jacquet's Liverpool absence explained as summer signing left OUT of pre-season squad

Liverpool saw off Sunderland in a pre-season friendly on Saturday but they did so without Jeremy Jacquet as the summer signing was left out of the squad

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet was left out of Liverpool's squad at the weekend

Andoni Iraola admits Jeremy Jacquet's long-term injury led to him being left out of Liverpool's squad on Saturday with the Reds prepared to "take it easy with him".

‌



The French defender was signed in January for £55million from Rennes, but allowed to play out the season with the Ligue 1 club. He's since made the move to Anfield but did so off the back of a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

‌



The 21-year-old was forced to miss the final few months of last season after picking up a shoulder injury. Given that he have surgery on the issue, his last game came all the way back on February 7.

‌



As a result Liverpool are taking a cautious approach to bringing him back into the fold and he was left out of the team that beat Sunderland 4-2 in Nashville. Iraola explained to LFCTV: “With Jeremy, we decided to take it easy with him."

“He has been a lot of months without playing with a shoulder injury. So, I think we are going to take it easy with him. He will play probably the last game of this US tour and he will have time to have minutes. It's true that we were kind of happy but we've lost one now.”

Iraola was referring to the injury sustained by Joe Gomez, who failed to complete ten minutes during Liverpool's clash on Saturday. There is no diagnosis on his injury but the defender has been plagued by injuries for years and could further test the team's backline depth.

‌



"Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe," said Iraola. "We were happy because we were going through training without losing any players and unluckily for us we've lost Joe straight away."

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet's move to Liverpool was confirmed this summer

Liverpool have seen Ibrahima Konate depart for Real Madrid after his contract expired whilst Giovanni Leoni is still getting back to 100 percent after rupturing his ACL last September. Virgil van Dijk has just turned 35 and will see his contract expire in the summer.

Article continues below

Jacquet is highly rated and was tipped to move to Chelsea, who had chased him throughout January, before Liverpool swooped in to complete a deal. He's relatively inexperienced but is likely to play a big role with Liverpool's resources already being tested in pre-season.

Sports.title: F1 news: Lewis Hamilton hit with new penalty as untelevised moment emerges
Sports.content:
F1 news: Lewis Hamilton hit with new penalty as untelevised moment emerges

F1 round-up ahead of the Hungarian Grand after Lewis Hamilton leaves one of his rivals furious

View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton will line up fifth for the Hungarian Grand Prix after receiving another penalty (Image: Formula 1 via Getty Images)

A thrilling Hungarian Grand Prix is on the cards after world champion Lando Norris took his first pole position of the season. With 2026 pace-setters Mercedes struggling at the tight and twisty Hungaroring track, Ferrari went into qualifying as the favourites for pole.

‌



However, Norris took advantage of an upgraded McLaren to set the fastest time. Joining him on the front row will be Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, with the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri third and Max Verstappen of Red Bull fourth despite a spin at the end of Q3.

‌



Hungaroring specialist Lewis Hamilton had to settle for fifth after being hit with a three-place grid penalty. Mercedes' George Russell, who desperately needs a good weekend after his no-score in Belgium last weekend, lines up sixth, a place ahead of team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who was also given a grid penalty.

‌



Here's a round-up of the latest F1 news ahead of the final race before the summer break…

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Fresh penalty for Hamilton

Having just missed out on pole, Hamilton suffered another blow when he was relegated three places. The seven-time world champion was deemed guilty of blocking Piastri at the first corner as the Australian started a quick lap.

‌



Ferrari failed to tell Hamilton about the oncoming McLaren and the mistake could be costly in the 41-year-old's title challenge. Hamilton has recently been no stranger to penalties. He was given a five-second penalty at the British Grand Prix for moving before the lights went out.

Lewis Hamilton one of two brutally punished as new Hungarian GP starting grid confirmed READ MORE :

In Belgium, he was controversially hit with the same sanction for his part in the first-lap clash that ended Russell's race, despite most observers viewing it as a racing incident.

Reacting to his Budapest penalty, he wrote on Instagram: "Sometimes you just can’t catch a break. Another weekend when I've been feeling great throughout all the sessions, but then it just falls apart.

‌



"To go from being so close to pole to then starting P5 is extremely frustrating. I always do my best to keep positive - sport is always about the highs and lows, but it’s also in the margins. Every point counts and you have to seize every opportunity.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"After 3 penalties in 3 weekends, it's becoming difficult to hang on to that positivity. Still, I won't let the setbacks take away from the progress we've been making as a team. With the pace we have, I'm hopeful we can get something out of the race."

‌



In a subsequent twist, Antonelli, who Hamilton trails by 45 points, was also served with a three-place grid penalty for failing to slow sufficiently under yellow flags following Verstappen's last-corner spin.

View 2 Images Oscar Piastri wasn't happy with Hamilton (Image: Getty Images)

Piastri's gesture

A previously unaired clip of Piastri's reaction to being blocked by Hamilton has emerged. The 25-year-old was impeded by the Ferrari at the start of Q3, with the Brit copping his aforementioned penalty.

Article continues below

The usually unflappable Piastri was left irate by the incident, calling it "pretty bad." In-car footage of the incident shows Piastri being clearly baulked by the Ferrari.

He then pulls up alongside Hamilton and gives him a sarcastic thumbs-up. Piastri said: "I saw him from the start line and kind of watched him, expecting him to get out of the way, and I've watched him basically all the way up until I nearly hit him."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Semi-final: Italy vs Northern Ireland

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off
