World.title: Iraq, Lebanon discuss economic partnerships
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said on Sunday that it is important to establish economic partnerships with Lebanon in different sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during discussions held in Baghdad with Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and his accompanying delegation, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The two leaders co-chaired discussions between the two countries, where ministers from both sides attended.

The discussions focused on improving bilateral ties in economic, political, and security areas. They also addressed approaches to strengthen the two countries’ partnership to promote comprehensive and long-term development and benefit both the Iraqi and Lebanese people.

Al-Zaidi also highlighted Iraq and Lebanon’s close friendship, dedication to development, and the need to form beneficial economic collaborations across all development areas.

The prime minister also emphasized the importance of joint coordination between the two nations in addressing regional challenges and supporting efforts to boost stability, reduce tensions, and resolve disputes.

World.title: Washington rejects Iraq’s deal with Turkmenistan to import gas
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s plan to purchase Turkmen gas has encountered another obstacle, as the US has raised objections to Baghdad’s proposal to transport the supplies through Iranian territory.

A source told Attaqa News that the United States has connected the agreement’s execution to negotiating a comprehensive political solution with Tehran, complicating the issue of obtaining the fuel required to run Iraq’s power plants.

The US position emerged during talks held in Washington by a government delegation accompanying Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, which included Electricity Minister Ali Wahib and Oil Minister Basim Khudair.

The two sides discussed energy and economic cooperation, but the Turkmen gas sale to Iraq via Iran drew strong American opposition, despite Baghdad’s urgent need for new fuel sources amid a worsening electricity crisis.

The rejection comes amid escalating military operations in the Middle East, with the United States and Iran exchanging attacks, as well as rising tensions in the Arabian Gulf, which have affected maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq signed a memorandum of understanding in 2023 with Turkmenistan to import the necessary gas for its power plants, as stated by the Ministry of Electricity. The ministry indicated that the initiative will necessitate additional negotiations regarding the transportation of gas through Iran.

Power plants in Iraq depend on gas imports from Iran, which cover one-third of the country’s energy needs.

This agreement permits Iran to receive a quarter of the gas supplied across its borders.

The gas supply agreement with Turkmenistan aims to provide Iraq with an average of 20 million cubic meters per day.

World.title: Iraqi court seizes IQD 27 billion in Jumaili’s case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s anti-corruption judiciary has seized IQD 27 billion in cash as part of an ongoing investigation involving Adnan Al-Jumaili, the detained former Deputy Oil Minister for Refining Affairs, in one of the country’s latest high-profile corruption cases.

Judicial authorities said the money was recovered during investigations into alleged financial losses linked to projects overseen by the former official and other individuals connected to the case.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the media office of Iraq’s judiciary said Judge Diaa Jaafar, the investigating judge at the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court, confirmed the seizure of IQD 27 billion.

According to the court, the funds were discovered after investigators traced financial proceeds allegedly generated through waste and irregularities in projects associated with Al-Jumaili and other suspects.

Officials said the cash had been hidden by several individuals believed to be involved in the case. The court said investigators are continuing to pursue additional suspects and trace other assets that may be linked to the alleged offenses.

Judicial authorities indicated that the investigation remains active as efforts continue to identify everyone involved and recover additional public funds, if any are found.

The judiciary also released photographs showing stacks of newly recovered banknotes arranged in large piles following the seizure. According to the statement, the images document the IQD 27 billion recovered during Sunday’s operation, which authorities said had been concealed by individuals connected to the former deputy minister.

Officials did not disclose how many people are under investigation or provide further details about the locations where the money was found.

The case is among several recent corruption investigations pursued by Iraq’s anti-corruption courts as authorities seek to recover public funds and hold officials accountable for alleged financial crimes.

The judiciary reiterated that investigations remain ongoing and that further legal action could follow as additional evidence emerges.

World.title: Iraq completes initial designs for Development Road Project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has completed the preliminary designs for its flagship Development Road Project and railway corridor, marking a major milestone as the government prepares to advance one of its largest infrastructure initiatives into the implementation phase.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Sunday that the initial designs are now 100% complete, with work shifting to detailed engineering plans covering infrastructure, bridges, railway stations, and technical facilities along the project’s route.

According to a source at the ministry’s media office, engineers have begun preparing the project’s detailed designs to ensure the corridor meets international engineering and construction standards. The next phase includes finalizing plans for the railway network, highways, bridges, stations, and supporting infrastructure before construction begins.

Officials described the transition as a key step toward launching the long-awaited project after completing the necessary preparatory stages.

The announcement follows a recent visit by Turkish Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu to Baghdad on July 21, where he held talks with Iraqi officials on strengthening cooperation in transport and communications.

During the meetings, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahb Al-Hassani and his Turkish counterpart agreed to accelerate technical planning and implementation procedures for the Development Road Project.

The ministry said both sides consider the corridor a transformative initiative that could reshape regional trade and economic cooperation. The ministry also revealed that Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has instructed officials to prepare a comprehensive financing mechanism for the project.

Securing funding will be a priority ahead of the project’s implementation and is expected to feature prominently during Al-Zaidi’s upcoming visit to Ankara, where discussions with Turkish officials will focus on advancing strategic cooperation and moving the project toward construction.

The Development Road Project is designed to create a major transport corridor linking Iraq’s ports with regional and international markets. The combined railway and highway network aims to connect the Grand Faw Port in southern Iraq with Turkey and Europe, positioning Iraq as a key logistics hub between Asia and Europe.

Officials say the corridor will significantly improve trade flows while strengthening Iraq’s role in global supply chains. Alongside the engineering work, the Ministry of Transport is preparing the project’s economic model to maximize investment returns and attract local and international partners.

The ministry said the framework will also align with the government’s broader reform agenda, including digital transformation and modern project management systems.

The government views the Development Road Project as one of Iraq’s most important strategic investments. Officials expect it to diversify the economy beyond oil, generate new non-oil revenues, attract foreign investment, and create thousands of jobs across multiple sectors.

By leveraging Iraq’s geographic position between East and West, the project is also expected to strengthen the country’s role as a regional center for transportation, logistics, and international trade.

World.title: Iraq’s non-oil revenues jump to 16%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Eco Iraq Observatory, which studies economic performance indicators, disclosed on Saturday that non-oil income now accounts for 16 percent of Iraq’s overall financial revenues, the highest percentage recorded so far.

According to a statement released by the observatory, this is the first time that the percentage of non-oil earnings has climbed to 16 percent during the months of May and June, having not exceeded five percent in years.

Eco Iraq noted that the proportion originally grew to roughly 10 percent between May 2020 and October 2022, then remained stable at that level during Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani’s leadership before recently hitting its peak.

The statement highlighted that non-oil revenues are divided into commodity taxes, production fees, general fees, income and wealth taxes, transfer revenues, and other sources.

Iraqi Kurdistan’s income, which it distributes to the federal government in Baghdad, accounts for around 5.5 percent of overall non-oil revenues.

As part of the government’s efforts to diversify the economy and achieve Iraq’s long-term development goals, Mazhar Saleh, the Prime Minister’s Advisor for Financial Affairs, stated in early June that an initiative would be launched. This initiative aims to create an integrated link between enhancing the structure of non-oil revenues within the framework of state finances and diversifying the non-oil GDP.

The Iraqi government established the ambitious goal, referred to as ‘Iraq 2035,’ in May. It includes both public finance reforms and social market economy policies, which aim to facilitate a gradual structural transformation of the national economy, as stated by Saleh.

The vision transforms fiscal policy to ensure that non-oil income accounts for at least 46 percent of total governmental revenues. This will improve budgetary sustainability and reduce the volatility caused by overreliance on oil earnings.

World.title: Iraq to launch ferry routes to Iran, Kuwait, UAE, and Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is preparing to launch a network of regular maritime passenger routes connecting the country with Iran, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, and Saudi Arabia, as part of a broader effort to revive the country’s maritime transport sector and strengthen regional tourism.

According to Iraq’s Ministry of Transport, the initiative will begin after technical and administrative requirements are completed in coordination with relevant authorities inside Iraq and neighboring countries.

A source at the ministry’s media office told Iraq’s official newspaper that the government has developed a comprehensive plan to operate regional maritime transport services using an expanded fleet of boats and ferries.

The ministry currently operates 40 boats and ferries under its river transport program and has recently added 15 new boats and three ferries to the fleet. The upgraded vessels are expected to provide modern, safe transportation for passengers while supporting Iraq’s growing tourism sector.

According to the ministry, most of the new vessels will be deployed on passenger and tourism routes linking Iraq with Kuwait, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Iran. Officials said services will begin once all operational approvals, safety procedures, and cross-border coordination have been finalized to ensure the routes meet international maritime safety standards.

The planned connections are expected to facilitate both tourism and commercial travel between Iraq and neighboring countries. The Ministry of Transport believes the new maritime routes will provide an affordable and practical alternative for regional travel, particularly for leisure tourism.

The project is also expected to improve mobility for official delegations and religious visitors while strengthening economic ties with Gulf states and Iran through enhanced passenger connectivity.

Officials described the initiative as a significant step toward revitalizing Iraq’s maritime transport sector after years of limited regional ferry services. The ferry project forms part of a wider government strategy to modernize Iraq’s river and maritime transport infrastructure.

Alongside expanding its fleet, the ministry is investing in the development of ports, docks, and river terminals to improve passenger services and operational efficiency.

The broader vision aims to restore river and maritime transport as an important component of Iraq’s transportation network while supporting economic development, tourism, and greater regional integration.

World.title: Kirkuk Engineers Syndicate accuses BP of sidelining local talent and demands an 85% local hiring quota
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Kirkuk Engineers Syndicate has voiced strong concerns over hiring practices and subcontract awards linked to BP’s operations in the province’s oil fields, alleging that local engineers and businesses are being overlooked in favor of workers and companies from outside Kirkuk.

While welcoming international investment in Iraq’s energy sector, the syndicate warned it would pursue legal action and peaceful protests if local employment requirements are not enforced.

In a statement, the syndicate said it is closely monitoring recruitment procedures and the awarding of secondary contracts related to BP’s projects in Kirkuk.

It argued that the current approach has resulted in several violations, including the exclusion of qualified local engineers despite the availability of experienced graduates and professionals from the province.

The syndicate also claimed that engineering and technical staff are being recruited from outside Kirkuk, while numerous subcontracting and logistics contracts have been awarded to companies based elsewhere.

According to the statement, these practices undermine the local economy and deprive Kirkuk residents of employment opportunities linked to projects operating within their province.

The syndicate stressed that Kirkuk residents bear the environmental and health impacts associated with oil production and should therefore receive priority in employment opportunities.

It called on the Ministry of Oil and the Kirkuk provincial administration to require that at least 85% of jobs across all project stages be reserved exclusively for residents of Kirkuk.

In addition, the syndicate demanded formal representation on the joint recruitment committee to ensure transparency and fairness in hiring decisions. It also urged authorities to use the syndicate’s database of registered engineering graduates when filling vacancies.

Among its proposals, the syndicate called for all job applications to be processed exclusively through the employment office of the Kirkuk Governorate, arguing that a centralized system would improve transparency and ensure equal access to opportunities.

The organization also backed government efforts to distribute employment opportunities fairly among all communities in Kirkuk without discrimination.

The statement concluded with a warning that the syndicate would not remain silent if local engineers continue to be excluded from employment opportunities.

It said it is prepared to coordinate with legislative and executive authorities and pursue all available legal avenues, alongside peaceful protests, to protect the rights of Kirkuk’s engineering community. The statement did not include a response from BP regarding the allegations.

World.title: Iraq’s central bank improves non-bank financial oversight
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – As part of a major institutional reform, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) upgraded its Directorate of Non-Bank Financial Institutions Supervision to a complete General Directorate.

This change intends to increase regulatory control, develop digital solutions, and improve institutional performance in Iraq’s expanding financial industry.

The reform entails significant changes to departments, name practices, and reporting structures.

The newly established general directorate will include all important departments in charge of policy, regulatory structures, digital technologies, and financial service operations.

The Information Technology and Payments Directorate is now known simply as the Information Technology Directorate. Its old financial inclusion and information security sections have been removed and merged with risk management and other operational directorates.

The CBI closed its office for coordinating branch activities. The major branches in Basra, Mosul, and Erbil will report directly to the bank’s deputy governor.

The Human Resources Directorate has directed that all personnel transfers and systemic transitions will be effective by July 30, 2026.

This change corresponds with CBI Governor Nizar Hussein’s increasing regulatory push on financial technology businesses to decrease cash dependency and adhere to international compliance requirements.

World.title: 'Attempt to repair PM's tarnished image': Congress on high-powered exam reforms task force
World.content:
PM Narendra Modi; Jairam Ramesh

NEW DELHI: Reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's announcement of a high-powered task force on examination reforms, the Congress on Sunday termed it a "high-powered attempt" by the prime minister to "repair" his "irreparably tarnished image. ""Friends, in June 2024, after irregularities in several exams, including NEET-UG, the Modi government formed a high-level expert committee chaired by former ISRO chairman Dr K. Radhakrishnan to 'ensure the transparent, smooth, and fair conduct of examinations.' In July 2026, after irregularities once again in NEET-UG and other exams, the Modi government has formed a 'high-level task force' to focus on exam reforms," Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X shortly after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's announcement.He added that the government was yet to fully implement the 101 recommendations made by the Radhakrishnan committee."Instead, for nearly two years between 2024 and 2026, it did not even appoint a full-time director general for the National Testing Agency (NTA). Ultimately, all of this is nothing but a high-powered attempt to repair the Prime Minister's irreparably tarnished image," Ramesh said.PM Modi's announcement came amid demands for examination reforms following the NEET (UG) question paper leak controversy, which affected over 22 lakh aspirants.On Saturday, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online satirical platform, ended its indefinite sit-in at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and broader education reforms.CJP ended its agitation hours after Pradhan resigned, as student protests intensified in Delhi and other parts of the country. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi has been given additional charge of the Ministry of Education.Meanwhile, besides Nilekani, who co-founded IT giant Infosys, other members of the high-powered task force include former Isro chairman S Somanath, ex-Intelligence Bureau director Tapan Deka, IIT Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary Anita Karwal, and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.According to the prime minister, the government will implement the task force's recommendations to establish a "foolproof examination system."The panel will help revamp NTA examinations, with a focus on technology-driven improvements and structural reforms in the system, PM Modi added.

World.title: CDSCO cancels 7 clinical trial ethics panels over serious violations
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has cancelled the registration of seven Ethics Committees across India overseeing clinical trials after inspections found serious violations of regulatory norms.

The regulator said the committees failed to comply with the New Drugs and Clinical Trials (NDCT) Rules, 2019, Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines and other requirements, compromising their ability to carry out their responsibilities.

The action covers Ethics Committees in Delhi, Pune, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata, which review and monitor clinical trials to protect the rights, safety and well-being of participants.

The CDSCO said the committees were inspected as part of a risk-based compliance exercise to assess adherence to the NDCT Rules, 2019, Good Clinical Practice guidelines and quality management systems. The inspections identified significant deficiencies and major regulatory non-compliances in the functioning of the committees.

According to the regulator, the registrations were cancelled only after completion of the regulatory process, including evaluation of inspection reports, review of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) responses, issuance of show-cause notices and personal hearings, wherever applicable.





The seven committees whose registrations have been cancelled are Rational Independent Ethics Committee, New Delhi; Hurip Independent Bioethics Committee and Dr T K Pal Memorial Bio Ethics Committee, Kolkata; Ethiwell Ethics Committee and Ethos Ethics Committee, Navi Mumbai; Institutional Ethics Committee, Aatman Hospital, Ahmedabad; and Royal Pune Independent Ethics Committee, Pune.

World.title: PM taps UIDAI architect Nilekani for exam overhaul
World.content:
NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi announced Sunday a high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder and founding UIDAI chairman

to recommend measures for making Indiaâs public examination system leak-proof, transparent and technology-driven.

Modi said the panel would examine how technology could be used to clean up the examination process and make it more reliable. âThe Nilekani committee will give suggestions on maximum use of technology for making exams clean and transparent,â he said, adding that the government would work on its recommendations to build a âfool-proofâ system.

The task force has been asked to suggest next-generation examination reforms, with a particular focus on technology as well as structural changes in the

and the wider testing framework.

Besides Nilekani, who led the creation of Aadhaar as the first chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India, the multidisciplinary panel includes former ISRO chairman S Somanath, former Intelligence Bureau director Tapan Deka, IIT Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary and ex-CBSE chairperson Anita Karwal, and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.

The choice of Nilekani signals an attempt to draw on his experience in building technology platforms at scale.





The committee is expected to study the entire examination cycle â from question-paper preparation and transmission to centre management, candidate authentication and post-exam processing â and identify points where technology can reduce human intervention and plug security gaps.

The announcement comes amid a wider government push to restore confidence in high-stakes entrance examinations after the NEET-UG paper leak.

The Centre is also moving to strengthen penalties under the law against unfair means in public examinations.

The latest task force follows the K Radhakrishnan committeeâs recommendations on restructuring the NTA, improving governance and strengthening exam security. Several changes in staffing, operations and examination conduct have since been initiated, but the Nilekani panel will focus more sharply on a technology-led roadmap for future examinations.

The political significance of the announcement is heightened by its timing. It came a day after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned, taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG crisis following weeks of student protests.

Modi said those who had played with studentsâ futures were facing action, but stressed that the government also had to look ahead and create an examination system that was dependable, transparent and made maximum use of technology. The task forceâs recommendations are expected to guide the next phase of the NTA overhaul.

World.title: ‘Responsible for brutal assault on innocent students’: After Dharmendra Pradhan, opposition turns heat on Amit Shah, seeks resignation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The opposition is set to intensify its attack on the government in Parliament on Monday by demanding the resignation of Union home minister Amit Shah over the police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak, CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas said.

Speaking to reporters in New Delhi on Sunday, Brittas said opposition parties would also raise the appointment of Naresh Pal Gangwar as secretary, department of higher education, when Parliament resumes.

The remarks come a day after education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following a 36-day agitation led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), with the government also accepting the protesters' other key demands.

"Last day, Shah said the government respected the youth who led the protest. Where was that respect for the last 36 days? When students were being beaten on the streets of the national capital, and their skulls were being cracked open, where was that respect?" Brittas said.

"If there is even a grain of sincerity in those words, Amit Shah too should resign. Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. The home minister, who is responsible for this brutal assault on innocent students, must resign," he added.





Opposition prepares to corner government in Parliament

Brittas said the opposition would support any move to strengthen laws against examination-related fraud but questioned the government's decision to amend the existing legislation instead of ensuring its implementation.

He noted that Parliament had enacted the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act in 2024 after the government claimed it would curb paper leaks.

"Now the government is only proposing amendments to that law.

The problem is not the absence of legislation but the lack of political will to enforce it and the authorities' alleged compromise with vested interests," he claimed.

INDIA bloc parties are planning to seek an urgent discussion in Parliament on the alleged use of excessive force against students protesting the NEET paper leak.

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has written to home minister Amit Shah seeking accountability, while Trinamool Congress MP Sagarika Ghose has submitted a notice in the Rajya Sabha seeking suspension of business to discuss the issue.

The opposition is expected to raise allegations regarding the use of pellet guns, the deployment of men in plain clothes during the July 20 protest, and injuries suffered by students. The government, meanwhile, is scheduled to introduce amendments to the anti-paper leak law in the Lok Sabha on Monday.

The proposed Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, seeks stricter penalties for paper leaks, including imprisonment of up to 10 years and fines of up to Rs 50 lakh for individuals involved, while organised crimes related to examination fraud could attract fines of up to Rs 10 crore.

Questions over higher education secretary appointment

Brittas also questioned the appointment of Naresh Pal Gangwar as secretary, department of higher education, alleging that the officer had previously faced accusations of irregularities in the disbursal of central government subsidies.

"Such an officer has now been appointed to head the department responsible for public examinations, where transparency and integrity are of utmost importance. All these issues will be raised during the discussion in Parliament," he said.

He further alleged that while authorities had released details of police personnel injured during the protests, no information had been made public about injured students.

"The home ministry has released details of police personnel who were allegedly injured. But not a single detail has been made public about the protesters who were brutally assaulted. There is a complete veil of secrecy over their condition," Brittas claimed.

He said the identities and medical condition of injured students should be disclosed so that their families and organisations willing to assist them could provide support.

Separately, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut also blamed Amit Shah for the police action during the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march organised by the CJP at Jantar Mantar.

Raut alleged that students were attacked and women protesters were harassed, holding the home minister responsible for the incident.

He also claimed Shah was responsible for "whatever bad and undemocratic is happening in the country."

The BJP rejected Raut's remarks, with Maharashtra BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban asking the Shiv Sena (UBT) leader to focus on his "already depleted party".

The protests, which began on June 20 over the NEET paper leak, were called off on Saturday after the government accepted key demands of the protesters and Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down as education minister.

The July 20 police action against protesters marching towards Parliament has since become a major flashpoint, with opposition parties alleging excessive use of force, including pellet guns.

Delhi Police has denied using pellet guns during the protest, while the CRPF has not publicly responded to allegations involving its Rapid Action Force.

World.title: Infosys co-founder, Aadhaar architect: Who is Nandan Nilekani, set to lead high-powered exam reforms task force
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Continuing his announcements on examination reforms, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said the government has constituted a high-powered task force to be led by Infosys co-founder

.

Also Read:

"HIGH-POWERED TASK FORCE on examination reforms under the leadership of Shri Nandan Nilekani constituted," PM Modi said in a video message on X, a day after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical platform, called off its 37-day-long agitation following the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET (UG) question paper leak.

Led by CJP, thousands of students had been on an indefinite sit-in in Delhi since June 21, demanding the resignation or removal of Pradhan and broader reforms in the education sector.

Meanwhile, joining Nilekani on the task force are former Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) chairman S Somanath, former Intelligence Bureau (IB) director Tapan Deka, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary Anita Karwal, and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.

Also Read:

Who is Nandan Nilekani

Nilekani is the co-founder and chairman of Bengaluru-headquartered IT giant Infosys. He also served as the founding chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), the body that issues Aadhaar cards, with the rank of a Cabinet minister in the Congress-led central government from 2009 to 2014.





In January 2023, he was appointed as the co-chair of the âG20 Task Force on Digital Public Infrastructure for Economic Transformation, Financial Inclusion, and Development.â

Born in Bengaluru, Nilekani, 71, graduated from IIT Bombay in 1978. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian honour, in 2006. Time magazine named him among the world's 100 most influential people in 2006 and 2009, and included him in its 2024 list of the 100 Most Influential People in AI.

Nilekani has also authored or co-authored three books.

World.title: Sonam Wangchuk to be discharged from hospital on Monday after CJP ends 36-day protest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk will be discharged from Medanta Hospital in Gurugram on Monday after recovering from a 26-day indefinite fast in support of students protesting alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, his team said.

Wangchuk is expected to be discharged at around 11.30 am. Before returning to his home in Ladakh, he will visit Rajghat to pay homage to Mahatma Gandhi. He had also paid tribute at Rajghat on June 28 before joining the agitation at Jantar Mantar.

The activist joined the protest on June 28 and remained on an indefinite fast for 26 days. On July 18, he was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital, where he alleged that he was being kept in detention.

Following an order of the Delhi high court, he was later transferred to Medanta Hospital for treatment.

Protest ends after Pradhan's resignation

The 36-day agitation, led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), concluded on Saturday after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister from the Union council of ministers. The protest, which began on June 20, demanded accountability over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations and reforms to the examination system.





The CJP announced the withdrawal of its agitation in "good faith" after Pradhan stepped down and the organisation received assurances from the Centre on its other demands.

Pradhan had said he submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the interest of students and to ensure that the ongoing protests were not exploited by "anti-national forces." Following his resignation, President Droupadi Murmu assigned the additional charge of the Ministry of Education to Union minister Pralhad Joshi, who has since assumed office.

World.title: 'Govt-ordered probe an eyewash': Tripura Congress MLA demands judicial inquiry into DGP Anurag Dhankar's death
World.content:
Tripura DGP Anurag Dhankar was found dead in state police headquarters on July 20

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Tripura Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman on Sunday reiterated the party's demand for a judicial probe into the death of state DGP Anurag Dhankar, who was found dead at the police headquarters in Agartala on July 20."From day one, we have been demanding a judicial probe by a sitting high court judge into the unnatural death of the DGP, keeping in mind the circumstances leading to the recovery of his body," he told a press conference at the Congress Bhavan in Agartala."The condition in which we saw his body at the morgue was as if he was in deep sleep, with no visible wounds that are generally found in such cases. We strongly believe that a team led by an SP-rank officer cannot clear the many doubts surrounding the incident.That is why we want a judicial inquiry into the unnatural death," Roy Barman added.A three-member team headed by West Tripura SP Namit Pathak has been constituted to investigate the matter.Roy Barman termed the Tripura government's decision to investigate the case through a three-member team as an "eyewash." He alleged that the "honest DGP was heckled over some issues days before his death."The Congress MLA also expressed disappointment over the Tripura high court not taking suo motu cognisance of Dhankar's death."The people of the state are also upset over the role of our high court. When the legislature, bureaucracy and media succumb, it is the judiciary that comes out and stands for the cause of people's rights. Unfortunately, we have not seen the high court take any suo motu cognisance in many incidents in the state since former Chief Justice Deepak Kumar Gupta's tenure ended," he said.Dhankar, a native of Uttar Pradesh's Baghpat, was a 1994-batch IPS officer of the Tripura cadre. He took over as the state's DGP in May 2025.The officer had led the CBI probe into the alleged Rs 13,000-crore Punjab National Bank fraud involving diamantaire Nirav Modi and the reinvestigation into the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

World.title: From Chita Andolan to Jal Satyagrahas: Why the Ken-Betwa project has upset MP tribals
World.content: The surplus water of Ken River will be transferred to Betwa River through the 221 km long link canal from Daudhan Dam, providing irrigation and drinking water facilities in both MP and UP.

World.title: Tension in village in Pudukottai district over temple ritual issue
World.content:
Tension prevailed at Valavampatti village in Gandharvakottai taluk in Pudukottai district on Saturday following a problem that arose between SC Adi Dravidar and caste Hindu communities over performing ‘mandagapadi’ ritual in a Ayyanar temple that comes under the control of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department.

The problem between the two communities eventually led to the suspension of the temple festival. Police personnel have been deployed in the village. The 10-day festival at the temple began a few days ago and was to conclude on July 26. The problem arose on the ninth day on Saturday over performing ‘mandagapadi’ by the SC Adi Dravidar community.

The police said the caste Hindus had opposed the performing of the mandagapadi ritual by the SC Adi Dravidar community triggering tension. A section of Adi Dravidar community people staged a road roko on the Pudukottai-Thanjavur national highway warranting police intervention. The festival was suspended as the opposition continued.

An official of the HR & CE department reportedly took away the metal idol from the temple as there was no solution. This apparently provoked the caste Hindus to stage a road roko on the highway later. They gave up their stir after the idol was brought back to the temple, the sources said.

World.title: Neighbours’ dispute turns fatal, youth hacked to death in Thiruvananthapuram
World.content:
A long-standing neighbourhood rivalry over a boundary dispute allegedly culminated in the brutal daylight murder of a 42-year-old man at Chambakada in Kaithamukku on Sunday. Within hours of the crime, the City police arrested the prime accused, Pradeep, 38, along with three other accomplices. The victim, Vishakh, 42, a resident of Chambakada, was attacked around 1.30 p.m. outside his house.

According to the police, the group of four men purportedly arrived in a rented car and attacked Vishakh with deadly weapons, inflicting severe injuries to his hands, legs and abdomen, before fleeing the scene in the vehicle. Preliminary investigations indicate that the murder is linked to a long-standing boundary dispute between the neighbours, who are also believed to be distant relatives. The duo had also been involved in several confrontations over the years, many of which resulted in criminal cases.

A similar clash had occurred around six months ago, during which Vishakh allegedly attacked Pradeep. Vishakh had been named the accused in the particular case, Local residents informed the police that the previous disputes between the two families had prompted interventions by other neighbours and the local residents’ association. However, no one anticipated that the conflict would escalate into a fatal attack, they said.

The vehicle was later found abandoned at Pulayanarkotta, after which the suspects attempted to evade arrest. The gang was apprehended from the locality following a search operation. The four suspects were later taken to the Armed Reserve Camp at Nandavanam for interrogation. The police also recovered three knives suspected to have been used in the murder, along with liquor bottles from inside the abandoned car.

The police have also confirmed that the vehicle used in the crime had been rented allegedly for the attack. Senior police officers, including District Police Chief (Thiruvananthapuram City) Arul R.B. Krishna, visited the crime scene and supervised the investigation. The accused will remain in police custody for interrogation and are expected to be produced before the court on Monday, following which investigators are likely to seek further custody to continue questioning.

World.title: Mayiladuthurai police launch probe into death of man
World.content:
The Anaikaran Chathiram police in Mayiladuthurai district have launched an investigation into the death of a 55-year-old man Subhash at Thirumayiladi village on Sunday.

According to police, a quarrel broke out between Subhash and his neighbour in the morning following problems over land issue. Subhash died later and his family alleged that his death was due to assault.

Police personnel conducted inquiries and the body was shifted to the Government Hospital, Sirkazhi, where autopsy was conducted. The Anaikaran Chathiram police have registered a case under Section 194 (iii) of the BNSS and are conducting an investigation, police sources said.

World.title: RBI sees rupee as undervalued; FCNR(B) inflows cross $32 billion
World.content:
The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) recent measures to attract foreign capital have garnered strong investor response, with banks mobilising nearly $32 billion, largely through Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) or FCNR(B) deposits, while government securities have attracted more than $7 billion in foreign inflows since the June policy measures, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has said.

Also read | Examining the RBI’s remittances survey

In an interview with The Hindu BusinessLine, Mr. Malhotra dismissed concerns that the inflows merely represent a recycling of existing deposits. He added that the RBI has adequate tools to manage any resulting liquidity. The inflows have strengthened India’s external position amid heightened geopolitical uncertainty and volatile global capital flows, he said.

Responding to concerns over the RBI bearing the hedging cost of fresh FCNR(B) deposits and offering concessional forex swaps for external commercial borrowings (ECBs) by public sector entities, Mr. Malhotra said: “It is not something which should be a matter of concern because we have a foolproof system of insuring ourselves. So, whatever dollars we get, the excess foreign currency is invested in foreign assets. The risk, therefore, is not there.”

The Governor said the measures should be viewed in the context of challenging global conditions facing emerging markets and are expected to further strengthen India’s balance of payments and currency stability.

Mr. Malhotra also sought to reassure markets on the rupee, arguing that recent depreciation does not reflect any weakness in the country’s economic fundamentals. According to him, pressure on the currency has largely stemmed from geopolitical tensions, dollar strength and broader volatility across emerging markets.

“We do not target any specific exchange rate or band for the rupee. Our intervention, whenever necessary, is targeted to curb excessive volatility,” he said, adding that the currency is “not overvalued” and could even be considered undervalued in both nominal and real effective exchange rate terms.

He cited the current account surplus during April-May, robust services exports, resilient remittance inflows, rising merchandise exports and improving foreign direct investment flows as indicators of the strength of the external sector.

Forex management

On forex reserve management, Mr. Malhotra said the RBI continues to be guided by the principles of safety, liquidity and returns, while reviewing reserve deployment periodically.

Turning to monetary policy, the Governor reiterated that inflation control remains the RBI’s foremost priority even as it remains mindful of growth risks. He said the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) will continue to adopt a data-dependent approach while navigating the evolving growth-inflation trade-off.

“Our primary mandate is inflation and price stability. Therefore, we will do whatever is required first, to keep price stability and then, to see to what extent we can support growth,” he said.

While inflation has moved above the 4% midpoint of the MPC’s target band, Mr. Malhotra indicated that policymakers do not yet see signs of broad-based price pressures becoming entrenched.

On policy rate

Mr. Malhotra defended the current policy rate, saying it reflects prevailing growth-inflation dynamics and elevated global uncertainties. The MPC’s neutral stance, he noted, provides flexibility to maintain the status quo or move rates in either direction depending on incoming data, with decisions guided by domestic conditions rather than policy actions of global central banks.

The Governor downplayed concerns that strong credit growth could lead to overheating, arguing that credit creation generates deposits while capital adequacy, liquidity coverage and stable funding ratios remain the key constraints on lending. He added that Indian banks remain well positioned on these parameters.

Addressing governance issues, Mr. Malhotra said the RBI’s regulatory and supervisory framework remains robust, while growing foreign interest in Indian banks and NBFCs reflects confidence in the country’s financial system and long-term growth prospects. Ownership norms, he added, will continue to emphasise fit-and-proper criteria and diversified shareholding structures.

(The writers are from the Hindu BusinessLine)

World.title: Former DRDO chairman Satheesh Reddy honoured with ‘Changemaker-2026’ award
World.content:
Former DRDO chairman and National Security Advisory Board member G. Satheesh Reddy on Sunday said India was no longer dependent on developed countries for critical military technologies.

Speaking after receiving the EMESCO-Dr B.V. Pattabhiram’s ‘Changemaker-2026’ award from actor-politician Chiranjeevi at a function held here, Mr.Reddy dedicated the honour to the contributions of thousands of scientists, from Suri Bhagavantam to A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, who had worked towards strengthening India’s scientific capabilities.

D. Vijayakumar, CEO of EMESCO Books, said Pattabhiram had worked extensively for the welfare of students and youth through counselling and guidance. He said Mr. Reddy was also inspiring youth across the country through lectures, interviews and symposiums organised under the banner of Kalam’s Institute of Youth Excellence.

Mr. Chiranjeevi recalled the contributions of Pattabhiram as a magician, student adviser and family counsellor. A Telugu booklet titled ‘Okadu Satheesh Reddy’, profiling Mr. Reddy, was also released on the occasion.

Andhra Pradesh Minister for Medical and Health Services Mr. Satya Rao, former MP K.V.P. Ramachandra Rao, senior editor K. Ramachandra Murthy, Jaya Pattabhiram and Prashant Pattabhiram participated in the programme.

World.title: Madhya Pradesh content creator booked over ‘highly abusive’ reel against Pradhan
World.content:
A social media content creator has been booked in Madhya Pradesh’s Niwari district for allegedly using “highly abusive” language against former Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Delhi Police in a video clip amid the student agitation.

According to the police, the accused, Yashpal Soni, a local social media influencer, was booked on July 23 over an Instagram reel he had posted and has been questioned in the matter.

Mr. Soni was booked under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Sections 296(a) (obscene act in any public place to the annoyance of others) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of the peace) following a complaint from local BJP leaders led by its block president Kamlesh Chourasiya.

Speaking to The Hindu, Niwari Superintendent of Police Ray Singh Narwaria said that the video was “way out of the purview of freedom of expression”.

“He has used such objectionable curse words in the video. This is in no way freedom of speech and should not be promoted,” he said.

Mr. Narwaria said that the action was taken as per legal provisions and Mr. Soni was questioned in the matter.

“He himself realised his mistake and apologised for it,” he said.

In the video titled ‘Desh dobara gulam ho gaya hai (the nation has been enslaved again)’, Mr. Soni could be heard cursing Mr. Pradhan and BJP leaders over the former’s resignation, and the police authorities over their crackdown on student protestors.

He has now removed the video from his Instagram account.

In the complaint, the BJP leaders also demanded that his social media account be restricted.

Mr. Pradhan, who has been facing heat over the NEET question paper leak and irregularities in various other exams, stepped down from his post on Saturday (July 25, 2026) following weeks of student agitation in New Delhi and several other parts of the nation. His removal was a key demand of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which was leading the movement. Mr. Pradhan has been replaced by his colleague in the Union Cabinet, Pralhad Joshi.

World.title: FIR against actor Sreelekha Mitra for allegedly carrying objectionable poster of PM in CJP rally
World.content:
She was allegedly carrying a poster with an objectionable cartoon of PM Narendra Modi at the massive students’ rally in Kolkata on Friday

Multiple first information reports (FIRs) have been lodged against Bengali actor Sreelekha Mitra across West Bengal on Sunday (July 26, 2026) for allegedly carrying a poster with an objectionable cartoon of Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the massive students’ rally in Kolkata on Friday (July 24, 2026) demanding Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.

The protest march, led by Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and several Left-affiliated students’ wings, started from the Sealdah station in which thousands of young students and also people from various section of the society showed up on Friday in solidarity with the protesters at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. Ms. Mitra also walked with the students in the rally with the poster in hand that later surfaced controversy on the social media.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Keya Ghosh on Sunday (July 26) lodged the first FIR against her at Kolkata’s Anandapur police station that was followed by more such complaints at various police stations in different districts of West Bengal, said police officials.

“We witnessed hooliganism during the protest, including attacks on journalists. Even women journalists were not spared and were allegedly molested. Such actions by the Left are completely unacceptable. Meanwhile, displaying a poster depicting the Prime Minister in such a derogatory manner cannot be tolerated under any circumstances. That is why this FIR has been filed,” Ms. Ghosh told the presspersons.

Ms. Mitra is known for her often outspoken views on politics and also against the nepotism and syndicate rule by political leaders in the Tollygunge film industry. In 2024, she also lodged an FIR against the Malayalam film director Ranjith soon after the Hema Committee report was published. She accused the director of sexual misconduct during the pre-production/audition phase of his 2009 film Paleri Manikyam: Oru Pathirakolapathakathinte Katha.

Meanwhile, the BJP state president Shamik Bhattacharya on Sunday also took a dig at the protesters in Friday’s rally by calling them anti-nationals. He said that the ones who have been arrested for the violence in Friday’s rally are directly involved with Trinamool Congress while the Left are appeasing them.

“They also raised ‘Azadi’ slogan in the protest. Our country is already free. Such slogans of the anti-national forces patronised by the Left will not be apred. BJP government will take necessary action in it,” he added.

World.title: 400 kg of gutkha products seized, one held
World.content:
The Cuddalore police seized 400 kg of gutkha and other banned tobacco products, being smuggled in an SUV and arrested one person in Vriddhachalam on Saturday.

Following a tip-off on the movement of the contraband, a police team intercepted the SUV at Periyar Nagar in Vriddhachalam. On searching the vehicle, the police found 400 kg of gutkha and other banned tobacco products.

The car driver, identified as Virender Singh of Jalore district in Rajasthan, was arrested and remanded in custody.

World.title: Inside Amaal Mallik’s 800-sq-ft home: Fan art, piano corner and a balcony retreat
World.content:
Singer-composer Amaal Mallik recently offered a glimpse into a home that reflects both his creative personality and his preference for understated design, as she invited Mashable India.

Spread across 800 square feet, the two-bedroom apartment has been designed around a simple, modern and highly functional concept, with every corner balancing allure and practicality. The house opens to a cosy living room with plush seating and a classic piano sitting in the corner.

Living space featuring curated fan artworks

The living room sets the tone for the home with a lively mix of grey, yellow, and red. An L-shaped sofa anchors the space and also features carefully curated artworks that add character to the walls. A piano occupies a prominent spot in the room, serving as one of the places where the composer often creates music. The space is decorated with myriad art pieces gifted to Amaal by his fans.

World.title: ‘Reproductive patterns’: Shashi Tharoor’s cheeky response to son’s ‘ban boomers from WhatsApp’ post
World.content:
After the Cockroach Janta Party’s 36-day long protest over NEET paper leak turned successful following the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor had a banter with his son Ishan Tharoor online as the latter remarked that Boomers should be banned on WhatsApp in India. The Parliamentarian said, “Given our reproductive patterns, my son, unlike in the West, every generation of Indians, including yours, qualifies as [baby]Boomers!”

Given our reproductive patterns, my son, unlike in the West, every generation of Indians, including yours, qualifies as [baby]Boomers! https://t.co/wpCgTXHsMb — Shashi Tharoor (@ShashiTharoor) July 26, 2026

Ishan, who is an American journalist, was responding to a post by Zoho’s co-founder Sridar Vembu on France passing laws banning social media for those under the age of 15. The 42-year-old wrote on X, “I agree young kids should not be on social media at all. But India needs to ban Boomers on WhatsApp first before it does anything else.”

I agree young kids should not be on social media at all. But India needs to ban Boomers on WhatsApp first before it does anything else https://t.co/Vh24ZdIQKT — Ishaan Tharoor (@ishaantharoor) July 24, 2026

Vembu had posted, “India should ban social media for young children too. I believe young children should read physical books, play in the dirt under the sun and stay away from social media!”



India’s online revolution wins on the ground

Abhijit Dipke had founded the CJP by setting up an Instagram account asking social media users to join the party on May 16. Soon, Gen Z mobilised and agitation began over NEET paper leak followed by activist Sonam Wangchuk’s hunger strike. Eventually, Pradhan tendered his resignation as the Centre paid heed to the relentless Gen Z.

‘You don’t need to be treated like cockroaches’

In an opinion column published in The Indian Express, addressing Gen-Z, Tharoor said, “The emergence of movements like the CJP offers a powerful, albeit heartbreaking, piece of political theatre. It captures the visceral feeling of being treated as disposable by a system that seems unresponsive to the struggles of ordinary citizens. It seems a safe space for those of you dealing with the crushing weight of unemployment, the rising cost of living, and the narrowing of the pathways to quality education….Frustration is not an end in itself. You don’t need to be treated like cockroaches, and you don’t need to adopt the label as your permanent identity.”

World.title: Israeli settlers’ violence: How two West Bank mosques ended up in flames
World.content:
Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Sunday and set fire to two mosques, officials said amid a rise in deadly violence in the region that killed four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers.

The violence comes as Israeli opposition and Palestinians accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of ignoring the reported attacks by settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. The attacks threaten to trigger broader violence across the territory.



Israeli soldiers operate in the West Bank Palestinians city of Nablus. (AP Photo) Israeli soldiers operate in the West Bank Palestinians city of Nablus. (AP Photo)

Security crackdown after mosque arson

After the two mosques were burned down, Israeli soldiers and police spread across the West Bank and shut major roads that blocked access to the hospital, where it was reported that two militants were hiding, AP reported. Israeli authorities have arrested about 70 Palestinians in an attempt to contain the violence in the area.

World.title: Punjab Police busts Pakistan-linked BKI terror module, arrests key operative
World.content:
Yadav said Punjab Police remains committed to dismantling terror networks, curbing organised crime and maintaining peace and security in the state.

The Punjab Police Sunday claimed to have have busted an ISI-sponsored Babbar Khalsa International (BKI) module, operated by foreign based handlers, and arrested its key operative from Jalandhar.

The operation also led to the recovery of an Improvised Explosive Device (IED) packed with 1.3 kg of explosive, along with shrapnel and ball bearings, indicating preparations for a high-impact attack aimed at disturbing public peace, Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav said.

The accused has been identified as Satbir Singh, a resident of village Padiana in Adampur, Jalandhar. Apart from recovering explosives, police teams have also recovered his motorcycle, which he was riding, the police said in a statement.

World.title: p-tau217: What the new Alzheimer’s blood test can — and can’t — do
World.content:
Diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease has traditionally involved a combination of cognitive assessments, brain scans, and, in some cases, invasive spinal fluid tests—an often lengthy process that can delay clarity for people experiencing memory loss and cognitive decline. Now, a simple blood test measuring a protein called p-tau217 is offering fresh hope.

Backed by a recent JAMA study and additional findings presented at the Alzheimer’s Association International Conference (AAIC), researchers say the test could help doctors identify Alzheimer’s disease earlier and distinguish it from other causes of dementia. While doctors caution that it is not a replacement for conventional diagnostic methods, they believe it could become a valuable addition to the diagnostic toolkit, making Alzheimer’s detection faster, less invasive, and more accessible.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

What is the p-tau217 blood test?

According to Dr Sheetal Goyal, Consultant, Neurologist, Wockhardt Hospitals, Mumbai Central, the p-tau217 blood test detects a protein that rises when the abnormal tau changes associated with Alzheimer’s disease begin in the brain.

“The p-tau217 blood test measures a protein that increases when the abnormal tau changes linked to Alzheimer’s disease start in the brain. It provides a simple and minimally invasive way to detect the biological changes related to the disease,” says Dr Goyal.

Unlike cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis, which requires a lumbar puncture, the blood test involves a routine blood sample, making it significantly less invasive and potentially easier to access, she adds.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by People Magazine (@people)

How accurate is it?

“Research has shown that the p-tau217 test is highly accurate and closely aligns with findings from amyloid PET scans and CSF analysis,” explains Dr Goyal.

However, she emphasises that it should not be viewed as a standalone diagnostic test.



“MRI scans remain essential for ruling out conditions such as stroke, brain tumours, or other neurological disorders, while cognitive assessments continue to play a critical role in evaluating memory, thinking, and overall brain function. At present, the blood test is best used to support these existing assessments rather than replace them,” she says.

Who should consider this test?

“The test is mainly intended for people with persistent memory problems or other cognitive symptoms where Alzheimer’s disease is suspected,” she says.

People who occasionally forget names or misplace their keys because of stress, inadequate sleep, or normal ageing generally do not require the test. “It is not recommended for healthy individuals simply because they have a family history of Alzheimer’s. A thorough neurological evaluation should always come first to determine whether the blood test is appropriate,” Dr Goyal adds.

Can earlier diagnosis improve outcomes?

One of the biggest advantages of the p-tau217 test is its potential to identify Alzheimer’s disease earlier, when interventions may be more effective.



“Earlier detection allows patients to begin treatment sooner, better manage modifiable risk factors, plan for future care, and, where appropriate, access disease-modifying therapies,” says Dr Goyal.

She notes that while the test is not a cure, earlier diagnosis can improve treatment planning and may help slow disease progression in eligible patients.

What are the current limitations?

“The major challenges include standardising the test across laboratories, validating its performance in diverse populations, ensuring affordability, and improving access,” Dr Goyal explains.

She is optimistic, however, about its future in India.

“As research continues to expand, these tests are likely to become more widely available over the next few years, particularly at tertiary care centres,” she says.
